You are designing a streaming analytics structure for ride events with fields (driver_id, trip_id, distance, ts, city). Implement a data structure that: (1) deduplicates events with identical (driver_id, trip_id) within a sliding window W = 30 seconds, (2) maintains per-city total distance for events in the last T = 300 seconds, (3) supports retrieving the top-K cities by current total distance in O(log K) per update, with efficient expirations. Describe your data structures and algorithms and analyze time/memory?

Design a data structure MultiTagRollingTopK that processes a stream of events with fields (user_id, tag, value, ts) and supports: (1) for each (user_id, tag) maintain the sum of values in the last W seconds; (2) return the top-K users by the sum across all tags for the last W seconds in O(log K) per update, with efficient expirations. Propose data structures, algorithms, and complexity analyses, and show how you handle expirations as time advances?

Design a mutable sequence analytics structure SequenceAnalytics with operations:
- append(v)
- insertAt(i, v)
- removeAt(i)
- topKByFrequency(k)
- topKInLastWindow(k, w)
Your design should use an array for the sequence, a doubly linked list to support efficient insertions/removals, a hashtable mapping value->frequency, and a max-heap to extract top-K values. Ensure updates keep O(log n) and handle expirations for the last-window queries as new elements arrive?

Design a per-sensor moving-window data structure: each sensor keeps a circular buffer of its recent events (ts, metric, value) and a hashtable for (sensor_id, metric) -> latest to deduplicate within W. Maintain sensor_totals[sensor] as sum of non-expired values. Use a min-heap of size K to store current top-K (total, sensor) with lazy validation. On insert/expire, update totals and push to heap; pop stale entries. Expire via global clock advancing; remove old events from buffers. How would you implement and analyze?

Design a streaming page-leaderboard data structure to process events (user_id, page_id, ts). Requirements: (1) deduplicate updates for the same (user_id, page_id) within a 60-second sliding window; (2) maintain per-page total clicks in the last 60 seconds; (3) support retrieving top-K pages by current total in O(log K) per update; (4) handle expirations efficiently as time advances. Outline the data structures and algorithms, and analyze time and memory?

Design a streaming data structure for events (user_id, item_id, value, ts). For each user, keep only the most recent item_id within a sliding window W seconds, and accumulate the value of non-expired events per user. Support retrieving top-K users by total value in O(log K) per update, with efficient expirations as time advances. Describe the data structures and algorithms?

Design a live leaderboard data structure for streaming tasks: each event is (task_id, delta, ts). Requirements: (1) adjust a task's score on new events; (2) return top-K tasks by current score in O(log K); (3) expire tasks older than W seconds; (4) implement with a hashmap and a max-heap. Explain data layout, updates, and complexity?

Design a streaming per-player score engine for a mobile game. Each event is (player_id, event_type, delta, ts). Requirements: (1) for each player, keep only the latest event_type within the last 60s and accumulate its delta; (2) maintain global top-K players by total delta in the last 60s, updating on arrivals and expirations; (3) implement with arrays, linked lists, a hashtable, and a min-heap for expirations. Explain data structures and update logic?

Design a real-time streaming processor for market data: events are (symbol, price, volume, ts). For a sliding window W seconds, maintain per-symbol VWAP and a global top-K symbols by VWAP. Requirements: (1) addEvent(symbol, price, volume, ts) supports out-of-order arrival within the window, (2) getTopK(K) returns the current top-K symbols by VWAP, (3) expirations are handled as time advances with O(1) amortized updates, (4) space O(S+W). Explain data structures and give complexity/edge-case handling?

Design a data structure to process events (user_id, game_id, score, ts). For each (user_id, game_id), keep only the most recent score within a sliding window W seconds; compute total_score per user as the sum of latest scores across all games; support retrieving top-K users by total_score in O(log K) per update; handle expirations as time advances?

Design a streaming data structure for events (user_id, category, ts). Requirements: (1) deduplicate identical (user_id, category) within a sliding window of 30 seconds; (2) maintain per-user count of distinct categories seen in the last 30 seconds; (3) support retrieving top-K users by this per-user count in O(log K) per update, with expirations as time advances. Provide concrete structures and complexity?

Design a data structure HybridTopK that processes a stream of events with fields (id, category, score, ts). Requirements: (1) For each (id, category), keep only the latest event within the sliding window W seconds; (2) maintain per-category total as the sum of the latest non-expired scores across all ids; (3) support retrieving the top-K categories by current total in O(log K) per update; (4) handle expirations as time advances using a lazy expirer. Explain data structures and algorithms, and analyze time/memory?

Design a RealTimeTopKWindow to process streaming events of the form (array_id, value, ts). Maintain, for each array_id, the sum of values within the last W seconds. Provide getTopK(K) to return the top-K ids by current sums. Support out-of-order arrivals within the window and handle expirations as time advances. Use a hashtable for id->window, a per-id linked list (deque) for the window, and a heap for top-K; describe API, data structures, and complexity; ensure lazy expiration to keep updates fast?

Design a CityLeaderboard data structure for streaming ride events: each event is (city, driver_id, earnings, ts). Requirements: (1) For each city, deduplicate events so that within a moving window W seconds only the latest per (city, driver_id) contributes to the per-city sum; (2) maintain per-city total earnings from non-duplicate events in the last W seconds; (3) support retrieving top-K cities by current sum in O(log K) per update; (4) handle expirations efficiently as time advances. Explain data structures and algorithms, and provide complexity analysis?

In an online ad platform, events arrive as (ad_id, region, bid, ts). For a sliding window W seconds, maintain per-ad totalBid = sum of bid across all regions within the window, and a global top-K of ads by totalBid. Provide APIs: addEvent(ad_id, region, bid, ts), getTopKAds(K) in O(log K) amortized, and getTopKRegionsForAd(ad_id, K) by region totals within the window. Expire old bids as ts advances. Describe data structures: hashtable mapping ad_id -> per-region sums (arrays/linked lists), per-ad event queues (linked list), and a max-heap of (totalBid, ad_id) with lazy deletions. Analyze time and memory?

Design a data structure LatencyTopK to process events (service_id, endpoint_id, latency_ms, ts). For each service_id maintain, for every endpoint_id, a sliding window of the last W seconds of latency values using a linked list per endpoint. Compute per-service average latency across all endpoints in their windows. Implement:
- addEvent(service_id, endpoint_id, latency_ms, ts)
- getTopK(K) returning the top-K services by their current average latency
Expirations must happen as time advances (remove old samples). Use arrays, linked lists, a hashtable, and a heap. Explain update/expiration semantics and analyze time/memory?

Design a data structure BurstyRoomWindow that processes streaming events (room_id, sender_id, len, ts) with a sliding window W seconds. For each room, deduplicate multiple events from the same sender within the window, keeping only the latest len, and maintain per-room total length. Support getTopKRooms(K) by total length in O(log K) per update, and expire old events as time advances in O(1) amortized per expiration. Explain data structures and complexity?
How would you implement a thread-safe LRU cache using a HashMap and DoublyLinkedList, considering eviction policy and O(1) operations?

In a social app, process a stream of like events (user_id, post_id, ts). For a sliding window W seconds, design a data structure LivePostLikes that (1) counts distinct users who liked each post within the window, and (2) maintains a top-K leaderboard of posts by those counts with efficient expirations as time advances. Explain data structures, update ops, and time/memory complexity?

Design a data structure CityWindowLeaderboard that processes streaming events (city_id: int, temp: float, ts: int). For the last W seconds, maintain per-city average temperature and support: 1) addEvent(city_id, temp, ts); 2) getTopKCities(K) returning the K city_ids with highest averages; 3) expire(now) advancing time and pruning old events. Use a hashtable for city buckets, a per-city deque for (ts, temp), and a min-heap for top-K with lazy updates. Explain time/memory?

Design a SlidingTagTopK data structure to process streaming events with fields (tag, user_id, value, ts). For a sliding window W seconds, maintain per-tag sums of values with ts in [currentTime-W, currentTime]. Provide operations: 1) addEvent(event) in O(1) amortized, 2) topKTags(K, currentTime) in O(log K) with a heap and lazy expirations. Outline data structures, update logic, and overall time/memory complexity?

Design a data structure ScoreWindow that processes a stream of events (user_id, delta, ts). For a sliding window of W seconds, implement: 1) addEvent(ts, user_id, delta) in O(log N), 2) topKUsers(K, currentTime) returning the top-K user_ids by total delta within the window in O(K log N). Explain the data structures and trade-offs, including expiration handling, tie-breaking, and memory usage?

Design a data structure WindowedTopKAdapter to process a stream of events with fields (arrayId: int, value: int, ts: int). For a sliding window of W seconds, implement: 1) addEvent(arrayId, value, ts) in amortized O(1) with occasional O(log A) heap work; 2) topK(currentTime, K) returns the K arrayIds whose latest value within [currentTime-W, currentTime] is largest; 3) use lazy expirations so arrays with latest timestamp outside the window are ignored; 4) support ties by latest timestamp and arrayId. Explain structures and complexity?

Given a stream of events (user_id, score, ts) and a sliding window W seconds, design a data structure that maintains per-user sums within the window and supports: 1) addEvent(user_id, score, ts) in O(1) amortized, 2) topK(currentTime, K) returning the top-K users by their sums in the window in O(K log K). Use a hash map for totals, an array-based queue for expirations, and a heap for top-K with lazy updates. Explain expirations as time advances?

Design a real-time item leaderboard system: events (user_id, item_id, score, ts). For a sliding window W seconds, maintain per-item the number of distinct users who scored that item and a top-K leaderboard by these counts. Implement addEvent(event) in O(1) amortized and topKItems(K, currentTime) in O(K log N) with a max-heap and lazy expirations. Use an array-based queue, a linked list for timestamps, a hashtable for pair counts, and a heap for top-K. Describe data structures and update logic; provide complexity and potential bottlenecks?

Design a streaming data structure that ingests two streams: an array-quality stream of sensor readings (ts, sensor_id, value) and a linked-list of corrections (sensor_id, delta, ts). For the last W seconds, compute per-sensor current value = sum(readings in window for that sensor) + sum(corrections up to current time). Support: 1) pushReading(ts, sensor_id, value) in O(log M) amortized, 2) addCorrection(ts, sensor_id, delta) in O(1) (append to linked list), 3) topK(currentTime, K) in O(log K) returning top K sensors by current value with only readings in window, using a hashtable for state and a max-heap with lazy removals. Explain data structures and update rules?

Use a linked list for order, a hashtable for counts, and a max-heap for top-k with lazy deletions. Expire events as time advances; discuss complexities?

Design a SlidingTopK structure for a stream of integers with a fixed window W. Design a data structure WindowedKeyTopK to process a stream of events (key, value, ts). For a sliding window of width W seconds, maintain for every key the sum of values with ts in [currentTime-W, currentTime]. Support:
- addEvent(key, value, ts) in O(log N)

Design a streaming data structure TagAwareTopK that processes events with fields (id, tag, value, ts). Design a data structure MultiMetricTopK for a real-time stream: each event is (user_id, action, value, ts) with action in {click, like, share}. With a sliding window W and weights w_action, S(u) = sum value*w_action over events in (now-W, now]. Implement addEvent(ts, user_id, action, value) and queryTopK(now, K) returning the top-K users by S(u); include advanceTime(now) to purge expired events. Design a data structure CategoryWindowTopK for a streaming events system with fields (id, category, value, ts) and a fixed window W. Implement: 1) addEvent(id, category, value, ts) to insert or update an event and maintain per-category sums for [ts-W, ts], 2) topK(now, K) to return the K categories with largest sums in the current window in O(K log C). Use arrays, a hashmap, per-category queues, and a max-heap with lazy expirations. Explain data structures and complexity?

Design a SlidingUserAvg data structure to process a stream of events (user_id, value, ts). It must maintain for each user the average of values within the last W seconds. Given a stream of user actions with timestamps, design a system to find the top K most frequent actions in the last N minutes using O(1) time per query?

Design a data structure called LiveTopK to process a continuous word stream with timestamps. It must support:
- add(word, ts): register an occurrence
- expire(ts): remove all occurrences with timestamp <= ts - W (sliding window)
- topK(k): return the k words with highest frequency in the current window, breaking ties lexicographically

Constraints: window size W seconds; memory O(D) where D is distinct words in window. Use a hashmap for counts, a heap for top-k with lazy updates, and a queue to expire old occurrences. Provide function signatures and a brief implementation sketch. Analyze time and memory trade-offs?

Design a streaming analytics structure that processes events with fields (service, id, value, ts). Requirements: (1) deduplicate events with identical (service,id) within a moving window of W seconds, (2) maintain per-service sum of values for events within the last W seconds, (3) support retrieving top-K services by current sum in O(log K) time and updating as new events arrive or old ones expire. Design a streaming scoreboard for a game. Each event is (playerId, delta, ts). Implement a structure that (1) deduplicates events with the same (playerId, ts) within 1 second, (2) updates per-player total scores, and (3) returns the top-K players by score after each event in O(log K). Use a hashtable for scores, a per-player linked list to track recent events, and a min-heap of size K for top players. Provide approach and time bounds?

Design a data structure TopKFrequent that processes a stream of integers and supports: add(x) increments x's frequency, and getTopK() returns up to K values with the highest frequencies, breaking ties by smaller value. Use a hashtable for counts and a min-heap of size K to maintain the current top-K; should updates be O(log K) per add?

Design a rolling-window per-video leaderboard for a video streaming service. Each event is (userId, videoId, duration, ts). With a window W seconds, implement a data structure that: 1) deduplicates repeated (userId, videoId) within W seconds by keeping the latest duration; 2) maintains per-video total duration within the window; 3) supports retrieving top-K videos by total duration in O(log K) time as events arrive or expire. Provide addEvent, expire, getTopK interfaces and discuss memory usage?

Design a data structure to process a stream of events with fields (user_id, action, score, ts). Requirements: (1) deduplicate the latest (user_id, action) within a sliding window W seconds, (2) maintain each user's total score from non-expired events, (3) support retrieving the top-K users by current total score in O(log K) time per update, with efficient expirations. Specify data structures (arrays, linked lists, hashtables, heap) and analyze time/memory?

Design a data structure FreqMax that processes a stream of integers. It must support two operations: add(x) and getMaxFreq(). add(x) increments x's frequency; getMaxFreq() returns the value with the highest frequency; in a tie, return the smallest value. Use a hashmap for counts and a max-heap for (count, -value) with lazy deletions. Describe and sketch the implementation; what are the time/space complexities?

Design a data structure ExpiringLeaderboard with operations: add(key, score, ts, ttl), getCurrentScore(key, ts), getTopK(ts, K). The entry for a key expires ttl seconds after ts. Use arrays, a hashtable, a doubly linked list for LRU-like recency, and a max-heap to support getTopK efficiently. Explain how you'd handle expirations and stale heap entries, and analyze time/space?
You have a staircase with n steps. You can climb 1, 2, or 3 steps at a time. How many distinct ways can you reach the top? Implement a solution with O(n) time and O(1) space?
Given a string, find the minimum cost to transform it into a palindrome where insertions cost 2 and deletions cost 1. What is the optimal dynamic programming approach?
Given a target sum n, count the number of ways to reach it using dice rolls where each roll can be 1-6. Return the result modulo 10^9+7. Optimize for O(n) time and O(1) space?

Given an array of integers where each element represents the maximum number of steps you can jump forward from that position, find the minimum number of jumps required to reach the last index. If it's not possible to reach the end, return -1. How would you implement this efficiently?
What is Dynamic Programming and how does it differ from plain recursion? When would you choose one over the other?

For a staircase of N steps, some steps are blocked. You can move 1 or 2 steps at a time, and you may not land on a blocked step. How many distinct ways are there to reach exactly step N from step 0, modulo 1e9+7? Provide both a bottom-up DP solution with O(N) time and O(N) space and a memoized top-down variant, and explain edge cases (start blocked, end blocked, consecutive blocked steps)?

Given an array A of length N and a target sum K, count the number of ways to partition A into contiguous blocks such that each block sums to exactly K. Return the count modulo 1e9+7. Provide a bottom-up DP using a hashmap to accumulate counts in O(N) average time and a top-down memoized variant; discuss edge cases and complexity?

Scenario: DNA sequence S and motif T. How many distinct ways can T occur as a subsequence of S, modulo 1e9+7? Provide a bottom-up DP using O(|S|·|T|) time and O(|T|) space plus a memoized top-down variant. Consider empty T, empty S, and repeated nucleotides in T?

Given N features, each with duration t[i], deadline d[i], and value v[i], schedule on a single machine starting at time 0. You may pick any subset and order arbitrarily; each feature once and must finish by its deadline. Return the maximum total value and a feasible sequence of feature indices. Provide memoized top-down DP with time as capacity and a bottom-up tabulation solution; include reconstruction and edge cases (no feasible set, tight deadlines, ties)?

You are given a string s of length N and a dictionary D mapping substrings to integer scores. A valid decomposition partitions s into consecutive pieces where each piece is a key in D. Compute the maximum total score achievable for s, or -1 if no decomposition exists. Implement both a bottom-up DP (O(N * maxLen) time, O(N) space) and a memoized top-down solution, with maxLen = max key length in D. How would you handle edge cases like no valid decomposition and overlapping options?

Given a grid of non-negative costs with dimensions m x n, you start at (0,0) and move only right or down to (m-1,n-1). You may zero out the cost of at most one cell along the path. Return the minimum achievable path sum. Provide a DP solution (memoized or tabulated) and discuss time/space?

Count the number of ways to partition a positive-integer array nums into contiguous blocks such that each block sums to target. Return the count modulo 1e9+7. Provide a top-down memoized solution and a bottom-up tabulation sketch in JavaScript/TypeScript, including edge cases (empty input, large target) and a short correctness justification?

Given an array a1..an (n up to 2e5) and an integer k, partition into exactly k non-empty contiguous segments. The cost of a segment [l..r] is (sum(l..r))^2. Design an O(k n log C) DP using a Li Chao segment tree to minimize total cost. Explain the initialization, recurrence dp[k][j] = min_i dp[k-1][i] + (S[j]-S[i])^2, how lines L_i(x) = (dp[k-1][i]+S[i]^2) + (-2 S[i]) x are managed, and discuss potential pitfalls in practice?

You are given a string s of length n and an integer k. You may delete up to k non-overlapping palindromic substrings. Each deletion yields a reward equal to the substring's length. Return the maximum total reward you can obtain. Provide a memoized top-down solution and an iterative tabulation version, including palindrome preprocessing in O(n^2). Explain state definitions, transitions, and how you would reconstruct the deletions. Example: s ababa, k 2?

You have N jobs with nonnegative durations a[1..N]. Partition the sequence into at most K contiguous batches. The cost of a batch is the maximum duration among its jobs. Minimize the total cost across batches. Provide a bottom-up DP (O(N^2 K)) and a memoized top-down version, and discuss edge cases (K>=N, zero durations, empty input)?

On an n×m grid with 0 (free) and 1 (blocked) cells, count the number of monotone paths from (0,0) to (n-1,m-1) moving only right or down. How would you implement both a memoized top-down DP and a bottom-up tabulation, handle edge cases (start/end blocked), and analyze time/space?

Partition an array of N daily workloads into exactly K contiguous blocks. Each block cost is (sum of workloads in the block)^2. Return the minimum total cost to cover all days with exactly K blocks. Provide a bottom-up DP (O(N^2K) time, O(NK) space) and a memoized top-down variant; discuss edge cases (N < K, negative workloads)?

You are given an array nums of length n (n <= 1000). Count the number of ways to partition nums into contiguous blocks so that the sum of each block is a power of two (1, 2, 4, 8, ...). Implement both a memoized top-down solution and a bottom-up tabulation solution. Return the total count. Example: nums = [1,1,1] yields 3 ways: [1|1|1], [1|1,1], [1,1|1]?

You’re given a string s and a dictionary dict of lowercase words. Implement a function minWordSegments(s, dict) that returns the minimum number of dictionary words needed to concatenate to form s exactly, or -1 if impossible. Provide both a top-down memoized (with memoization on index) and a bottom-up tabulated DP solution. Assume |s| <= 500 and dict size up to 10k?

Given an array blocked of length n where blocked[i] is 0 (free) or 1 (blocked). Start at index 0 (assume it's free) and reach index n-1. You may move 1 or 2 indices at a time. Return the number of distinct paths modulo 1e9+7. Implement using a memoized DFS and a bottom-up DP; discuss time/space and edge cases?

You have a staircase of n steps, with certain steps blocked. You can jump any number of steps from 1 up to maxJump at a time, but you may not land on a blocked step. Starting at step 0, write a dynamic programming solution to count the number of distinct ways to reach step n. Provide both a memoized recursive version and a bottom-up tabulation version, and discuss time/space complexity and edge cases?

Given an array arr of length n and an integer k, partition the array into contiguous subarrays of length at most k; the value of each subarray is the maximum element in that subarray; what is the maximum total value achievable?

Context: In a data pipeline, a string s of digits (length n) is produced without separators. Count the number of ways to partition s into non-empty substrings with no leading zeros and values strictly increasing. Return modulo 1e9+7. Propose a memoized DFS dfs(pos, prevLen) and a bottom-up DP; discuss time/space trade-offs and edge cases (leading zeros, equal-length compare)?

Given a string s of length n (n up to 2000) and an array delCost where delCost[i] is the cost to delete s[i], determine (1) the minimum total deletion cost to obtain a palindrome by deleting characters, and (2) the number of distinct deletion sets achieving this minimum (mod 1e9+7). Implement both: a memoized DFS over (l,r) and a bottom-up DP; discuss time/space and edge cases?

Given an array a[1..n] of integers and an integer m, select exactly m elements such that no two chosen indices are adjacent (i_{t+1} - i_t >= 2) to maximize the sum. What is the maximum sum, or is it impossible to meet the constraints?

Given a string s and a dictionary of words dict, count how many different ways to segment s into a sequence of dictionary words. Return the count modulo 1e9+7. Provide a top-down memoized solution and a bottom-up tabulation sketch. Assume dict lookup is O(1) via a hash set and that n = len(s) up to 500?

In an n x m grid with non-negative costs and obstacles, starting at (0,0) you may move only right or down and must make exactly K turns; design a DP (memoized or tabulated) to compute the maximum path sum achieving exactly K turns from start to bottom-right, or report impossibility. Provide recurrence and complexity?

You are given an integer n (0 <= n <= 100000) and a set of allowed steps S (e.g., {1,3,5}). A move adds s to your current position and costs s. Return the minimum total cost to reach exactly position n from 0, or -1 if impossible. Show both: (a) a top-down memoized solution minCost(n) using a memo map, (b) a bottom-up tabulation solution using an array of size n+1. Provide complexity and edge-case notes?

You are given a string s of length n. In one operation you may delete any contiguous palindromic substring. What is the minimum number of operations needed to delete the entire string? Provide a memoized top-down DP and a bottom-up tabulation approach, with explicit state definitions, transitions, base cases, and discuss time/space complexity and edge-case handling?

Given an integer array A of length N, count the ways to split it into contiguous segments from left to right such that each segment’s sum is non-decreasing relative to the previous segment. Implement both a top-down memoized function f(i, minS) and a bottom-up tabulation, using prefix sums for O(1) segment sum. Return count modulo 1e9+7. N ≤ 200?

In a streaming analytics scenario, you have an array a[0..n-1] of non‑negative costs and a per‑session budget B. Count the number of ways to partition the entire sequence into contiguous sessions so that each session’s sum ≤ B. Return the count mod 1e9+7. Implement both bottom‑up DP (O(n) space) and a top‑down memoized version; discuss edge cases like zeros and very large B?

Given a string s of length N (N up to 10^3) consisting of lowercase letters, find the minimum number of insertions required to transform s into a palindrome. Implement both a top-down memoized function and a bottom-up tabulation, and describe time/space complexities and edge-case handling. Provide a small example: s = "abca" -> 2 insertions?

You're building a budgeting tool: given an array nums of length N with non-negative integers, choose days such that no two chosen days are adjacent and the sum is maximized. Implement a function that returns this max sum. Provide a top-down memoized solution and a bottom-up tabulation, with time/space analyses and edge cases?

Given an array nums of non-negative integers and a target sum S, how many ways are there to assign + or - signs to each element so the total equals S? Implement both a memoized recursive solution and a bottom-up tabulation approach. Example: nums=[1,1,1,1,1], S=3 => 5 ways?

Problem: In an n x m grid with some blocked cells (grid[i][j] = 1 means blocked). From (0,0) to (n-1,m-1) you may move only right or down. You cannot land on blocked cells, and you cannot take more than L consecutive moves in the same direction. Return the number of valid monotone paths modulo 1e9+7. Implement both a memoized DFS and a bottom-up DP; discuss edge cases (start or end blocked, L large, small grids) and runtime?

Given an array nums of positive integers and a target sum S, count the number of subsets that sum exactly to S. Each element can be chosen at most once. Return the answer modulo 1_000_000_007. Provide both a top-down memoized solution and a bottom-up tabulation solution with O(N*S) time; explain edge cases like empty subset and S=0?

Given an array A[1..N] and an integer D, partition A into exactly D non-empty contiguous subarrays. The cost of a subarray is min(subarray) times max(subarray). Return the minimum possible total cost. Provide both a memoized top-down DP and an iterative bottom-up DP implementation, with recurrences, base cases, and time/space analyses. Assume N up to 200 and D up to 20?

In a weighted DAG with N nodes and edges (u, v, w) where w >= 0, count the number of distinct paths from node 0 to node N-1 with total weight <= W. Return modulo 1e9+7. Provide both a memoized top-down DFS and a bottom-up topological DP, each running in O(EW) time with O(NW) space. Include edge cases: unreachable sink, W too small, multiple distinct paths?

You have N days with savings s[1..N]. You may pick any subset of days such that no two chosen days are adjacent. Return the maximum total savings. Provide a memoized (top-down) and a tabulated (bottom-up) solution, and discuss their time/space trade-offs. How would you optimize further?

In an r x c grid, start at (0,0) and end at (r-1,c-1). You may move right or down, some cells are blocked. A separate boolean grid boost[i][j] marks boost cells. You have at most B boosts. If you step on a boost cell you may spend one boost to teleport to any unblocked cell in the same row or column. Count paths modulo 1e9+7. Propose a bottom-up DP with O(r c B) time using row/col prefix sums for boosted sources, and a memoized variant. Discuss edge cases?

Given an array cost of length n with non-negative integers and a budget B, you start at a virtual before-first-step and may jump to i+1 or i+2, paying cost at the landing step. Count the number of distinct paths that end at index n-1 with total cost exactly B, modulo 1e9+7. Implement bottom-up DP with O(n*B) time and O(B) space and a memoized DFS variant; discuss edge cases?

You have an array A of length N and an integer K. Define cost(l,r) = (sum A[l..r])^2 for any 0 <= l <= r < N. Partition A into exactly K contiguous segments to minimize total cost. Propose DP solutions using both memoized top-down and bottom-up tabulation, employing prefix sums for O(1) segment sums. Include time/space analyses and edge-case handling (e.g., N < K)?

Given an array nums of length N and an integer K, compute the maximum sum obtainable by choosing exactly K non-overlapping subarrays (contiguous) of nums. Each chosen subarray contributes its sum to the total; subarrays must be disjoint and ordered left-to-right. Provide both a top-down memoization approach and a bottom-up tabulation approach with O(NK) time and O(NK) space, and discuss edge cases (K > possible, negative values)?

You are given an R x C grid with non-negative integers and -1 representing blocked cells. Start at (0,0) and end at (R-1,C-1). You may move only right or down. The score of a path is the sum of visited cell values. You are allowed to make at most T turns (a direction change). Compute the maximum possible score under this constraint. If no valid path exists within T turns, return negative infinity or a sentinel value. Provide a memoized top-down solution and a bottom-up DP, with time/space complexities and edge cases?

In a workload-balancing context, given an array loads of length n and an integer k, partition the array into exactly k non-empty contiguous blocks. The cost is the maximum sum among blocks. Return the minimum possible cost and the number of partitions achieving it. Provide a memoized top-down DP and a bottom-up DP, and discuss edge cases (n < k, zeros, large sums)?

Given an array revenue of length N, choose exactly K indices such that no two are adjacent to maximize the sum of the selected values. How would you implement both a bottom-up DP (O(NK) time, O(K) space) and a memoized top-down solution, and what edge cases (e.g., K > ceil(N/2)) must you handle?

Given an array profits of length n, you may move from index i to i+1, i+2, or i+3 as long as the destination exists. Each visited index contributes profits[i] to your total. Compute the maximum total you can accumulate when reaching index n−1 and the number of distinct paths achieving this maximum, modulo 1e9+7?

Given an array stones of length n, you may repeatedly merge two adjacent piles into a new pile whose size is the sum of the two, paying that sum, until one pile remains. Implement a bottom-up DP to compute the minimum total merge cost to merge all piles into one. Analyze time and space complexity and edge cases?

Given a grid of size m x n where each cell contains a non-negative integer representing the cost to enter that cell, find the minimum cost path from the top-left corner (0,0) to the bottom-right corner (m-1,n-1) moving only right or down. Return both the minimum cost and the path itself?
Given a string s and dictionary wordDict, return all possible sentences where s can be segmented into space-separated words from wordDict. Handle overlapping subproblems efficiently?

Given an array nums of positive integers and an integer limit, partition nums into contiguous blocks so that the sum of each block is <= limit. The cost of a partition is the sum over blocks of (length)^2. Return the minimum cost and one valid partition achieving it. Provide both a memoized DFS and a bottom-up DP solution with reconstruction. Handle the case where a single element exceeds limit by returning -1?

Given a string s and a dictionary wordDict, return all possible sentences formed by inserting spaces in s such that each word exists in wordDict. Use DP with memoization to avoid exponential recomputation?

Given a string s of length n consisting of lowercase letters and '?', and a dictionary D of m words, partition s into consecutive dictionary words. When a word w is placed at position i, its cost is the number of positions where s[i+j] is a concrete letter and differs from w[j]. '?' matches any letter with zero cost. Minimize total cost to cover the entire s; return the minimum cost and the chosen segmentation. If no segmentation covers s, return -1. Propose an O(n * sum|w|) DP with memoization and backtrace?

Count the number of ways to segment a string s into dictionary words from wordDict; provide both a memoized DFS and an iterative DP solution; discuss how a Trie-based optimization would prune checks and improve runtime. What are the time/space trade-offs and common edge cases?

Given an array of positive integers nums and a target sum S, write a function countSubsets(nums, S) that returns the number of subsets whose elements sum to S. Each element can be used at most once. Provide both memoized top-down and bottom-up tabulation solutions, discuss time/space complexity, and handle cases with zeros and large S under modulo 1e9+7?

Given a string s of length n, what is the minimum number of insertions required to transform s into a palindrome, and provide a bottom-up dynamic programming approach to compute this value in O(n^2) time and space? You may insert any character at any position. For example, 'abca' requires 1 insertion?

Design and implement a function countWays(coins, target) that returns the number of unordered combinations to form target using unlimited coins from coins. For example, coins=[1,2,3], target=4 -> 4 ways. Provide a top-down memoized solution and a bottom-up tabulation solution, with time/space complexity and edge cases?

You are given a convex polygon with n vertices labeled 0..n-1 in order, each vertex i has weight w[i]. The cost of a triangulation is the sum over all triangles of w[a] * w[b] * w[c]. Compute the minimum possible cost and the number of triangulations achieving it. Provide both a top-down memoized interval DP and a bottom-up tabulation solution, and discuss time/space trade-offs?

Given an array A of length N and an integer K, partition A into at most K contiguous subarrays. The cost of a subarray is max(subarray) - min(subarray). Return the minimum total cost and one set of breakpoints. Provide both a memoization-based top-down solution and a bottom-up tabulation variant. Constraints: N <= 2000, K <= 50, A[i] <= 1e9. How would you implement and reconstruct the solution?

Given a string s and a dictionary dict of valid words, how many ways can s be segmented into a sequence of dictionary words? Implement a top-down memoized function countWays(i) that checks substrings s[i:i+len] for len up to maxWordLen, and also provide a bottom-up tabulation version. Constraints: |s| <= 1000, |dict| <= 200, maxWordLen <= 20?

Given an N x M grid of integers, start at (0,0) and reach (N-1,M-1) in exactly k moves. From (i,j) you may move to (i+1,j), (i,j+1), or (i+1,j+1). The score is the sum of visited cells (including start and end). Implement a memoized DFS and a bottom-up tabulation to return the maximum sum, and discuss time/space trade-offs and memory-optimized variants?

In a service-call graph for a distributed system (nodes are services, directed edges carry propagation latency; scenario inspired by internal deployments at MongoDB/Zoom), an origin service issues a config change. Design an algorithm to compute the earliest arrival time for all services, assuming immediate forwarding on receipt and respecting dependency constraints. Explain how you'd use BFS/DFS to explore reachability, Dijkstra for shortest propagation times, and topological sort if the graph is a DAG. Include data structures and complexity?

Given a directed graph with n nodes and m weighted edges (non-negative), and a source s, compute shortest distances from s to all nodes using a topological-order DP if the graph is acyclic. If a cycle is detected, explain how you would fall back to Dijkstra. Provide a function signature and a concise code sketch that handles unreachable nodes, and discuss time/space complexity?

Given a directed graph with N nodes and M edges (weight 1), with some nodes blocked, compute (1) the length of the shortest path from s to t avoiding blocked nodes, and (2) the number of distinct shortest paths modulo 1e9+7. Describe a BFS-based approach that counts shortest paths and discuss edge cases (unreachable, s/t blocked, multiple shortest paths)?

In a directed graph with positive edge weights, some nodes are blocked. From s to t determine: (1) whether a path exists avoiding blocked nodes; (2) the shortest distance; (3) the number of distinct shortest paths modulo 1e9+7. Outline an implementation that uses DFS to prune to the reachable unblocked subgraph, Dijkstra on that subgraph for distances, and a DP on the shortest-path DAG (edges where dist[u]+w=dist[v]) in topological order to count paths. Include edge cases?

Given a directed graph with N nodes, M edges (non-negative weights), and two nodes s and t, compute (1) the length of the shortest s→t path and (2) the number of distinct shortest paths modulo 1e9+7. Use a single Dijkstra pass that also maintains path counts. Describe how you update counts on relaxing edges and when you re-visit with equal distances, and discuss edge cases (unreachable, zero-weight edges, multiple shortest paths)?

Given a directed, weighted graph G=(V,E) with non-negative edge weights, implement a function shortestAndTopOrder(start) that returns: 1) a topological ordering of the DAG portion reachable from start, 2) the shortest distance from start to every node using Dijkstra, and 3) a boolean flag indicating whether any cycle exists in the reachable subgraph. Provide function signatures, a brief sketch, and explain how cycles affect shortest-path computation?

You're given a directed graph with two edge types: A (unweighted, cost 1) and B (weighted, cost w). The subgraph formed by A-edges is acyclic. There may be cycles when B-edges are included. Find the minimum total cost to travel from s to t with at most K B-edges on any path. Propose an algorithm using (1) topological ordering of the A-DAG for DP, (2) a Dijkstra-based layered graph to enforce the B-budget, and (3) a BFS/DFS prune to shrink the search space. Example: N=1e5, M=2e5, K=5?

Scenario: a manufacturing pipeline is a DAG of tasks. Each node i has duration d[i], each edge (u,v) has a setup s[u,v]. A task can start when all prerequisites finish and the maximum EFT[u]+s[u,v] over its incoming edges is achieved. EFT[v] = ES[v]+d[v], ES[v] = max_u(EFT[u]+s[u,v]); sources have EFT = d[i]. The project finish time is max EFT. Compute EFT for all nodes and the number of distinct critical schedules (mod 1e9+7), i.e., number of longest paths achieving the project finish time. Provide an O(N+M) DP?

You're given a DAG G=(V,E) describing tasks with processing times p[u] and edge delays c[u->v]. With unlimited parallelism, makespan is max finish[u], where finish[u] = p[u] + max(0, max_{(w,u) in E}(finish[w] + c[w->u])), and sources finish[u] = p[u]. You may choose at most one edge to set its delay to zero. Which edge yields the largest reduction in makespan, and how would you compute it in O(M log N) time by first obtaining a DFS-based topological order and then a DP pass? Explain data structures and steps?

In a CI pipeline, each node is a task with a duration; edges A->B denote prerequisites. Implement a function earliestFinish(n, edges, duration) that returns the earliest completion time for the entire pipeline, assuming unlimited workers and that a task can start as soon as all its prerequisites finish. Return -1 if there is a cycle. Use a topological DP approach?

In a DAG with N nodes, M non-negative weighted edges, and designated s and t, compute: (1) the number of distinct shortest s→t paths, (2) one concrete shortest s→t path, and (3) the runtime and reconstruction method. Use a topological order. Provide an algorithm sketch and discuss edge cases where multiple paths tie in length. Constraints: large N and M; no negative weights?

You're given a weighted directed graph G=(V,E) with non-negative weights. You have up to K boost tokens; applying a token to edge (u,v) reduces its weight to floor(w(u,v)/2). Compute the minimum travel time from s to t using at most K tokens, and show how to reconstruct the path. Outline the augmented-Dijkstra approach, complexity, and edge cases?

Given a DAG representing a build graph of services, with edge weights as setup times, compute for every node the earliest finish time from source s, the total project duration, and the number of distinct critical paths achieving the duration; also return one example critical path. Provide a topological DP solution, handle up to 2e5 nodes/edges, and avoid recursion depth issues?

Given a directed graph with non-negative weights, compute the length of the second-shortest s→t path (strictly longer than the shortest) and the number of distinct second-shortest paths modulo 1e9+7. Propose a single-pass Dijkstra variant that maintains for every node the two smallest distances and their path counts, handle equal distances, and explain how to count multiple equal shortest paths that lead to distinct second-shortest routes?

Given a DAG where each node is a task with a positive duration and edges u -> v indicate v cannot start until u finishes, write a function that returns (1) the earliest start time for every task and (2) the overall project duration. Input: n, duration[], edges[]. Output: {earliestStart: number[], totalDuration: number}. Assume no cycles; implement using topological sort and dynamic programming; what is the time complexity?

Given a directed weighted graph with edges labeled hard or soft and an integer K, find the minimum-cost path from s to t that uses at most K soft edges. If the graph is a DAG, devise an O(V+E) DP using a topological order; otherwise, build a layered graph with states (node, usedSoft) and run Dijkstra for O((V+E) log(VK)). Specify input/output formats and tie-breaking rules?

Given an undirected weighted graph G=(V,E) with positive weights representing travel times, you have a one-time coupon that halves the weight of exactly one edge on the s→t path. Compute the shortest possible travel time from s to t and identify which edge to discount. Outline the augmented-graph Dijkstra solution, derive the time complexity, and discuss tie-breaking when multiple paths share the same length?

You're given a directed graph G=(V,E) with non-negative edge weights w(u,v) and per-node processing delays d(v). A subset S ⊆ V starts the update at time 0. The finish time of a node v is the earliest time it completes processing after receiving the update along any path from S. Design an algorithm that handles cycles and runs in ~O((V+E) log V). Explain two routes: (1) when G is a DAG (topological DP in O(V+E)); (2) the general case using Dijkstra with transformed edge costs (w(u,v)+d(v)). Provide correctness intuition?

Given a directed acyclic graph G=(V,E) with non-negative edge weights w(u,v). You are given a source S, a target T, and an ordered list of checkpoints [c1,...,ck]. Find the minimum total distance of a path from S to T that visits S -> c1 -> c2 -> ... -> ck -> T in this exact order. If any leg is unreachable, return -1. Describe an O(N+M) approach that uses a topological sort and DP to compute the shortest path for each leg, and explain how you'd reconstruct the full path?

In a DAG G=(V,E) with non-negative weights, there is a source s, a sink t, and a landmark set L of size k (k ≤ 15). Find the minimum-weight s-t path that visits every landmark in L at least once. Output the total weight and the full path. Propose an algorithm leveraging a topological order that runs in O((n+m)(k+1)) time and describe how you reconstruct the path?

In a directed acyclic weighted graph G=(V,E) with non-negative weights, given start S, target T, and a list of k mandatory edges M=[(u1,v1,w1),...,(uk,vk,wk)] that must appear on the S→T path in this exact order, design an algorithm to compute the minimum possible path cost or report impossible. Use a topological order to verify reachability and a DAG DP to compute segment shortest paths from each segment's source to its next target, then sum with the mandatory edge costs and reconstruct the path?

Count the number of distinct shortest paths from s to t in a directed weighted graph with non-negative weights. Describe and implement an algorithm that uses Dijkstra to compute dist[], then builds a shortest-path DAG (edge (u,v) included if dist[u] + w(u,v) == dist[v]), and finally uses DP in topological order to count paths from s to t modulo 1000000007. Include complexity and edge cases?
Given a directed weighted graph with up to 10^6 edges and frequent edge weight updates, design a data structure that supports dynamic shortest path queries with sub-millisecond response time?

Given a DAG G=(V,E) representing a microservice call graph. Each edge (u,v) has a non-negative weight w(u,v). A message starts at source s. In one model, informed nodes can immediately forward along all outgoing edges, but v is only informed after sum of weights along a path from s to v. Compute earliest inform time for every node, i.e., the shortest path distance from s to each node. Provide an O(V+E) solution using a topological order and DP. Explain how you build the topological order and perform relaxations?

Given a directed weighted graph with positive weights, implement a function shortestPathWithOneFreeEdge(graph, src, dst) that returns the minimum travel time from src to dst if you may set the cost of at most one edge on the path to zero. Describe your approach, provide a code sketch, and analyze complexity?

Given a directed, non-negative weighted graph G modeling a road network, implement routePlanner(G, s, t) that returns: shortestTime via Dijkstra from s to t; minHops via BFS from s to t on the unweighted graph; if G is a DAG, earliestArrival times from s to all nodes using topological order; if a cycle exists, report it and skip the DAG part?

Scenario: A DAG-structured transport network has non-negative costs on edges. From a source S, compute the minimum cost to reach every node using at most K edges. Propose an algorithm that uses a topological order and dynamic programming with a state per number of edges, derive the recurrence, show how to reconstruct the path, and discuss complexity. How would you adapt if cycles exist (SCC condensation and DP on the DAG or alternative methods)?

You are given a weighted directed acyclic graph (n nodes, m edges) with non-negative weights. Implement a function to compute the shortest path from a source s to all nodes using a topological order. Provide a code sketch and explain complexity and edge cases?

In a directed weighted graph with non-negative weights, some vertices are landmarks. Find the shortest s->t path that visits at least one landmark. Propose an O((N+M) log N) solution and implement a two-layer graph: state 0 (pre-landmark) and state 1 (landmark visited). Transitions follow edges; if a destination vertex is a landmark, you move to state 1. Return the shortest distance and the number of distinct shortest paths under this constraint, modulo 1e9+7, plus one exemplar path. Handle corner cases (no landmark reachable, s or t is a landmark, multiple shortest paths)?

Given a directed weighted graph with non-negative weights, moving inside any strongly connected component costs 0; crossing components costs the edge weight. Compute the min cost from s to t. Provide: (1) SCC condensation plus topological DP on the DAG; (2) Dijkstra on the condensed DAG. Explain correctness, complexities, and edge cases (e.g., same SCC, no path, multiple edges).?

You are given a directed weighted graph with non-negative weights, node IDs 0..n-1, and two nodes s and t. Compute: 1) the shortest distance from s to t using an O(m log n) approach, 2) the number of distinct shortest s-t paths modulo 1e9+7, and 3) output one shortest path that is lexicographically smallest by node ID. Assume weights are positive to avoid zero-cost cycles. Provide the approach and how to reconstruct the path?

You have a DAG of microservices. Each node v has a startupTime[v] in seconds. An edge u -> v means v cannot start before u is online. You can start multiple services in parallel once their prerequisites are online. Given a target service t, determine the earliest time t can be online and provide a topological order to compute it. Also describe how you would detect cycles and handle them?

Given a directed weighted graph representing a road network with N intersections and M one-way roads, each edge has a positive travel time. S is the start, T the destination, and H is the maximum allowed number of edges (hops). Design an algorithm to compute the fastest route from S to T using at most H edges and reconstruct the path. Provide a JS skeleton for shortestPathWithHops(graph, S, T, H) and path reconstruction?

You have a build pipeline modeled as a DAG. Each node i has duration d[i], and an edge u -> v means v cannot start until u finishes. Implement earliestFinishTimes(graph) that returns a map node -> earliestFinishTime and the project duration. Use a topological sort to process nodes, propagate earliestStart[v] = max(earliestStart[v], finish[u]), then finish[u] = earliestStart[u] + d[u]. Provide a code sketch or pseudocode?

Given a DAG where each node is a task with duration d[v], and an edge u -> v means v starts after u finishes, compute the earliest finish time for every node and identify the project’s critical path (longest duration path). How would you implement a linear-time algorithm using topological sort and dynamic programming, including cycle-detection?

Given a directed graph with N nodes and M edges, non-negative weights, a source s and target t. Design an algorithm to compute: (1) the shortest distance dist[t] from s to t using Dijkstra; (2) the number of distinct shortest paths from s to t modulo 1e9+7. Build a shortest-path DAG with edges (u->v) where dist[u] + w(u,v) = dist[v], then run a topological DP on that DAG to count paths from s to t. Provide implementation outline and time complexity?

Design an algorithm for a directed graph with positive weights. Given source s and target t, compute: (1) the shortest distance dist(s,t), (2) the number of distinct shortest s->t paths modulo 1e9+7, (3) the minimum number of edges among all shortest paths. Propose an implementation that uses Dijkstra to obtain dist, then builds the shortest-path DAG of edges (u,v) with dist[v] = dist[u] + w(u,v) and runs a topological DP to count paths and track minimum hops. Explain time and space?
Explain the difference between BFS and DFS and when would you use each?

Problem: You are given a directed, weighted graph G=(V,E) representing a city map. Some edges are flagged as dependency roads that must respect a topological order. For a given start S and target T, perform: (1) cycle detection with DFS; if a cycle exists, report cyclic. (2) if DAG, compute a topological order and a shortest-path from S to T using a single pass DP along that order. In parallel, compute the minimum hop count from S to T using BFS on the unweighted graph. Return the path and times?

Given a directed graph with nonnegative weights, possibly with cycles. Find the shortest path from s to t and output the path. Your task should exploit graph structure: first compute SCCs (via Tarjan/DFS), condense to a DAG, and compute distances by a topological order DP; inside each SCC run limited Dijkstra between boundary vertices to capture intra-component costs. Present path reconstruction?

Given a directed graph G=(V,E) with node costs d[v], start s, target t. First, detect cycles with DFS and report any cycle nodes; if no cycle, compute a topological order and then: for each v, earliestFinish[v] = max over u in preds(v) of earliestFinish[u] + d[v], with earliestFinish[s] = d[s]. Output earliestFinish[t]. Second, count the number of distinct s→t paths that achieve earliestFinish[t], modulo 1e9+7. Explain data structures, steps, and time complexity?

You are given a DAG with n nodes and m edges. Each edge has a color from a small set {A,B,C}. From a start node s, compute for every node v the minimum number of color changes required to reach v (a color change occurs when consecutive edges have different colors; the first edge does not count as a change). Also compute the number of distinct paths achieving that minimum modulo 1e9+7. Propose an O(m) DP using topological order and explain how to track the color state and counts?

You are given a directed acyclic graph with n nodes, m weighted edges (weights non-negative). Node 0 is the source. Compute for every node the shortest distance from 0 and the number of distinct shortest paths to that node. Use a single topological order and DP. Return dist and counts modulo 1e9+7. Explain time complexity and how you handle unreachable nodes?

Given a directed graph representing city intersections and one-way streets, implement a function to find if there's a valid route from point A to point B using BFS. Return the shortest path distance or -1 if no route exists?
Given a directed acyclic graph representing task dependencies where each task takes 1 unit of time and you have unlimited workers, what is the minimum time to complete all tasks?

Given a weighted directed graph with N nodes and M edges, positive weights, and two nodes s and t, implement a function that returns the shortest distance from s to t and the number of distinct shortest paths achieving that distance. Provide a signature and concise outline of the update rules, and explain complexity and edge cases?

In a project planning DAG, each node represents a task with a duration; edges u -> v mean v cannot start until u finishes. Implement a function that returns the minimum total time to finish all tasks (the makespan) assuming unlimited parallelism. Use a topological-sort-based approach and provide a concise code sketch?

You're given a DAG representing tasks with dependencies and durations. Each node has a positive duration. Implement earliestFinishTimes(n, edges, durations) that returns the earliest finish time for every node assuming all prerequisites finish before a task starts. Use a topological sort to process tasks in dependency order. Provide a signature, outline the algorithm, and its time complexity. Realistic scenario: building a data pipeline?

Given a DAG where each node i has a duration d[i], and edges (u -> v) indicate that v cannot start until u finishes, write a function to compute the minimum total project duration assuming unlimited parallelism. Return both the finish time of every task and the overall project duration. Use a topological ordering approach and describe its time complexity?

You're given a DAG of modules. Each node i has processing time d[i], each edge (u,v) has transfer time t[u][v]. A node can start only after all predecessors finish and data arrives. Using a single worker, (a) compute earliest finish times and the critical path via topological order; (b) compute the minimum end-to-end latency from source to sink along any path by running Dijkstra on a transformed graph where edge weight is t[u][v] + d[v] (initial cost includes d[source])?

Context: algorithms/graphs, beginner. Scenario: a build-pipeline DAG where each edge (u,v) has a non-negative duration to finish the dependency; node 0 is the start. Implement a function shortestPathDAG(n, edges, start, target) that returns the earliest finish time to target and the actual path. Use a DFS-based topological sort to order nodes, then relax edges in that order. If target is unreachable, return -1 and empty path. Provide a concise code sketch and explain correctness and complexity?

Design an algorithm for a DAG G=(V,E) where each edge e has two attributes: latency w(e) >= 0 and a boolean skip(e) indicating latency can be skipped but the edge still counts as a step. Given source s and target t, find a path from s to t that minimizes the tuple (hops, total_latency), where total_latency sums w(e) for edges with skip(e)=false. Output the path and the metric. Explain how to detect cycles if present and how to adapt?

Given a directed graph with N nodes and M weighted edges (positive weights) and a source s, describe an implementation to (1) identify nodes reachable from s via BFS, (2) compute shortest distances dist[] to all nodes with Dijkstra, and (3) count the number of distinct shortest s→v paths for every v (mod 1e9+7). How would you build a DAG of edges on shortest paths and perform a topological DP over dist-ordered nodes to obtain path counts?

Model city roads as a directed, weighted graph with non-negative weights. Given start s and target t, compute: 1) the shortest distance from s to t using Dijkstra; 2) the number of distinct shortest paths from s to t (mod 1e9+7); 3) one concrete shortest path as a node sequence. Then describe how to identify all vertices that lie on any shortest path without enumerating all paths, using a topological view of the shortest-path subgraph?

Design an algorithm to compute the shortest s→t distance in a directed, weighted graph with non-negative weights, where you may set the weight of at most K edges along the chosen path to 0 (free passes). Edges beyond K must keep their original weights. Provide a function signature and a compact code sketch, discuss data structures, and analyze time/memory complexity. Include path reconstruction and edge cases?

You're given a DAG with N tasks; each task i has duration d[i] > 0 and edges i -> j mean i must finish before j starts. Implement a function computeEarliestFinish(n, durations, edges) that returns {est, total}. Use a topological order to compute est[i] = durations[i] if in-degree of i is 0 else max(est[p] + durations[i] for all predecessors p). Return est and total = max est; assume acyclic. How would you handle a cycle?

You are given a graph of tasks with dependencies as a directed graph (edge u -> v means u must finish before v). Implement a function that, for any given graph, returns a valid build order if the graph is a DAG, or returns the first detected directed cycle as a list of node IDs. Use DFS with color marking to detect cycles and produce a topological sort for acyclic graphs. Provide a compact function signature and brief reasoning?

Given a DAG of tasks with dependencies, implement a function topoSort(n, edges) that returns a valid topological order to execute tasks, or null if a cycle exists. Then implement a BFS-based routine to compute the minimum number of steps to reach each task from a given root task. How would you implement both and handle edge cases?
Explain the differences between round-robin, least connections, and IP hash load balancing algorithms. When would you choose each one?
Explain the difference between round-robin and weighted round-robin load balancing algorithms. When would you choose one over the other?
You have an array where each element appears twice except one element that appears once. Sort the array in O(n) time without using extra space for sorting. How would you approach this?
Compare QuickSort, MergeSort, and Timsort. When would you choose each algorithm and what are their key trade-offs in production systems?

Implement a sort(arr) function that guarantees O(n log n) worst-case time by using Introsort: start with a quicksort partition (3-way to handle duplicates) and track recursion depth. If depth exceeds 2*floor(log2(n)), switch to heapsort for the remaining elements. Provide a complete self-contained JavaScript implementation and discuss time/space trade-offs and stability?

Design and implement an in-place, three-way partition quicksort optimized for arrays with many duplicates. Use a Dutch flag style partitioning into < pivot, == pivot, and > pivot regions. Aim for average time O(n log m) where m is the number of distinct keys, and O(log n) extra space via tail recursion. Compare to a standard top-down mergesort (O(n log n), extra space). Include edge cases (all equal, already sorted, no duplicates) and provide a compact skeleton plus a test plan?

Design a stable, cache-aware hybrid sort. You have an array of objects {key: number, value: any} with up to 1e6 elements. Implement hybridSort that uses quicksort on partitions below a cache-friendly threshold and a bottom-up mergesort pass on larger partitions to guarantee worst-case O(n log n) time and O(n) extra space. Explain edge cases (duplicates, empty input) and provide a concise complexity analysis?

Design and implement a function sortBatch(arr) that sorts an array of integers using a hybrid strategy: for subarrays of length 16 or less, use insertion sort; for larger segments, use merge sort with a single preallocated buffer of size n. The aim is to minimize overhead while keeping O(n log n) time and O(n) space. Explain your choices?

Implement an in-place introsort for an array of integers: start with quicksort using median-of-three pivot, and switch to heapsort when recursion depth exceeds 2*log2(n). Provide the core functions and explain the reasoning behind the depth-guard, including time and space complexity. Assume worst-case input like already sorted or reverse-sorted?

Design and implement an in-place introsort-based sorter: start with quicksort using median-of-three pivot; track recursion depth; if depth exceeds 2*log2(n), switch to heapsort for the rest of the array. Provide a robust version in your language of choice and discuss edge cases, stability implications, and memory usage?

You are given an array of n integers composed of r sorted runs. Design an algorithm to sort the full array in O(n log r) time using O(r) extra space by performing a k-way merge. Outline run-detection in a single pass and implement the merge step with a min-heap over the current heads from each run. Include analysis of edge cases: empty input, all elements equal, and r=1?

Design an external sort for N records, each 100 B, stored on disk, with 256 MB RAM. Use in-memory sorts for chunks and a k-way merge to produce a single sorted file by key. Provide: how to choose chunk size, the number of passes, and a rough I/O cost. Include a concrete example with N=10^9, block size 4 KB?

Design a cache-aware hybrid sort: partition the array into fixed-size blocks, sort each block in place with quicksort, then perform a bottom-up in-place merge across neighboring blocks using a small buffer of size B to merge. Choose B to fit L1/L2 cache. Analyze time, memory, and stability?

Design a stable hybrid sort for an array of 32-bit integers that blends QuickSort and MergeSort to guarantee O(n log n) worst-case time while using O(n) extra space. Start with an introspective QuickSort with depth limit log2(n); if a partition is unbalanced or a long run of identical elements is detected, switch to a stable MergeSort using a single auxiliary buffer. Describe your pivot strategy, switching criteria, and provide a concise code sketch for the hybrid sorter?

Implement an in-place, non-recursive 3-way quicksort to sort an array of integers with many duplicates. Use a stack for subproblems and Dutch National Flag partitioning (<, ==, >). How does median-of-three pivot choice help avoid degeneracy, and how does your approach handle worst-case inputs? Provide a complete in-place implementation and complexity reasoning?

Design a hybrid sorting engine for an array of 64-bit integers that blends QuickSort and MergeSort to maximize cache efficiency and worst-case performance. Implement an in-place hybrid where subarrays larger than a threshold use QuickSort, and smaller ones switch to a bottom-up, in-place stable MergeSort. Use a depth limit of 2*log2(n). Provide an implementation in JavaScript and analyze time/space?

Design and implement an in-place, hybrid sort for an array of integers that uses quicksort with three-way partitioning on subarrays with few duplicates and switches to an in-place, stable merge-based sort for blocks of equal values to minimize data movement; discuss the insertion-sort threshold, stability, and edge cases (all equal, already sorted, all unique). How would you implement it?

In a log processing context with many duplicate timestamps, design an in-place, cache-friendly sort that guarantees O(n log n) worst-case time and minimal data movement. Outline an introspective three-way quicksort: median-of-three pivot, Dutch national flag partition for duplicates, and switch to heapsort if recursion depth exceeds 2 log n. Provide pseudocode and brief complexity notes?

You're processing a disk-stored batch of N records, each record is (ts: int64, id: int32, value: float). RAM holds M records. Describe a robust two-pass external sort to order by ts ascending, then by id ascending. Explain how you form initial runs, the k-way merge strategy, and the overall I/O and time complexity given N >> M. Include a concise in-memory sort used for runs?

Given an array of objects {id, priority (1-3), time}, write a stable sort that orders first by priority ascending and, within the same priority, by time ascending. Implement in JavaScript without relying on any built-in multi-key sort utilities and explain the time/space trade-offs?

Scenario: You have an array of N records, each with a 32-bit unsigned key and payload. N up to 1e7. Design a practical, stable sort that uses O(1) extra space and runs efficiently on real hardware. Propose a hybrid in-place MSD radix approach that sorts by the top 16 bits first using in-place three-way partitioning, then recursively sorts the partitions and merges with in-place rotation to preserve stability. Include a plan to bound worst-case to O(n log n) via a depth limit switch to heap sort?

Design and implement a hybrid sort that blends quicksort and mergesort: start with standard quicksort partitioning; when a partition's size falls below a threshold (e.g., 32), switch to stable mergesort for that partition to improve cache locality and stability. The algorithm should sort in ascending order. Provide pseudocode or real code, and analyze worst-case time complexity, including how the threshold affects runtime. Address duplicates and memory usage?

Implement a bottom-up iterative mergesort to sort a singly linked list of integers in non-decreasing order; describe how you split into blocks of size w, merge adjacent blocks in place by relinking nodes, and terminate when a single list remains, and provide the merge routine for two sorted sublists?

Scenario: You receive a batch of N integers that is almost sorted—each element is at most k positions away from its final place. Implement a stable sort in O(n log k) time using a min-heap of size k+1 and O(k) extra space. Include lightweight test data and justify when this beats standard O(n log n) sorts in practice?

You have N integers stored on disk and can hold at most M in memory at a time. Design an external merge sort: generate sorted runs by batching M items, sort each in memory, and write runs back. Then perform a  k-way merge with a min-heap across the runs, repeating until a single sorted output remains. Describe run generation, merge strategy, and analyze I/O and time?

Given an array of 32-bit integers, sort them primarily by the number of set bits in their binary representation (Hamming weight) ascending, and secondarily by numeric value ascending. Propose a stable sorting approach, implement it (you may pick mergesort, which is stable by default), and explain the time and space complexity. Explain why stability matters here and how ties are resolved?

Design a sorting routine that guarantees O(n log n) worst-case in-place while efficiently handling duplicates. Implement a 3-way quicksort using a deterministic median-of-medians pivot and partition into <, =, > without extra memory. For subarrays larger than a threshold (e.g., 64), switch to an in-place bottom-up merge pass that merges adjacent runs. Provide core functions and analyze trade-offs?

Scenario: In a data processing service, you must sort an array of n 32-bit integers in ascending order in-place, with no more than O(1) extra space. Propose a practical hybrid sorting approach that minimizes cache misses and handles adversarial inputs. Describe your pivot strategy (e.g., median-of-three), 3-way partitioning, threshold for switching to insertion sort, and whether to implement recursively or iteratively. Provide a concise outline and justification?

Design an in-place, stable sort for an array of integers with O(1) extra space and O(n log n) worst-case time. You may implement a bottom-up in-place mergesort with a rotation-based merge, or a stable partition-based quicksort. Describe the approach, outline the core in-place merge or partition operation, invariants, and the precise time/space trade-offs?

Given an array A of size n containing integers with many duplicates and a highly skewed distribution, implement a 3-way partition quicksort to sort A in O(n log n) average time. Use a pivot p and partition into <p, =p, >p; move elements accordingly so all equals cluster in the middle. This avoids quadratic behavior on duplicates. For worst-case, switch to introsort or heapsort when recursion depth grows beyond log n; keep in-place with O(log n) stack?

Sort an array of n integers where values are in the range [0, 9999] in non-decreasing order using only O(log n) extra space (excluding the output). Propose a practical in-place sort variant that achieves O(n log n) time and explain how the in-place merge works, including a small example of the merge step and why it is stable?

Given an array of integers with many duplicates, implement an in-place 3-way quicksort that partitions into less than, equal to, and greater than the pivot and then recursively sorts the outer partitions. Include a discussion of pivot selection (random vs median-of-three) and analyze best, average, and worst-case time complexity?

Design and implement a hybrid sort that first detects monotone runs in the input array, sorts each run with insertion sort if the run length is <= 32 or else with mergesort, and finally merges all sorted runs using a min-heap to produce a fully sorted array. Provide a concrete implementation and analyze the expected time and space complexity, as well as stability. End with a brief justification of when this approach shines?

Design an in-place hybrid sort (introsort) that starts with quicksort using median-of-three pivot, tracks recursion depth, and switches to heapsort if depth exceeds 2*log2(n). Use insertion sort for small partitions. Explain how you ensure O(n log n) worst-case, in-place memory usage, and how duplicates affect behavior?

In a telemetry data pipeline, implement a hybrid sorter for an array of n 64-bit integers that begins with quicksort but switches to mergesort when the recursion depth exceeds 2 log2 n or a partition becomes imbalanced. The goal is to guarantee O(n log n) worst-case time with O(log n) extra space. Provide an implementation and complexity analysis, including how duplicates are handled and performance on nearly-sorted data?

Design and implement a hybrid sorter for an array of N integers with many duplicates. Start with a 3-way partition quicksort to minimize swaps; track recursion depth. If depth exceeds 2*log2(N) or a partition is small, switch to mergesort (or heapsort) for the remaining parts to guarantee O(n log n) worst-case. How would you implement this and justify the transitions?

Scenario: you process N events with a 64-bit timestamp and payload, and must sort by timestamp while keeping memory usage near O(n) with external storage. Propose a hybrid sort that uses in‑memory quicksort for small runs and a stable mergesort for larger runs, via a radix-like partitioning of data into blocks that fit in memory. Describe partitioning, the in‑memory strategy, the final merge, and the expected complexity and tradeoffs?

Implement an iterative quicksort using an explicit stack to sort an array of integers in ascending order. Describe how you manage subarray bounds, partitioning, and pivot choice; avoid recursion. Compare its average and worst-case time against mergesort and discuss space usage?

Implement a sorting function sortWithEarlyMerge(arr) that sorts an array of integers by first performing a single O(n) check for nondecreasing order; if already sorted, return arr. Otherwise, perform an iterative (bottom-up) mergesort. Provide the code and explain the time complexities?

Implement an in-place hybrid sort: use 3-way quicksort partitioning for large subarrays and switch to insertion sort when the subarray size is 16 or less; assume random pivot selection to reduce worst-case risk. Explain average time complexity, worst-case behavior, and memory usage, and why this hybrid is beneficial in practice compared to a standard mergesort?

Given an array of strings (handles), sort them first by length ascending; if two handles share the same length, sort them lexicographically. Implement a stable mergesort in JavaScript (no built-in sort) that preserves input order for equal keys. Provide the function and a brief justification of stability and the overall time/space complexity?

Design an adaptive sort for an array of integers that uses a 3-way quicksort (Dutch national flag) with median-of-three pivot and tail recursion elimination, plus a depth-limit: if depth exceeds 2*log2(n), switch to a stable mergesort that uses an auxiliary buffer. The merge step may use O(n) extra space. Explain how this hybrid handles duplicates and avoids worst-case behavior?

Context: You have an array of n log entries, each {ts: number, msg: string}. The array is unsorted by ts. Implement an in-place, stable sort that uses O(1) extra space and runs in O(n log n) time on average. Provide a concrete in-place merge procedure (recursive or bottom-up) and analyze stability and worst-case behavior. Include a small in-place example demonstrating correctness?

Given an array of n integers where every element is in the inclusive range 0 to 9, sort the array in O(n) time with O(1) extra space. Explain the counting sort approach for fixed-range digits, outline the two passes (count and write-back), and show a concise in-place implementation?

Context: Given an array of N integers (duplicates allowed). Implement a stable sort that returns a permutation P of indices so that A[P[0]] <= A[P[1]] <= ... <= A[P[N-1]], preserving the relative order of equal elements. Do this with a stable sorting strategy and return both P and the corresponding sorted values?

You are given an array of events where each element is an object {id: string, ts: number}. Sort the array by ts in ascending order but preserve the original relative order for events with identical ts. Implement a stable O(n log n) solution and explain how stability is maintained during the merge steps?

You have an array of objects each with fields score (int) and time (int). Sort by score ascending and preserve the original order for equal scores. Propose and implement a stable sort that uses minimal extra memory (O(n)) for n elements, and compare its worst-case time to quicksort. What would your approach look like in code?

Given an array of 64-bit integers, design a hybrid in-place sorter that is stable and memory-efficient. Combine a 3-way quicksort partitioning pass with a bottom-up mergesort for runs, reusing a fixed-size scratch buffer. Explain pivot selection, when to switch, and analyze worst-case and average complexities for varying duplicate densities?

Design and implement an introsort variant: a hybrid of quicksort and heapsort with a depth limit floor(2*log2(n)). Perform quicksort with a 3-way partition; if the recursion depth ever exceeds the limit for a subarray, switch to heapsort on that subarray to guarantee O(n log n) worst-case. Provide an in-place JavaScript implementation sorting an array of integers and explain pivot strategy and complexities?
Explain the difference between quicksort and mergesort, including their time and space complexities?

Design a hybrid in-place sorting algorithm that uses quicksort with median-of-three pivot and a depth limit of 2*log2(n). If recursion depth for a subarray exceeds the limit, switch to an in-place mergesort for that subarray to avoid worst-case behavior. Explain pivot choice, switching threshold, and the overall time and space bounds, including how you handle small partitions?

Given two sorted arrays A and B, where A has length m with m valid elements and enough trailing space to hold n additional elements from B, merge B into A in-place so the final A is sorted with all m+n elements.
