Propose a delete-friendly sketch, update and query times in terms of U, n, B, eps, and compare to exact rebuild after every batch. How would you design and analyze this?

You're monitoring a sensor streaming values v_t in [0, M-1], arriving in batches of size B. After each batch, compute online linear regression with x = t (time) and y = v_t to estimate the trend. Propose O(1) updates per sample using running sums (n, sumX, sumY, sumXX, sumXY), then slope m = (n*sumXY - sumX*sumY) / (n*sumXX - sumX^2). State per-element update, memory usage, and compare to reprocessing all data each batch (O(n) time). Include a short concrete example that demonstrates the updates?

You have a directed graph with n nodes; edges can be added or removed in online batches of size B. After each batch, compute the exact number of nodes reachable from a fixed influencer t within at most H hops. Propose a practical incremental structure that (i) precomputes a compact reachability index, (ii) updates amortized per batch for both insertions and deletions, (iii) answers the count in O(1) or near, (iv) uses near-linear space, (v) provides two optimizations, and (vi) compares to rebuilding reachability from scratch after every batch. Give asymptotics in n, m, B, H?

Design a tiered dynamic array using blocks of sizes 1,2,4,8,... . Each batch inserts B elements by placing them into the smallest available block; when a block overflows, merge with the next block in a binary-counter fashion. After each batch, state the amortized insertion cost per element and the worst-case time to answer a range-sum query on [l,r)?

A logistics network expands: weighted undirected graph with n nodes. Edges arrive online in batches of size B. After each batch, report the total weight of the minimum spanning forest (MSF). Propose a practical incremental-MSF maintenance structure: (i) preprocessing time/space, (ii) amortized per-batch update time, (iii) query time for MSF weight, (iv) memory, (v) two optimizations, (vi) a comparison to rebuilding the MSF after every batch. Give asymptotics in n, m, B?

In a streaming analytics pipeline for ad clicks, events arrive in batches of size B. You must maintain a sliding window of the last W events and after each batch output the top-3 most frequent user_ids in the window. Design a data structure that supports per-event insertions and evictions with amortized O(log n) time and O(n) memory, while answering the top-3 in O(1). Provide a tight amortized analysis and compare to recomputing frequencies from scratch after every batch. Ignore deletions other than evictions?

Design a dynamic array stored on disk (external memory) that grows geometrically by factor g>1. Elements are appended and resizing copies contents. In the external-memory model with block size B, after N insertions, derive the amortized I/O per insertion for g=2 and g=1.5, and discuss cache implications. Propose two practical optimizations and compare to rebuilding from scratch?

Maintain a dynamic convex hull via batches: points arrive in batches of B; after each batch, output the perimeter of the convex hull of all points seen so far. Propose a practical incremental convex hull data structure that (i) supports batched inserts efficiently, (ii) updates the hull in amortized O(log n) per point, (iii) reports the hull perimeter in O(1), (iv) uses near-linear space, (v) includes two optimizations, and (vi) compares to rebuilding the hull after every batch. Provide asymptotics in terms of n=total points and B?

Streaming bipartiteness: edges arrive in online batches of size B; after each batch determine whether the undirected graph remains bipartite. Propose an incremental DSU with parity that processes a batch in O(B α(n)) time, uses O(n) space, and answers isBipartite in O(1) per batch. Include two practical optimizations and a comparison to recomputing from scratch?

You're ingesting a real-time stream of user IDs representing actions in a web app. After each batch of B IDs, output the top-K most active users by total actions seen so far, without storing a full histogram over M IDs. Propose a streaming top-K algorithm (e.g., generalized Misra-Gries), specify per-element update time, memory O(K), and accuracy guarantees. Compare to a naïve O(M) histogram approach?

Grid percolation with batched edge additions. An n×n grid, edges activate in online batches of size B (no deletions). After each batch, determine if a path exists from the left boundary to the right boundary using only activated edges. Propose a practical incremental connectivity structure that (i) processes each edge insertion near-constantly, (ii) answers in O(1) per batch, (iii) uses near-linear space, (iv) includes two optimizations, and (v) compares to rebuilding from scratch. Provide asymptotics in n,B?

You receive a real-time stream of user IDs in [0, N-1], arriving in batches of size B. After each batch, output the number of distinct users appearing in the last W events (a sliding window). Propose an online approach using a fixed-size window and a hash map of counts, describe how you handle evictions, provide per-element and per-batch time complexities, memory usage, and compare to recomputing from scratch. Include a concrete numeric example with W=6, B=3 and events: 2,5,2,7,2,3,5, showing the distinct count after each batch?

You receive a real-time stream of integers in [0, M-1], arriving in batches of size B. After each batch, output the smallest subset of seen values that accounts for at least 95% of all readings so far. Propose a streaming method with fixed memory to maintain value frequencies, and analyze per-element update cost, per-batch query cost, and memory usage. Include a small example?

Real-time stream of integers in [0, M-1] arriving in batches of size B. After each batch, estimate the total number of distinct values seen so far with bounded memory. Propose a HyperLogLog sketch with m registers; specify per-element update, batch time, memory O(m), and error guarantee (relative RMSE ≈ 1.04/√m). Compare to exact counting requiring O(M) memory. Include an example?

You start with an empty string S. You get online batches of B characters to append. After each batch, output the number of distinct substrings of S. Propose a practical incremental algorithm using a suffix automaton; show that extending by a batch takes O(B) amortized time and O(n) space, discuss alphabet size impact, and compare to recomputing from scratch?

You have an array a[1..n] of integers. Process online batches of B point updates (i, delta) that modify a[i] by adding delta. After each batch, output the maximum subarray sum of the updated array. Propose and justify a batched sqrt-decomposition data structure that (i) stores per-block summary data to support the overall max-subarray sum, (ii) rebuilds only affected blocks per batch, (iii) includes two optimizations to reduce rebuilds, and (iv) compares to recomputing Kadane from scratch after every batch. Include preprocessing, amortized per-batch time, and memory?

Real-time sessions: maintain last_seen timestamps for active sessions; you receive online batches of B events: (a) add a new session at time t, or (b) refresh an existing session to t' > t. After each batch, report how many sessions have last_seen within the last W seconds. Propose a practical data structure and an amortized update/query analysis; include preprocessing, memory, and a comparison to recalculating counts from scratch after every batch?

You receive a real-time stream of integers in [0, M-1], batch size B. After each batch, output the top-2 most frequent values seen so far. Propose a fixed-memory streaming algorithm (e.g., Misra-Gries) with m counters to identify heavy hitters. Analyze per-element update time, per-batch query time, and memory usage. Include a small example?

Maintain the number of triangles in an undirected graph as edges are added online in batches of size B. After each batch, print the triangle count. Propose a practical incremental triangle counting scheme using degree-based orientation (orient edges from lower-degree to higher-degree vertex). When a batch adds edges, count new triangles by intersecting neighbor lists of oriented endpoints, updating the total. Include preprocessing, per-batch amortized time and space, and compare to rebuilding from scratch. Define parameters n, m, B, and initial triangle count?

You monitor a set of n routes with a live travel-time value t[i]. Online you receive batches of B updates changing t[i] to a new value. After each batch, output the sum of the K smallest travel times (K fixed, e.g., 50). Propose a practical data structure that exactly maintains the K smallest values, handles updates amortized, and uses near-linear memory. Include preprocessing, two optimizations, and a comparison to recomputing K smallest from scratch after every batch. Provide asymptotics in n, B, K?

You are processing a real-time clickstream where each event is a product_id in [0, M-1]. Every batch of B events arrives, and you must report the current top-3 product IDs within the sliding window of the last W events. With memory limited to O(W) extra, propose a practical exact-maintenance approach to keep the top-3 as items enter and leave the window, specify per-element update time, worst-case memory, and compare to recomputing the top-3 from scratch after each batch?

Maintain an array a[1..n] of integers with online point updates in batches of size B. After each batch, output the length of the Longest Increasing Subsequence (LIS) of the current array. Propose a batched data structure that (i) updates in O(log n) per index, (ii) yields LIS length in O(1) after a batch, (iii) uses near-linear memory, (iv) includes two optimizations, and (v) compares to recomputing LIS from scratch after every batch. Provide preprocessing, amortized per-batch cost, and memory bounds?

You receive a real-time stream of user IDs (strings) in batches of size B. After each batch, output the approximate cardinality of distinct IDs seen so far using bounded memory. Propose a HyperLogLog solution with m registers, specify per-element update steps, memory usage, error guarantees (about 1.04/√m), and how to merge counts from multiple streams. Compare to exact counting requiring O(U) memory. Provide asymptotics in N, m, B?

Maintain a dynamic set P of 2D points with online insertions in batches of size B. After each batch, determine whether any two points lie within distance D of each other. Propose a practical data structure and an amortized analysis that (i) inserts efficiently, (ii) answers the yes/no query in O(1) or near-constant time, (iii) uses near-linear space, and (iv) includes two optimizations and a comparison to rebuilding from scratch after every batch. Express asymptotics in n=|P|, B, D, and coordinate bounds?

You have a text stream that only appends, with batches of B characters at a time. After each batch, output the number of distinct substrings in the current text. Propose a data structure to support updates in amortized O(B) time per batch (i.e., O(total length) over all batches), explain how to maintain the suffix automaton, give space bounds, and compare to rebuilding a suffix array after each batch?

Incremental single-source shortest paths with batched edge insertions: You have a directed graph G=(V,E) with nonnegative weights. Edges are added only in batches of size B. After each batch you must output SSSP distances from a fixed source s to all nodes within a (1+ε) approximation. Propose a practical incremental structure that (i) preprocesses in O(m log n), (ii) amortized updates per batch of O(B log n / ε), (iii) answers dist(s,v) in O(1) for all v using stored buckets, (iv) uses near-linear space, (v) includes two optimizations, (vi) compares to re-running Dijkstra after every batch. Give asymptotics in n,m,B,ε?

You maintain an array a[1..n]. Online batches of B point updates set a[i] = v. After each batch, output the length of the LIS of the current array. Propose a practical data-structure approach (e.g., sqrt-decomposition with per-block LIS summaries and a merge procedure) that supports updates and LIS queries efficiently. Provide preprocessing, memory bounds, and asymptotics, plus two optimizations. Compare to recomputing LIS from scratch after every batch?

You receive a real-time stream of integers in [0, M-1], arriving in batches of size B. After each batch, output the current top-k most frequent values seen so far, without storing a count for every possible value. Propose a fixed-memory online algorithm (e.g., Misra-Gries heavy-hitters) to maintain an approximate top-k, specify update time per element, per-batch query cost, and expected error characteristics. Include a small example with M=100, k=3, B=5 and two batches?

You maintain an array a[1..n] of integers. Online, you receive batches of B point updates (i, v) changing a[i] to v. After each batch, output the number of local inversions with distance at most d, i.e., pairs (i, j) where i<j, j-i <= d, and a[i] > a[j]. Propose a practical structure with preprocessing, amortized update time, memory bounds, two optimizations, and a comparison to recomputing all such pairs after every batch. Provide asymptotics in n, d, B?

You maintain a stream of numeric events that arrive only in batches of B values. After each batch, you need the k-th smallest value seen so far (k fixed, e.g., 100). Propose a practical data structure and amortized analysis for: (i) batch insertion cost, (ii) k-th retrieval, (iii) memory usage. Compare to rebuilding a balanced BST after each batch. Provide asymptotics in n=|S|, B, k?

You maintain a dynamic multiset of n numbers. Updates arrive in batches of B (insert new element or update an existing value). After each batch, output the sum of the largest K elements. Propose a practical two-structure approach, analyze amortized per-batch update time, and compare to recomputing the top-K from scratch after every batch; discuss edge cases when K is small vs large?

You receive a real-time stream of integers in [0, M-1], arriving in batches of size B. After each batch, estimate the median of all values seen so far using a fixed-bin histogram with W buckets, instead of maintaining exact counts. Propose the histogram design, per-element update time, per-query time to estimate the median, and the error bound relative to the true median. Include a concrete example with M=100, W=10, B=5 and two batches?

You receive a real-time stream of integers in [0, M-1], arriving in batches of size B. After each batch, output the p-th percentile (e.g., 90th) of all values seen so far, under a fixed memory budget of K buckets. Propose a fixed-bin histogram approach, explain bucket mapping and boundary choice, and analyze per-element update time, per-batch query time, and memory usage. Include a small example?

You have a permutation a[1..n]. Partition indices into consecutive blocks of size K. For every pair of blocks (p<q) maintain inv(p,q) = number of inversions with i in block p and j in block q. After each batch of B updates (i, v) preserving the permutation, update the data structure and report the total number of inversions by summing inv(p,q) over all p<q. Propose a practical sqrt-decomposition design: (i) preprocessing, (ii) amortized update time per updated index, (iii) batch reporting time, (iv) memory, (v) two optimizations, (vi) comparison to recomputing inversions from scratch. Provide asymptotics in n, K, B?

You start with a set of N closed, non-overlapping intervals on the real line. Online, you receive batches of B new intervals [l, r] (l <= r). After each batch, update the union of all intervals and report the total covered length. Propose a practical data structure that supports batch inserts, with preprocessing, amortized per interval insertion time, memory bounds, two optimizations, and a comparison to recomputing the union from scratch after every batch. Provide asymptotics in N, B, and coordinate range?

Design a streaming top-K frequency estimator for batches of B events with n possible keys. Use a Count-Min Sketch (width w, depth d) to estimate counts and a min-heap of size K to track current top-K. After each batch, explain how you update CMS, refresh the heap, and bound the amortized per-event cost. Provide asymptotics in terms of n, B, K, w, d, and two practical optimizations; compare to exact hash-map tracking with rebuilds?

You hold an array a of length n with values in [1..D]. You receive online batches of B point updates (set a[i] = v). After each batch, output the two most frequent values in a and their counts. Propose a data structure to maintain top-2 frequencies with amortized update time for a batch, memory usage, and compare to recomputing frequencies from scratch after every batch. Provide asymptotics in n, B, D?

You're streaming user IDs during login events arriving in batches of B. After each batch, estimate the total number of unique users seen so far. Propose a HyperLogLog sketch with m registers. State memory O(m), per-element update O(1), and error ~1.04/√m. How to choose m for target relative error ε and confidence δ? Compare to exact counting requiring O(U) memory?

You have an initially empty sequence. You receive online batches of B insertions; after each batch, compute the total number of inversions in the concatenated sequence formed by all inserted values. Propose a practical data structure and amortized update scheme to maintain the exact inversion count with online inserts, achieving O(B log U) per batch using coordinate compression, and discuss handling duplicates and memory usage?

Maintain a streaming 2D Pareto frontier: you start empty and receive online batches of B points (x,y) with x,y ≥ 0. After each batch, output the current Pareto frontier F (maximizing both coordinates): no point outside F dominates a point in F. Propose a data structure and algorithm that (i) supports batched insertions efficiently, (ii) yields amortized update cost per batch, (iii) lists the frontier in O(|F|) time, (iv) uses near-linear space, (v) includes two optimizations, and (vi) compares to rebuilding the frontier after every batch. Provide asymptotics in n and B?

You maintain a DAG with n nodes. Edges arrive online in batches of size B; each batch adds edges (u -> w) but keeps the graph acyclic. After each batch you must output a valid topological order and support O(1) predecessor checks using that order. Propose a practical data structure and amortized analysis that (i) updates the order efficiently with batch inserts, (ii) uses near-linear space, (iii) confines reordering to affected regions with two optimizations, and (iv) compares to recomputing the topological order from scratch after every batch. Provide asymptotics in n, m, B?

Scenario: A real-time stream of integers in [0, M-1], arriving in batches of size B. After each batch, output the estimated number of distinct values seen so far. Propose a HyperLogLog-based approach, specify the register count p, how updates are computed, and how the estimator error scales with m. Compare to exact counting requiring O(M) memory. Provide a small numerical example (M=1e6, p=12, B=1000) and show the estimate?

You receive a real-time stream of product IDs (strings) from user activity, arriving in batches of size B. After each batch, output the current approximate number of distinct IDs seen so far. Propose an online algorithm using HyperLogLog with m registers. Specify per-element update time, memory usage, and error guarantees (relative error ε with probability at least 1−δ). Compare to exact counting requiring O(U) memory, where U is the number of unique IDs seen so far. Include a concrete small example?

You receive a real-time stream of integers in [0, M-1], arriving in batches of size B. After each batch, identify the approximate mode (most frequent value) seen so far using only O(k) memory. Propose a Misra-Gries style algorithm with k-1 counters, explain update time per element, per-batch cost, and how to bound the error on the mode frequency; include a small example?

Edge insertions in DAGs with online batches: G=(V,E) starts with no edges. Edges arrive in batches of size B; each batch preserves acyclicity (no cycles). After each batch, determine the length of the longest path (in edges) from any source to any sink. Propose a practical incremental data structure that (i) preprocesses in O(n+m), (ii) updates amortized to O(B log n), (iii) answers in O(1), (iv) uses O(n+m) space, (v) two optimizations, and (vi) a comparison to rebuilding a DP on a topological order after every batch. Provide asymptotics in n, m, B?

Scenario: a real-time analytics service ingests integers in [1..U] in batches of size B every second, maintaining a sliding window of the last W events. After each batch, report the current top-1 value and its frequency within the window. Propose a data structure and an amortized update analysis that (i) handles B inserts and expiry of up to B oldest items, (ii) achieves update cost O(log M) per operation where M is distinct values in the window, (iii) allows top-1 query in O(1) or O(log M), (iv) uses near O(W) memory. Compare to rebuilding frequencies from scratch after each batch, and discuss worst-case scenarios?

You receive a real-time stream of integers in [0, M-1] in batches of size B. After each batch, you must report the top-2 most frequent values observed in the last N elements (a sliding window). Propose a simple online approach with a bounded memory footprint (O(k) counters). Explain how you handle window slides, per-element cost, and provide an error bound and a small worked example?

You're receiving a real-time stream of hashed user IDs in [0, M-1], arriving in batches of size B. After each batch, output the Shannon entropy estimate of the distribution using a fixed K-bin histogram (hash(x) mod K). Propose a streaming method to maintain counts per bucket, analyze per-element update cost, per-batch entropy compute cost, and memory usage O(K). Discuss hashing collisions and bias vs true entropy, and provide a small numerical example with K=4, B=5?

You're given a real-time stream of user IDs (strings) arriving in batches of size B. After each batch, you must report whether any user ID has appeared more than r times within the last W elements (sliding window). Propose a practical online algorithm that uses fixed memory to maintain frequencies in the window and determine if the threshold is crossed. Describe data structures (e.g., a circular buffer plus a hashmap), update cost per element, per batch, memory usage, and how to pick W, r, B. Include a concrete small example?

You receive a real-time stream of integers in [0, M-1], arriving in batches of size B. After each batch, output the current estimate of the number of distinct values seen so far. Propose a bounded-memory approach suitable for beginners (e.g., HyperLogLog with a small number of registers). Specify per-element update time, memory usage, and the expected relative error as a function of the number of registers. Compare to exact counting requiring O(N) memory and full history?

Maintain a dynamic MST for an undirected graph under online batches of B edge insertions. After each batch output the total weight of the MST. Propose a practical data structure using a forest-maintenance technique (e.g., Link-Cut Trees) that (i) preprocesses efficiently, (ii) updates amortized per batch, (iii) reports MST weight after each batch in O(1), (iv) uses near-linear space, (v) include two optimizations, and (vi) compare to rebuilding MST from scratch after every batch? Provide asymptotics in n, m, B?

Online paging with batched access: cache size C, batch size B; before serving each batch you may inspect the batch and decide evictions/prefetches only within that batch. Propose a strategy with amortized O(1) misses per request, prove competitive ratio against offline optimum, and discuss practical data structures?

In a streaming setting, characters arrive in batches of size B. You must maintain the exact number of distinct substrings observed so far using a suffix automaton. Describe an incremental SAM update for each appended character, prove the amortized O(1) per character, and explain memory/time bounds for n total characters. Provide asymptotics in n and sigma?

In a real-time telemetry pipeline, integers in [0, M-1] arrive in batches of size B. After each batch, output the running mean and running standard deviation of all values seen so far using bounded memory. Propose a streaming approach (e.g., Welford’s online updates for both mean and variance), specify per-element update time, constant memory, precision guarantees, and compare against recomputing from scratch which would require O(N) memory?

You maintain an undirected graph G=(V,E) with n nodes; edges arrive in batches of size B (no deletions). After each batch, count the number of unordered pairs {u,v} with dist(u,v) ≤ 2. Propose a practical incremental data structure that uses near-linear space and supports updates in amortized time O(B * T) with a tunable threshold T, plus two optimizations (high-degree handling and lazy rebuild). Provide asymptotics in terms of n, m, B, and T?

In a stream of user IDs arriving in batches of size B, after each batch output the approximate number of distinct IDs seen so far using a HyperLogLog sketch. Specify per-element update, memory m registers, recommended m for 1% relative error, and the formal error guarantees (relative std error ~1.04/√m). Compare to exact counting requiring O(N) space?

You maintain an array a[1..n] of non-negative integers. Updates arrive in batches of size B; each update is either set a[i] = v or remove i (set to undefined). After each batch, output the number of unordered pairs (i<j) with (a[i] + a[j]) mod D == 0 for a fixed D. Propose a data structure to maintain this count with amortized O(B) per batch, and compare to recomputing from scratch. Provide asymptotics in n, B, D?

You receive a real-time stream of integers in [0, M-1], arriving in batches of size B. After each batch, output the sum of the K largest values seen so far (counting duplicates). Propose a streaming solution with bounded memory: maintain a min-heap of size K and a running sum. Provide per-element update, batch time, and memory usage O(K), and compare to the exact method that would require storing all past values (O(N) memory). Include asymptotics in N, K, B?

You receive a real-time stream of integers in [0, M-1], arriving in batches of size B. After each batch, output the current approximate number of distinct values seen so far. Propose a HyperLogLog-based solution with m = 2^p registers; specify per-element update, memory usage, and error guarantees, and compare to an exact approach that stores counts for all M values. Include a short example and guidance on choosing p for a target relative error?

Maintain a multiset of integers; batches of B elements are inserted (no deletions). After each batch, output the exact median of all elements. Propose a practical data structure to support (i) inserting B items, (ii) median query in O(1) or O(log n), (iii) near-linear space, (iv) cache-friendly updates. Give amortized per-batch time as a function of n and B, describe two optimizations, and compare to rebuilding a sorted array after each batch?

Scenario: In a chat platform like Discord, users are nodes in an undirected graph; friendships form edges. Edges can be added or removed in online batches of size B. After each batch, maintain the number of connected components. Propose a hybrid data structure that (i) preprocesses efficiently, (ii) updates amortized per batch, (iii) yields correct component count after each batch, (iv) uses near-linear space, (v) includes two optimizations and a threshold-based rebuild, and (vi) compares to recomputing from scratch after every batch. Provide asymptotics in n, m, B, with a recommended batch interval?

Streaming question: events arrive in batches of size B, each with (t, c). Maintain D = number of distinct categories in the sliding window of width W time units (last W). After each batch, output D. Propose a concrete data structure (queues + hashmap) and show amortized update cost O(B), O(1) query, and near-linear memory. Include two optimizations and compare to recomputing D from scratch after each batch. Give asymptotics in terms of W, B, and the number of active categories?

You're given a real-time stream of integers in [0, M-1], arriving in batches of size B. After each batch, compute an approximate Shannon entropy of the distribution of values seen so far using bounded memory. Propose a streaming sketch (for example Count-Min for frequencies with a plug-in entropy estimator) and specify per-element update time, memory, and error guarantees (ε, δ). Explain parameter choice and how it compares to exact entropy requiring O(M) memory. Include a small worked example?

Design a streaming top-k maintenance for batch-inserted keys: maintain an approximate top-k most frequent keys seen so far using a Count-Min Sketch plus a bounded top-k structure. After each batch of B inserts, report the current top-k with error guarantees. Provide amortized update cost, memory, and a comparison to recomputing from scratch?

Dynamic directed graph with n nodes. Edges insert in online batches of size B (no deletions). After each batch, decide if there exists a path from S to T with length at most L. Propose a practical incremental index to solve this: (i) one-time near-linear preprocess, (ii) amortized per-batch updates, (iii) O(1) query time, (iv) near-linear space, (v) two optimizations, and (vi) a fair comparison to rebuilding shortest paths after each batch. Provide asymptotics in n, m, B, L?

Scenario: In a weighted directed graph with nonnegative weights, you must maintain approximate betweenness centrality for all nodes under batches of edge insertions of size B. Propose a concrete, implementable scheme that (i) initializes estimates, (ii) updates after each batch with amortized cost, (iii) bounds memory, and (iv) provides guaranteed error bounds ε. Include two practical optimizations and compare to re-running Brandes' algorithm after every batch?

Design a data structure to maintain the MST weight of an undirected weighted graph as edges arrive in batches of B. After each batch, output the current MST total weight. Propose a practical incremental MST maintenance approach (near-linear space) that (i) preprocesses quickly, (ii) updates amortized per edge, (iii) exposes MST weight in O(1), (iv) uses near-linear space, (v) includes two optimizations, and (vi) compares to rebuilding the MST after every batch. Provide asymptotics in n = |V|, m = total edges so far, B?

You have a stream of axis-aligned rectangles inserted online in batches of size B; after each batch, compute the area of the union of all rectangles seen so far. Propose a practical data structure and an amortized analysis, including preprocessing, memory usage, two optimizations, and a comparison to recomputing the union area from scratch after every batch. Provide asymptotics in terms of n total rectangles, B batch size, and the number of distinct y-values U?

You have an n x n binary matrix. Online batches of B updates set a cell to 0 or 1. After each batch, output the number of 2x2 submatrices consisting of all ones. Propose a data structure to maintain this count with amortized O(B) per batch, including preprocessing, memory bounds, and a comparison to recomputing from scratch?

You have a text T of length n. Process updates in batches of B substitutions (set T[i] = c). After each batch, report the number of occurrences of a fixed pattern P of length m in T. Design a practical incremental data structure that (i) preprocesses in O(n), (ii) updates in amortized O(B log n) time, (iii) answers counts in O(1), (iv) uses near-linear space, (v) includes two optimizations, and (vi) compares to rebuilding with a full scan after every batch. Provide asymptotics in terms of n, m, B?

You maintain an array a[1..n] of integers. Updates arrive online in batches of size B; each update is either i -> v or delete i (set to undefined). After each batch, count the number of index triples (i<j<k) such that a[i], a[j], a[k] form an arithmetic progression (a[i] + a[k] = 2*a[j]). Propose a practical data structure and amortized analysis that achieves a per-batch bound, including preprocessing and memory bounds. Provide asymptotics in n and B?

You process a latency stream of integers in [0, M-1], batches of B, and must output the 95th percentile of the last W samples (sliding window) after each batch. Propose a simple fixed-bin histogram with S buckets plus a circular buffer of size W to support O(1) per-element updates and O(S) query to estimate P95, including how to map values to buckets, how to pick S, and error guarantees vs exact window recomputation?

You receive a real-time stream of integers in [0, M-1], arriving in batches of size B. After each batch, output the approximate median using the P^2 online quantile estimator (five markers). Describe per-element update steps, implement details, and derive Big-O time and memory. Discuss how error behaves with respect to distribution and batch size, and compare to maintaining a full sorted buffer of size N for exact median?

You have a fixed directed graph with n nodes and a source S. In each batch, B nodes toggle between active and inactive. After every batch, output the number of nodes reachable from S using only active nodes. Propose a practical incremental algorithm with amortized guarantees, a lazy invalidation scheme, and a periodic full rebuild plan; compare to recomputing via DFS from scratch after every batch?

Online graph growth with cycles: n nodes, edges added in batches of B; after each batch decide if the graph remains acyclic and, if a cycle is formed, return one witness cycle. Propose a data structure and amortized update strategy that (i) maintains a topological order, (ii) checks reachability efficiently to detect cycles, (iii) reports a witness path, (iv) uses near-linear space, (v) includes two optimizations, and (vi) compares to recomputing from scratch after every batch?

Data stream of API keys arrives in batches of size B. Maintain the exact top-k most frequent keys seen so far and report after each batch. Distinct keys up to N. Propose a data structure and an amortized analysis that (i) supports increments, (ii) uses O(D) memory with D ≤ N, (iii) updates in O(B log k) amortized per batch, (iv) reports top-k in O(k) after each batch, (v) includes two optimizations, and (vi) compares to rebuilding top-k from scratch. Provide asymptotics in N, k, B, D?

You maintain an undirected graph with n vertices; edges arrive online in batches of B (no deletions). After each batch, report the total number of length-2 paths (a, b, c) with a != c and edges (a,b) and (b,c). Propose an incremental data structure and amortized analysis; compare to recomputing from scratch after every batch?

You manage N tasks with dynamic priorities. In each batch of B updates, you may insert a new task with priority p or adjust an existing task's priority by delta. After every batch, return the IDs of the top-k tasks by priority. Propose a practical data structure that (i) preprocesses in O(N), (ii) updates amortized O(B log S) with S ≈ sqrt(N), (iii) answers top-k in O(k log (N/S)), (iv) uses near-linear space, (v) two optimizations, (vi) compares to re-sorting after every batch. Provide asymptotics in N, B, k?

You are given a real-time stream of API calls, each tagged with an endpoint from 0..M-1. After each batch of B events, report all endpoints whose total count since start exceeds a threshold T, using at most K counters. Propose a Space-Saving style algorithm to maintain candidate endpoints, describe update rules per event, batch extraction, and derive (or state) per-event update time, memory, and accuracy guarantees. Include a small concrete example?

You process a real-time stream of user IDs arriving in batches. After each batch, output the approximate number of unique users seen so far. Propose a HyperLogLog-based solution with m registers; detail per-id updates, memory footprint, and the expected error (≈1.04/√m), plus how to pick m given a target error. Compare to exact distinct counting using a hash-set and its memory. Include a brief numeric example with m=128?

Describe maintaining the number of distinct substrings of a string S that grows by appending batches of B characters. Propose a suffix-automaton based solution, give amortized update time per batch, space, and how to report the current count in O(1). Include two optimizations and compare to rebuilding after each batch?

You store a multiset S of integers. Updates arrive in batches of size B; each update is either insert x or delete x (guaranteed to exist for deletion). After each batch, determine whether there exists a pair of elements with difference exactly K. Propose a data structure that (i) initializes in O(N), (ii) processes each batch in amortized O(B), (iii) answers in O(1) whether such a pair exists, (iv) uses near-linear space, (v) two optimizations, and (vi) compares to re-scanning the whole set after every batch. Provide asymptotics in N, B, K?

You receive a real-time stream of strings (user IDs) in batches of size B. After each batch, output the estimated number of distinct IDs seen so far with a relative error ≤ ε using a fixed-memory sketch. Propose a HyperLogLog-based approach: choose number of registers m, hash function, how to update per element, how to compute the estimate, and how to merge sketches if needed. Analyze per-element update time, per-batch query time, and memory usage. Include a small example?

Telemetry IDs stream: IDs arrive in batches of size B. You must estimate the total number of distinct IDs seen so far with a fixed memory budget. Propose a HyperLogLog variant with m registers; specify per-element update, expected error as a function of m, and memory usage. Provide concrete values for m=1024 and m=2048, and discuss how to merge sketches across devices?

Maintain a real-time timestamp histogram: N existing events with timestamps in [0, T). Updates arrive in batches of B; each update is either insert t or delete t (t may repeat; deletions guaranteed to exist). After each batch, determine if any bucket of width W contains at least M events. Propose a data structure that (i) preprocesses in O(N), (ii) handles each batch in O(B log S) with S = ceil(T/W), (iii) answers in O(1) whether such a bucket exists, (iv) uses near-linear space, (v) provides two optimizations, and (vi) compares to re-scanning after every batch. Provide asymptotics in N, B, M, W, T?

Scenario: a real-time log stream grows only by appending batches of B characters to a string S. After each batch, determine for a fixed set of patterns {p1,...,pm} whether each occurs in S and report the earliest index of its first occurrence. Design a data structure and amortized update strategy, plus two optimizations, and compare to rebuilding suffix structures after every batch?

You are receiving a stream of 2D points representing GPS coordinates projected to a plane. The points arrive in batches of size B (no deletions). After each batch, compute the area of the convex hull of all points seen so far. Propose a practical data structure and update strategy that (i) preprocesses efficiently, (ii) updates amortized per batch, (iii) yields hull area in O(1) or O(log h), (iv) uses near-linear space, (v) includes two optimizations, and (vi) demonstrates how this compares to rebuilding the hull from scratch after every batch. Provide asymptotics in terms of n (total points) and B?

You are receiving a real-time stream of integers in [0, M-1], arriving in batches of size B. After each batch, output an unbiased estimate of the total sum of all values seen so far. Propose a bounded-memory approach and specify: per-element update time, memory usage, and how to bound the relative error (epsilon) for the sum estimate as a function of the reservoir size S and confidence delta. Include a short derivation and a small worked example?

Streaming motif counting: edges arrive in batches of B in a growing graph G with n nodes; after each batch, count exactly the occurrences of a fixed small pattern P (e.g., a 4-node motif) as a subgraph. Propose a streaming algorithm that (i) preprocesses once, (ii) updates per batch in O(B·poly(p)) time, (iii) reports the total count in O(1) per batch, (iv) uses near-linear space, (v) includes two optimizations, and (vi) compares to recomputing from scratch after every batch. Provide asymptotics in n,m,p,B?

You receive a real-time stream of user IDs as integers in [0, M-1], arriving in batches of size B. After each batch, estimate the total number of distinct IDs seen so far under a fixed memory budget of K registers. Propose a simple online unique-counting sketch (HyperLogLog‑inspired) with a small number of registers, describe per-element updates and how the batch estimate is computed, and analyze update time, memory, and error guarantees?

Scenario: You maintain N time-intervals [s_i, e_i) on a discrete timeline 0..P-1, representing user-active windows. Updates arrive in batches of B that change either s_i by ds or e_i by de, always preserving s_i < e_i. After each batch, determine if there exists a time t with at least K overlapping intervals. Propose a data structure and an amortized update strategy with: (i) preprocessing in O(N+P), (ii) batch updates in O(B log P), (iii) query in O(1), (iv) near-linear space, (v) two optimizations, (vi) a comparison to recomputing overlaps from scratch. Provide asymptotics in N, B, P, K?

Scenario: a real-time chat app ingests user IDs in batches of B; after each batch, estimate the number of unique users seen so far under a memory budget of K bytes. Design a HyperLogLog based solution: choose m registers from K, specify hash function, per-element update (leading-zero count), how to compute cardinality, and the expected relative error ~1.04/√m. Explain how to merge sketches across shards and provide a tiny numeric example with small m?

Design and analyze a streaming sliding-window problem: a real-time system emits error codes as integers in [0, M-1] in batches of size B. Maintain a moving window of the last W events. After each batch, output the top-3 most frequent error codes within the window. Propose a simple online approach with O(1) per-element updates (amortized) and O(W) memory; explain accuracy and trade-offs, and compare to a baseline that recomputes frequencies from scratch each batch?

You are ingesting a real-time stream of user IDs in the range [0, M-1], arriving in batches of size B. After each batch, estimate the number of distinct IDs seen so far within a fixed memory budget using a HyperLogLog sketch with m registers. Describe how to configure the sketch, per-element updates, merge behavior, and how the error scales with m and B. Include a small numeric example with M=1e6, m=128, B=1000?

Maintain a fixed-size window: a stream of integers, window size W. In each batch of B new elements, append them and advance the window by B positions (dropping the oldest B elements). After every batch, report the number of distinct values currently in the window. Propose a data structure with: (i) preprocessing in O(W), (ii) amortized updates in O(B), (iii) O(1) query for the distinct count, (iv) near-linear space, (v) two optimizations, and (vi) a comparison to recomputing from scratch after every batch. Provide asymptotics in W and B?

Advanced complexity-analysis: you maintain a rolling index for a text that only grows by appending blocks of size B. After each batch you rebuild a perfect hash mapping block IDs to their start offsets, costing O(n) where n is total characters so far. How do you derive the amortized cost per appended character and per block lookup over N characters, and how does changing B affect the trade-offs and cache behavior?

Imagine a live stream of user_id values (0..1e9) arriving in batches of size B. With a fixed memory budget of K bytes, after each batch, estimate the total number of distinct user_ids seen so far. Propose a practical approach, justify its memory-time trade-offs, state the expected relative error, and explain how to choose parameters given K and B. Include a small numeric example?

Design an incremental suffix array maintenance strategy for a string S that only grows by appending blocks of size B. After each batch, update the suffix array rather than rebuilding from scratch. Assume SA updates cost O(B log n) per batch, where n is current length, and you can store O(n) memory. Derive the amortized cost per appended character and per batch over N total characters, discuss the impact of B on cache locality, and compare to rebuilding SA after every batch?

You implement a dynamic array that grows by doubling its capacity when full. Each insertion costs O(1) plus O(n) to copy on resize. After N appends starting from capacity 1, what is the amortized cost per append? Show the derivation and note how a 1.5x growth factor would change the result; discuss cache implications?

You maintain a dynamic collection of closed intervals on [0, T). Updates arrive in batches of B; each update is either add [l, r) or delete a previously added interval [l, r). After each batch, decide whether the union of all intervals equals [0, T] (i.e., full coverage). Propose a data structure that (i) preprocesses in O(T), (ii) handles each batch in O(B log N) amortized, (iii) answers in O(1) whether full coverage holds, (iv) uses near-linear space, (v) include two optimizations, (vi) compare to recomputing coverage after every batch. Provide asymptotics in T, B, N?

You process a stream of integers arriving in batches of size B. The window is fixed at size N. After each batch you append the B values and drop the oldest B values to keep N. After each batch determine if there exists a pair in the window with difference exactly K. Propose a data structure with (i) O(N) initialization, (ii) amortized O(B) updates, (iii) O(1) query, (iv) near-linear space, (v) two optimizations, (vi) a comparison to re-scanning. Provide asymptotics in N, B, K?

Scenario: An append-only log uses an LSM-tree with levels growing by factor F. Writes arrive in blocks, and a background compaction runs after a batch of T inserted elements, sweeping roughly N elements at that moment. Derive the amortized write cost per element and the read amplification, as functions of N, T, and F. How would you pick T and block size to maximize throughput on real hardware while keeping cache misses low?

Streaming quantiles with batched inserts: a text stream appends B elements per batch. Maintain a mergeable quantile sketch to report the current median within error ε after each batch. Derive amortized per-element update cost and per-query cost as functions of N, B, ε, and sketch parameters; discuss cache behavior and compare to rebuilding exact order statistics after every batch?

Maintain exact single-source shortest paths from a fixed hub h under online edge insertions (batches). Propose a practical scheme that (i) initializes with Dijkstra, (ii) after each batch re-relaxes only affected nodes using a min-heap, (iii) bounds memory, and (iv) gives amortized update time. Include two optimizations and compare to rerunning Dijkstra after every batch. Provide asymptotics in n, m, B?

Maintain N numbers in a multiset. In each batch of B updates, you either insert x or delete x (guaranteed to exist). After each batch, determine whether the median of the multiset is at least T. Propose a practical data structure that (i) preprocesses in O(N log N) or better, (ii) handles each batch in amortized O(B log N), (iii) answers in O(1) whether median >= T, (iv) uses near-linear space, (v) two optimizations, and (vi) compares to re-sorting after every batch. Provide asymptotics in N, B?

You manage a directed graph with N nodes representing user interactions. Edges arrive in batches of size B; after each batch, determine whether the graph contains a directed cycle. Propose a practical data structure to maintain dynamic reachability that (i) preprocesses in O(N+M), (ii) updates amortized O(B log N) per batch, (iii) answers in O(1) whether a cycle exists, (iv) uses near-linear space, (v) two optimizations, and (vi) compares to recomputing from scratch after every batch. Provide asymptotics in N, M, B?

You implement a dynamic log data structure that stores appended records in fixed-size blocks of B entries, linked as a list of blocks. After each batch of B appends, you allocate a new block if needed. Analyze the amortized cost per appended item and per random access to the i-th item, in terms of B and number of blocks, and compare to a traditional contiguous array with doubling. How does B affect cache locality and latency? Include a concrete numeric example with B=1024 and N=10000?

In a data structure storing n keys, arrivals happen only in batches of size B. You need insert and point-lookup operations. Strategy A: insert each key with standard rebalancing (O(log n) per insert, O(log n) per lookup). Strategy B: after every batch, rebuild into a perfectly balanced B-ary tree (height O(log_B n)). Derive the amortized cost per insert and per lookup for both strategies, discuss cache effects, and give asymptotics in terms of n and B?

You have a stream of keys arriving in batches of size B, appended to an unbounded log. You must maintain the exact top-k most frequent keys over all seen items. After each batch, propose a data structure and the amortized update costs that achieve O(B log k) per batch and O(k) retrieval, with near-linear memory. Compare to recounting from scratch after every batch. Express asymptotics in terms of n total items, k, and B?

You have an undirected graph with N nodes. Edges toggle in batches of size B: each update flips the presence of an edge (u,v). After every batch, determine if the graph remains bipartite. Propose a data structure and amortized analysis that preprocesses in O(N+M), processes each batch in about O(B α(N)) time, and answers in O(1) per batch, with near-linear space. Explain how the choice of B affects time and memory?

You maintain a DAG with n nodes and m edges. Edges are updated in batches of size B (each update is insert u->v or delete u->v; deletions guaranteed to exist). After every batch, decide whether the graph contains a cycle; if yes, output any one cycle. Propose a data structure achieving preprocessing O(n+m), amortized per batch O(B log n) for updates, and O(1) cycle-availability queries with near-linear space; include two concrete optimizations and compare to rebuilding a topological order after each batch. Provide asymptotics in n, m, B?

You manage a dynamic undirected graph with N nodes and M potential edges. Edges are toggled in batches of size B (insert or delete; deletions guaranteed to exist). After each batch, determine whether the graph contains at least one triangle (3-cycle). Propose a practical data structure that (i) initializes in O(N+M), (ii) updates in amortized O(B sqrt M) using a heavy/light degree partition and bitsets, (iii) answers existence in O(1), (iv) uses near-linear space, (v) two optimizations, and (vi) compares to recomputing from scratch. Provide asymptotics in N, M, B?

Scenario: an append-only event stream arrives in batches of B events, each event labeled with a type from a large domain U. Design a data structure that, after each batch, returns the current top-k most frequent types with exact counts for those top-k. The structure must support O(B) batch processing, O(1) amortized per-event updates, near O(k log U) per-batch top-k retrieval, and O(U) space. Explain the combined use of a Space-Saving sketch to prune candidates and a per-batch exact consolidation to compute exact counts for the current top-k. Provide asymptotics in terms of n total events, U, B, and k, and discuss cache behavior as B varies?

You're building a streaming analytics store: data arrives in batches of size B and is appended to a log of N blocks. After each batch, design a cache-friendly data structure that (i) updates in O(1) amortized per batch, (ii) answers a fixed set of k range-sum queries over the last W blocks in O(1) time, (iii) supports membership checks for any of m query keys, and (iv) uses near-linear space in N. Derive amortized costs as functions of N, B, W, k, m, and discuss cache-friendly block layout and when constant factors dominate?

External memory indexing: Log grows by appending blocks of size B to disk. An on-disk index maps block IDs to file offsets. After each batch you may skip or perform a bulk merge into a B-tree-like index. Derive amortized I/O costs per appended character and per batch lookup after N total characters, in terms of M (disk block size), B, and N. Compare append-only vs batched merge, and give practical B choices for cache performance?

You receive a real-time stream of integers in [0, M-1], arriving in batches of size B. After each batch, estimate the 85th percentile of all values seen so far using a fixed-memory sliding histogram with K buckets. Every R batches you rebuild the histogram boundaries to sharpen the tail. Describe the data structure, per-element update time, per-batch query time, memory usage, and how R affects accuracy and performance. Include a small numeric example to illustrate?

You receive a stream of product_id in [0, M-1], arriving in batches of size B. After each batch, return the current top-3 products by total count seen so far, but you cannot store per-product counts for all M values. Propose a hybrid approach using a Count-Min Sketch to estimate counts and a tiny heap to keep the current top-3. Analyze per-batch update time, memory usage, and how to bound the probability that the actual top-3 equals the reported top-3; specify choices for w and d?

Design a Bloom-filter based solution to detect whether a string has already appeared in a real-time stream. Each batch contains B strings; the system has a fixed memory budget M bits and uses k hash functions. After each batch, you must answer hasSeen(s) for the incoming string s and report per-insert and per-query costs. How do you pick M and k for a target false positive rate p given expected unique items n? Provide a concrete numeric example with n=100000, M=2^24 bits, k=7 and compute p, and discuss trade-offs with batch size B?

Scenario: A real-time analytics service ingests event messages with a 32-bit integer key. Events arrive in batches of size B every second, and the system must report the number of distinct keys seen so far (cardinality) with a configurable error ε. Propose a practical streaming algorithm and data structure (no deletions) to maintain an ε-approximate cardinality. After each batch, specify (i) per-element insertion time and total batch time, (ii) space usage, (iii) query time for the current estimate, (iv) two optimizations, and (v) how this compares to re-scanning all seen events after every batch. Use asymptotics in n (seen events), B, and ε?

You maintain N items with non‑negative weights w[i]. Updates arrive in batches of size B; each update is (i, delta) meaning w[i] += delta or w[i] -= delta. After each batch, determine whether two distinct indices i != j exist with w[i] + w[j] >= T. Propose a data structure that (i) preprocesses in O(N), (ii) handles each batch in amortized O(B log N), (iii) answers in O(1) whether such a pair exists, (iv) uses near-linear space, (v) provide two optimizations, and (vi) compare to recomputing from scratch after every batch. Provide asymptotics in N, B, T?

Dynamic bipartiteness under batch edge updates: You maintain an undirected graph with N nodes and M edges. Edges are inserted or deleted in batches of size B. After each batch, determine whether the current graph is bipartite. Propose a data structure that preprocesses in O(N+M), handles each batch in amortized O(B log N), and answers bipartiteness in O(1), with near-linear space. Include two optimizations and compare to rebuilding from scratch after each batch. Provide asymptotics in N, M, B?

Design a dynamic (1+ε)-spanner for an undirected weighted graph under online edge insertions in batches of size B. Build a (k,ε)-spanner with O(n^{1+1/k}) edges. After each batch, update only edges that improve distances beyond ε; amortized O(B log n). Query dist via the spanner in O(1). Memory O(n^{1+1/k}). Optimizations: lazy rebuild; reuse tight edges. Compare to rebuilding: faster updates; worst-case near O(n^{1+1/k}) per batch?

Scenario: a streaming API records request latency every second. Maintain the moving median of the most recently observed W latency samples (W up to 100000). Design a data structure that supports append(new_latency), evict_oldest(), and get_median() efficiently. Explain the balancing invariants, per-operation costs, space, and how you handle duplicates and lazy deletions to keep the median correct?

You receive latency samples in blocks of B integers in [0, 1e6). After each batch, determine whether the current 95th percentile latency over all samples seen so far exceeds a threshold T. Propose two practical solutions: (A) a fixed-bin histogram with K buckets, updated in O(B) per batch, (B) an online quantile sketch (GK or KLL) with O(1) per item and fixed memory. Provide the amortized costs, memory usage, and a simple break-even example (B=1000, K=256, m=256)?

Maintain a DAG with N nodes and M edges. Updates arrive in batches of B (edge insertions or deletions). After each batch, determine if a cycle exists. Propose a practical data structure and amortized analysis achieving (i) preprocessing O(N+M), (ii) batch updates amortized O(B log N), (iii) cycle query O(1), (iv) near-linear space, (v) two optimizations, and (vi) a comparison to rebuilding a full topological order after every batch. Provide asymptotics in N, M, B?

In 2D, a growing set P of points is received strictly by appending batches of B points. You must support: (a) batch insertion of B points, (b) queries whether a given point q lies inside the current convex hull of P in O(log h) time, where h is the hull size, and (c) reporting the hull vertices. Design a practical data structure that maintains the hull with amortized work per batch, derive the asymptotics as n = |P| grows and B varies, provide two optimizations, and compare the performance to rebuilding the hull from scratch after every batch?

You're building a log processor that ingests event IDs in batches of size B and must keep only the IDs from the last W events. After each batch, estimate the number of distinct IDs currently in the window. Propose a simple approach using a Counting Bloom Filter with aging counters to approximate the distinct count; specify m, k, per-id cost, aging cadence, and how to derive an estimate. Compare to an exact approach that stores the last W IDs in a circular buffer plus a hash set. Include a small numeric example?

Maintain a dynamic set P of N 2D points with integer coordinates. Updates arrive in batches of B: insert (x,y) with id or delete by id. After each batch determine whether there exists a pair of points with Chebyshev distance dist∞ <= D. Propose a data structure that (i) initializes in O(N) time, (ii) handles each batch in amortized O(B), (iii) answers in O(1) whether such a pair exists, (iv) uses near-linear space, (v) two optimizations, and (vi) compares to re-scanning after every batch. Provide asymptotics in N, B, D?

Streaming Top-K: Events arrive in batches of size B; each event has a key in [1..U]. After each batch, report the exact current top-k frequent keys and their counts. Propose a data structure that maintains exact counts with amortized O(B log k) updates, uses near-linear space, and supports O(1) retrieval of the top-k after each batch. Include two optimizations and a comparison to re-scan of all events. Provide asymptotics in terms of N, B, k, U?

Scenario: A weighted directed graph with nonnegative weights tracks network latencies. Edges can be inserted or have their weights decreased in online batches of size B. After each batch, you must maintain exact distances from a fixed source S to all nodes. Propose a practical hybrid scheme that combines (i) an incremental update pass limited to affected nodes, (ii) periodic full re-computation every T batches, and (iii) a lazy rebuild trigger when incremental cost exceeds a threshold. Provide initial preprocessing, amortized update time per batch, memory bounds, two optimizations, and a comparison to re-running Dijkstra from scratch after every batch?

You receive a real-time stream of keys from a fixed domain of size M, arriving in batches of size B. After each batch, output the current top-k most frequent keys with estimated counts. Propose a streaming algorithm with bounded memory (e.g., Space-Saving/Frequent Items). State per-element update time, batch time, memory usage, and error guarantees for the reported items. Compare to exact counting requiring O(M) memory. Include a short example and guidance on choosing k for a target error?

You receive a real-time stream of string tags from logs in batches of size B. After each batch, output the approximate top-3 tags by total frequency seen in the last W batches. Propose a data structure and algorithm that supports O(B) per-batch updates, O(log K) top updates, fixed memory, and error guarantees, and compare to an exact approach storing counts for every tag in the last W batches. Include a minimal example and guidance on choosing W, w, d, and decay rate γ?

Maintain a dynamic topological order for a directed graph. Build initial order in O(N+M). For each batch of B updates, apply them; if adding edge u->v breaks the order (pos[u] > pos[v]), run a localized DFS from v in the affected region to see if u is reachable (cycle). If not, reposition v to its correct spot. Deletions cannot create new cycles. Amortized per batch: O(B log N); cycle query O(1); memory near-linear. Optimizations: lazy reorder; trigger full rebuild only when frontier grows?

Scenario: A telemetry stream emits event IDs in [0, M-1] in batches of size B. After each batch, estimate the number of distinct IDs seen in the last R seconds (sliding time window). Propose a compact structure under a fixed memory budget that supports O(B) updates per batch and yields a (1±ε) estimate with high probability. Explain how you bucket time, how expirations are handled, and how the error scales with parameters?

Design a rolling Bloom-filter window for a log stream where keys are appended in blocks of size B and only the last W blocks are kept. After each batch, derive the amortized insertion time for B keys, the query time for membership, memory usage as a function of n = W·B and S, and how the false-positive rate evolves with sliding window size; propose two practical optimizations that maintain correctness without overgrowing memory. Provide asymptotics?

Design and analyze a log-structured key-value store with append-only writes in batches of B records and multi-level compaction across L levels with ratio R (LSM-like). After each batch, derive amortized cost per appended record and per key lookup after N total records, in terms N, B, L, R. Explain how increasing B trades off write amplification, cache locality, and lookup latency, and give a concrete numeric example with N=1e9, R=4, B=1024?

Scenario: A string S is appended only in blocks of size B. After each batch you must maintain a suffix array SA for S and support substring queries in O(1) via an LCP RMQ, while minimizing rebuild work. Propose an incremental SA update strategy touching only affected suffixes, derive amortized costs per appended character and per block lookup in terms of n=|S|, B, and alphabet size σ, and discuss cache implications for small vs large B?

You collect API response times (integers 0-10000) in real time, arriving in batches of size B. After each batch, output the current median of all times seen so far. Propose a simple streaming median solution using two heaps, and derive per-element update time, memory usage, and how batch size B affects amortized cost. Include a small example?

Two-tier index design for an append-only text log: (1) per-block rolling-hash fingerprints to filter candidates for each B-block, and (2) a compact suffix automaton over the last W blocks for existence checks. On batch size B, update fingerprints O(B) and extend automaton amortized O(B). A query p runs in O(|p|) to fingerprint and verify. Optimizations: (a) rebuild every K batches; (b) merge small adjacent blocks into larger super-blocks for cache locality. Amortized per char: O(1); per query: O(|p|). Re-scan: O(n) per batch?

Dynamic bipartiteness under batched edge updates: Given N nodes, a sequence of M undirected edge insertions/deletions that occur in batches of size B, after each batch determine if the current graph is bipartite. Propose a data structure with preprocessing in O(N+M), amortized update cost per batch O(B log M) using a rollbackable DSU and a segment-tree over time; report answer in O(1) per batch. Compare to recomputing from scratch?

A log stream S grows only by appending blocks of size B. You need to answer, after each batch, which of M fixed patterns Pi occur anywhere in S and report the earliest occurrence index when available. Propose a two-layer index: (1) per-block suffix automata rebuilt lazily, (2) a global compact index that aggregates endpos information. Derive amortized costs per appended character and per batch in terms N, B, M, and total pattern length, and explain cache behavior as B changes?

A text S grows only by appending fixed-size blocks of length B. You maintain a suffix automaton for S incrementally, updating it after each batch. To speed queries, you attach a per-block Bloom filter summarizing its substrings. After each batch, given a set of patterns {p1,...,pm}, determine whether each occurs in S efficiently. Derive amortized update cost per appended character and per pattern query, and discuss how B and Bloom filter false positives affect space and cache behavior. Provide asymptotics in n=|S| and m=|{patterns}|?

Scenario: A real-time stream of user IDs arrives in batches of size B. After each batch, report the top-3 most frequent IDs within the sliding window of the last W elements. Propose a concrete, implementable approach using a deque for the window and a hashmap for counts; show update steps per batch, memory usage, and how to handle ties. Compare to recomputing top-3 from scratch after each batch?

A streaming text S is appended only in blocks of size B. After each batch, output the total number of distinct substrings of S. Propose an incremental data structure and algorithm to update this count after appending each block, with provable amortized costs. Derive per-character and per-batch costs, analyze how B affects time and memory, and compare to rebuilding a suffix automaton from scratch after every batch. Provide asymptotics in n=|S|, B, and D?

Scenario: a telemetry pipeline app appends data in fixed-size blocks of length B to a time-series log. After each append, design a data structure that maintains both the sum and the maximum of the last W elements (sliding window) in O(1) amortized update and O(1) query, using O(n) space and near-linear preprocessing. Discuss how B and W influence costs, cache behavior, and worst-case guarantees?

You maintain a binary array b[1..n]. In each batch of B updates, you toggle b[i] for various i. After a batch, determine if there exists a contiguous run of at least length L consisting of 1s. Propose a data structure that (i) preprocesses in O(n), (ii) processes each batch in amortized O(B log n), (iii) answers in O(1) whether such a run exists, (iv) uses near-linear space, (v) two optimizations, and (vi) comparisons to recomputing from scratch after every batch. Provide asymptotics in n, B, L?

In a real-time stream of integers in [0, M-1], arriving in batches of size B, after each batch determine if any value accounts for more than θ of all seen items. Propose a simple streaming heavy-hitter detector using a fixed number H of counters (e.g., Misra-Gries). Analyze per-element update time, per-batch processing cost, memory usage, and false positive/false negative bounds as a function of H, B, M, θ. Include a brief example with numbers?

You process a stream of integers in [0, M-1] arriving in batches of size B. After each batch, report all items whose cumulative count exceeds f*N_seen. Propose a Space-Saving style tracker with k counters: update rules per element, how to extract heavy hitters after a batch, and derive amortized per-element and per-batch costs as N_seen grows. Compare memory and accuracy to a full hash-map counter?

You implement a queue backed by a circular buffer. Start capacity is B. When enqueue would overflow, allocate a new buffer of size current_capacity + B and copy all elements, then swap. Dequeue just moves head. After N enqueues and N dequeues, derive the amortized cost per operation for enqueues as a function of B and N, and comment on dequeues. How does B influence total copies and cache behavior?

You're given an undirected graph with N nodes and M edges, initially arbitrary but with no multi-edges. Updates arrive in batches of size B; each update is either add edge (u,v) or delete edge (u,v) (deletions guaranteed to exist). After each batch, determine whether the graph contains at least one cycle. Propose a data structure and an amortized analysis that (i) preprocesses in O(N+M), (ii) handles each batch in O(B log N) time, (iii) answers in O(1) whether a cycle exists, (iv) uses near-linear space, (v) two optimizations, and (vi) compare to recomputing cycles from scratch after every batch. Provide asymptotics in N, M, B?

You're processing a real-time event stream of user actions, integers in [0, M-1], arriving in batches of size B. After each batch, compute the top-k most frequent values seen within the last W elements (sliding window). Propose a practical approach using a fixed-size Space-Saving sketch with expiration for elements leaving the window, and outline per-element update time, overall batch time, memory usage, and an error guarantee for the top-k results. Include a small concrete example with W=20, k=3, B=5?

You receive a real-time stream of category IDs in [0, M-1], arriving in batches of size B. After each batch, you must report the mode (most frequent category) seen so far, under a fixed memory budget that can store at most K distinct categories. Propose a practical streaming algorithm (or combination of data structures) that guarantees O(1) amortized update per item and analyzes the trade-offs for K, B, and worst-case distributions. Include a brief example?

You have a real-time stream of integers in [0, M-1], arriving in batches of size B. After each batch, return the approximate rank of a fixed value r among all values seen so far. Propose a solution using a fixed-size, d-way hashing histogram (Count-Sketch style) that supports insertions in O(B) time and rank queries in O(d) time, with memory O(d·s). Derive how s and d affect error ε and failure δ, and compare to exact counting requiring O(U) space?

Design a batched suffix-automaton update for an append-only string S that grows in blocks of size B. After each batch, ensure pattern queries remain O(|p|) and amortized per-batch updates are O(B) (or O(B log sigma) with a dynamic map). Explain handling of clones, provide amortized bounds, and discuss optimal B in terms of N and sigma?

You're processing a real-time stream of user IDs (strings) from a web service. After every batch of B events, identify the current top-5 most frequent IDs using a streaming algorithm with O(k) memory and fast per-item updates. Describe how Misra-Gries would be applied, the update cost per event, and the accuracy guarantees for the reported top-5?

Advanced complexity-analysis: A set of m patterns over a fixed alphabet is kept static, while a text S grows only by appending batches of size B. After each batch, report for every pattern whether it occurs in S and the earliest end position. Propose an incremental Aho-Corasick-based structure that rebuilds the automaton every T batches or updates lazily, and derive the amortized costs per appended character and per batch query as functions of n=|S|, m, B, T, and σ. Include two optimizations and compare to rebuilding after every batch?

Maintain N closed intervals [L_i, R_i] on a known integer universe with O(N) endpoints. Updates arrive in batches of B; each update is either add an interval [L, R] with a new ID or remove an existing interval by ID. After each batch, determine the maximum number of overlapping intervals at any point. Propose a data structure that (i) preprocesses in O(N log N), (ii) handles each batch in amortized O(B log N), (iii) answers in O(1) the max overlap, (iv) uses near-linear space, (v) two optimizations, and (vi) compares to reconstructing overlaps from scratch after every batch. Provide asymptotics in N, B?

Maintain a dynamic set P of N points in the plane with integer coordinates. Updates arrive in batches of size B; each update inserts a point (x,y) or deletes an existing one. After each batch, determine whether any pair lies within Euclidean distance <= R. Propose a practical data structure and amortized costs: (i) preprocessing in O(N), (ii) updates in O(B) amortized, (iii) query in O(1), (iv) near-linear space, (v) two optimizations, (vi) a comparison to brute-force recheck after every batch. Provide asymptotics in N, B, R?

You monitor a high-frequency activity stream of userIds in [0, M-1] arriving in batches of size B. After each batch, estimate how many distinct userIds appeared in the last W events (sliding window). Propose a practical online estimator using rotating HyperLogLog sketches: partition the window into K buckets (K = ceil(W/B)) and maintain one HLL per bucket. For a batch, update the corresponding bucket with every userId. For a query, merge the K sketches to estimate distincts. Analyze update time, memory, and error, and compare to a naive O(W)-memory approach?

You receive a real-time stream of product_view events, each with fields product_id and timestamp. In batches of B, keep a sliding window of the last W seconds. After each batch, report the top-K products by view count within that window and explain how the rank of the K-th product can change as new data arrives. Propose a practical data structure to support inserts, time-based evictions, and top-K queries in sublinear time, and derive the amortized cost per event in terms of B, W, and K?

You're maintaining a multiset of N labeled items drawn from U distinct labels. Updates arrive in batches of size B; each update is insert x or delete x (delete x guaranteed to exist). After every batch, determine whether any label occurs at least F times. Propose a data structure that (i) builds in O(N), (ii) processes each batch in amortized O(B), (iii) answers in O(1) whether max frequency >= F, (iv) uses near-linear space, (v) two optimizations, and (vi) compare to rebuilding histogram after every batch. Provide asymptotics in N, B, F, U?

Design an incremental suffix automaton (SAM) that supports appending blocks of size B to a string S, without reprocessing all previous characters. After each batch, answer for a set of patterns {p1,...,pm} whether each occurs in S, and report the earliest end position for each pattern. Derive amortized insertion cost per character, per-pattern query time, and memory usage; analyze how B influences cache behavior and worst-case cloning events; propose two practical optimizations?

Design a two-tier index for an append-only time-series log partitioned into fixed-size blocks of B characters. After every batch of B appended characters, you must be able to answer: give me the start offset for block i in O(1) time. Propose a data structure that keeps Tier-1 in-memory hash for hot blocks and Tier-2 on-disk offset table refreshed from Tier-1 every R batches. Analyze amortized costs: per appended character and per block lookup, in terms of total characters N, batch size B, rebuild frequency R, cache size C, and disk IO cost D. Include optimal guidance for choosing R relative to cache and IO costs?

You receive a real-time stream of integers in [0, M-1], arriving in batches of size B. After each batch, report the set of elements that occur more than phi times the total seen so far. Propose a Misra-Gries heavy-hitters algorithm with parameter k to bound report size; derive per-element update time, memory usage, and error guarantees (phi approximation and potential false positives). Also discuss how to choose k given phi?

You're maintaining a DAG of service dependencies with N nodes. Each batch of B updates adds or removes a single edge (u -> v). After each batch, decide if the graph remains acyclic and can be topologically ordered. Propose a data structure and amortized analysis: (i) preprocessing in O(N+M), (ii) batch updates in O(B log N) amortized, (iii) O(1) cycle-flag queries, (iv) near-linear space, (v) two optimizations, (vi) compare to re-running topological sort after every batch. Provide asymptotics in N, M, B?

You receive a real-time stream of integers in [0, M-1], arriving in batches of size B. After each batch, output the current approximate top-K most frequent values seen so far. Propose a Misra-Gries sketch of size k-1 counters; describe per-element update, batch extraction of top-K, and error guarantees (e.g., any value with freq > N/k will be captured), and compare to exact counting requiring O(M) memory. Include a small example and guidance on choosing k relative to K?

In a directed graph with nonnegative weights, updates arrive in batches of B edge insertions or weight decreases. After each batch, maintain P = { (u,v) | dist(u,v) ≤ D } for a fixed threshold D. Propose a practical scheme that (i) precomputes a compact structure, (ii) updates P after each batch with amortized time, (iii) bounds memory, and (iv) provides two optimizations. Compare to recomputing all-pairs distances up to D after every batch?

You maintain a growing list of N tasks with integer priorities. Operations arrive in batches of size B, appending new tasks. After each batch you must surface the current minimum priority quickly. Compare two schemes: (A) rebuild a heap from scratch after every batch; (B) insert the B new tasks into a single heap. Provide total time and per-operation costs, and derive the breakeven batch size B* in terms of N. Include memory usage considerations?

Scenario: A streaming service receives integers in batches of size B. After each batch, output the median of all values seen so far. Propose a practical scheme that (i) uses two heaps to balance lower/upper halves, (ii) inserts each new value with O(log n) cost, (iii) bounds memory, (iv) offers two optimizations, and (v) compares to recomputing from scratch after every batch. Give asymptotics in terms of n and B?

Scenario: Streaming terms from a document corpus arrive in batches of B. Estimate the number of distinct terms seen so far using a probabilistic counter. Design an implementable plan with initial preprocessing, per-batch updates, memory bounds, two optimizations, and a comparison to exact counting. Include formulas in terms of B, U (distinct terms), and target error ε?

You maintain a weighted undirected graph G=(V,E) with nonnegative weights. Edges arrive online in batches of size B.
