You need to answer s shortest-path queries dist(u_i,v_i) for i=1..s after each batch, within a (1+ε) approximation, reusing work across all pairs. Propose a single shared data structure (i) initialization to support all s pairs, (ii) amortized per-batch update cost when a batch arrives, (iii) per-query time, (iv) memory, (v) two practical optimizations, and (vi) a comparison to rebuilding from scratch per batch. Express asymptotics in n=|V|, m=|E|, s, B, ε?

In a directed graph with N nodes and M edges, edges arrive online in batches of size B. After each batch, estimate, with high probability, the number of nodes reachable from a fixed set S within at most D hops, within a (1±ε) factor. Propose a streaming sampling scheme: (i) pick k random walks of length D starting from S or uniformly; (ii) specify update rules per batch; (iii) derive variance/error bounds and how to set k for a target failure prob; (iv) amortized time and memory; (v) compare to rerunning a bounded-depth multi-source BFS after each batch. Provide asymptotics in n,m,k,B,ε,D?

Scenario: In a weighted undirected graph G=(V,E) with nonnegative weights, edges arrive in online batches of size B. From a fixed root r, maintain a (1+ε)-approximate shortest path tree (SPT) to all nodes after each batch. Propose a practical scheme that (i) initializes the SPT, (ii) updates after a batch with amortized time, (iii) bounds memory, (iv) offers two optimizations, and (v) compares to rebuilding the SPT from scratch after every batch. Provide asymptotics in n=|V|, m=|E|, B, ε?

Scenario: A ride-hailing network graph G=(V,E) with nonnegative weights receives edge insertions in batches of size B. You must maintain an ε-approximation to the top-r eigenvector centrality for all nodes after each batch, with update time sublinear in n. Propose a concrete scheme: (i) initial computation, (ii) update after batch using low-rank ΔA and a few subspace iterations, (iii) how to answer centralities fast, (iv) memory bounds, (v) two optimizations, (vi) comparison to recomputing from scratch after every batch. Express asymptotics in n, m, B, r, ε?

In a directed weighted graph G=(V,E) with nonnegative weights, edges are inserted online in batches of size B. After each batch you must maintain approximate eccentricities ecc(v)=max_u dist(v,u) for all v within a (1+ε) factor. Provide preprocessing, per-batch update time, memory, and a comparison to recomputing all-pairs eccentricities from scratch after each batch. Express asymptotics in n=|V|, m=|E|, k, B, ε?

Scenario: A DAG G=(V,E) with a fixed source S. Each edge e=(u,v) contributes 1 path along that edge; the number of distinct S→v paths is computed by DP over a topological order. Propose a practical hybrid scheme that maintains exact path counts to all v after each batch using (i) an incremental update pass limited to affected nodes, (ii) a periodic full recomputation every T batches, and (iii) a lazy rebuild trigger when incremental cost exceeds a threshold. Include initial preprocessing, amortized update time per batch, memory bounds, two optimizations, and a comparison to re-running the full DP after every batch?

Scenario: A log analytics service processes a high-velocity stream of user IDs and needs the number of unique users in the last W events (sliding window). Provide asymptotics for time and space in terms of N, W, and batch size B, and compare to a full recompute after each batch?

You have n users as undirected nodes. Edges arrive in batches of size B, each batch adding friendships. After each batch, report the number of connected components in the graph. Provide amortized per-edge cost, per-batch cost, and memory in terms of n, m, B, alpha(n). Also discuss when a rebuild might be preferable?

Count inversions in an array of length n. Compare the naive approach O(n^2) with a merge-sort based approach that runs in O(n log n). Explain which inputs favor each, and discuss space usage and stability implications. End with ?

You have an integer array a of length n. You receive online batches of B point updates (set a[i] = v). After each batch you must answer: how many elements in a exceed a fixed threshold T? You receive a real-time stream of integers in [0, M-1], arriving in batches of size B. After each batch, determine whether value x has appeared at least t times so far. Real-time logs: integers in [0, M-1] arrive in batches of size B. After each batch, determine how many distinct values have appeared at least t times in total so far. Dynamic graph: edges are inserted in batches of size B in a weighted directed graph. You receive a stream of integers in [0, M-1] in batches of B. Maintain a sliding window of the most recent N elements. After each batch, report the current number of distinct values in the window. Propose a practical data structure (e.g., hashmap + queue) to support batch inserts, updates, and a correct count, and derive update time, memory, and a comparison to recomputing from scratch?

Maintain a dynamic topological order for a directed graph as edges are inserted in batches of size B. Maintain a directed graph G=(V,E) with nonnegative weights. Edges arrive online in batches of size B (no deletions). Dynamic reachability indexing for DAGs: edges added in batches of size B; after each batch, build a (1+epsilon)-approximate reachability oracle using a dynamic two-hop labeling with k hubs. In a streaming setting, integers arrive in batches of size B; after each batch you must report the k-th smallest value seen so far, with k small (e.g., ≤100). In a real-time event stream, each event has a category in [1..C]. Events arrive in batches of size B. After each batch, return the current top-3 categories by estimated frequency. You process a stream of user IDs arriving in batches of size B. After each batch, determine if the number of distinct IDs seen so far is at least D. You process latency samples of database operations arriving in batches of size B. After each batch, you must report the approximate 50th, 90th, and 99th percentile latency over all seen samples. You manage a live 2D plane with axis-aligned rectangles representing ad slots. Rectangles arrive online in batches of size B; they never disappear. You receive a real-time stream of user IDs in batches of size B; after each batch, estimate the number of distinct IDs seen so far with relative error ε and confidence 1−δ. Given a directed graph G=(V,E) with n=|V|, edges inserted online in batches of size B (no deletions), after each batch determine if G contains a directed cycle. You maintain an undirected graph with n nodes and m edges; edges are inserted in batches of size B (no deletions). Each edge has a weight w. Maintain a growing string S that only accepts batch appends (no deletions). After each batch of B characters, output the total number of distinct substrings of S. You have a dynamic set P of n 2D points added in batches of B. Real-time status code monitoring: codes in 0..M-1 arrive in batches of size B. After each batch, determine if any code has appeared at least t times so far. You're building a real-time analytics dashboard that shows the top-k most frequent event types from a high-volume log stream (e.g., clicks, errors). Each event has a string type. In a DAG with N nodes and M edges, nonnegative edge weights. You maintain shortest-path distances from source S to a fixed set of target nodes {T1,...,Tk}. Implement a dynamic array that starts at capacity 4 and doubles on resize; after inserting N elements, what is the amortized cost per insertion, and how would a 1.5x growth factor change the bound, including cache implications?

You're building a real-time analytics component for a fintech platform. You must maintain the number of distinct values in the most recent W events in a streaming fashion. In a directed graph G=(V,E) with N nodes, M edges and nonnegative weights, a fixed source S, and an SSSP tree T. Dynamic path counting in a DAG: maintain the number of S→T paths of length at most L under online edge insertions and deletions. You maintain a dynamic set of closed intervals on a line. Initially empty. In online batches of B updates, each update adds a new interval [l, r] (l ≤ r). Design a dynamic, multi-source shortest-path maintenance scheme for a directed graph with nonnegative weights. Design a dynamic distance labeling scheme for an undirected weighted graph that supports edge insertions and deletions online. In an undirected weighted graph G=(V,E) with nonnegative weights, design a (1+ε)-approximate distance oracle based on a fixed landmark set L (|L|=k). After each batch, specify: (i) preprocessing time and space to build distances from every landmark, (ii) amortized update time per batch to update the oracle, (iii) query time for dist(u,v), (iv) total memory, (v) two practical optimizations, (vi) a comparison to rebuilding all-pairs distances after each batch. Dynamic 2D convex hull with batched insertions: Points are added to a set P in batches of size B. Maintain a dynamic 2D point set P in the plane. Points are appended in online batches of size B (i -> (x_i,y_i)); never deleted. After each batch, report the area of the convex hull of all points seen so far. Include a late-event policy, per-tenant watermarking, and a runnable sketch with a test plan?

Design a beginner-friendly concurrency exercise: a distributed log-aggregation pipeline. Dozens of services emit logs tagged by service and level. Each service's logs must be consumed in arrival order, while across services processing can be parallel. Implement per-service FIFO buffers feeding a bounded global worker queue. When backlog hits a threshold, degrade by sampling to only ERROR logs, preserving per-service order for kept logs. Explain backpressure, per-service ordering, and a concrete test plan for ordering, degradation, and shutdown?

Design a per-service ordered task scheduler with a bounded global worker pool. Each service's requests must be executed in arrival order, but slow services trigger backpressure via per-service credits. Implement a central arbiter with per-service FIFOs, a global ready-queue, cancellation, and a fast-path for urgent tasks. Provide runnable sketch in Go or Rust and discuss correctness, memory bounds, and failure recovery?

Design a concurrent job queue for an image-processing service: tasks arrive with tenant_id, priority, and deadline; implement a bounded, multi-queue system where workers always pull from the currently highest-priority non-empty tenant queue, but aging prevents any tenant from starving. Include backpressure on the global queue, cross-tenant fairness, and a test plan for liveness under bursty load. Provide concrete structures and trade-offs?

Design a concurrent HTTP request dispatcher for a microservice that calls multiple external hosts with per-host quotas. Producers enqueue requests as (host, path, payload, priority). A fixed-size worker pool processes requests, but must guarantee per-host in-order delivery and respect per-host rate limits using a token bucket. The dispatcher should support dynamic worker resizing at runtime and implement backpressure by delaying or dropping requests when quotas are exhausted. Provide data structures, a runnable sketch, and a test plan?

Design a beginner-friendly concurrency controller for a real-time notification dispatch system: dozens of apps push notification requests for many users; per-user FIFO ordering must be preserved, while the global queue and worker pool handle throughput; include a rate-limited gateway to respect external API limits; implement a degradation path that switches to 'fire-and-forget' for low-priority messages when backlog grows. Describe backpressure, per-user ordering, and a concrete test plan?

Design an intermediate concurrency problem: Build a real-time per-user activity coalescer. Ingest events from N sources, each event has user_id, seq, and payload. A central sequencer ensures in-order dispatch: if seq != expected, buffer until missing seq arrives. Use a bounded work queue; dynamic worker resize by adjusting channel capacity. Backpressure blocks producers when memory grows. Late events policy: drop if seq < last_seen, or re-sequence if within a grace window. Provide runnable sketch and tests?

Design an intermediate concurrency problem: implement a bounded, three-stage replay pipeline for a distributed cache invalidation service. Ingest events from N producers (tenant_id, key, seq, op) into a shared ingress; Stage 1 filters/normalizes; Stage 2 routes per tenant_id to M workers; Stage 3 applies invalidations to a mock cache and emits per-tenant stats. Guarantee per-tenant in-order across all stages under backpressure, support dynamic worker resizing, and define a policy for late/out-of-order events. Provide data structures and a runnable sketch with a test plan?

Design a beginner-friendly concurrency exercise for a chat notification service: dozens of rooms produce events (messages and typing); ensure per-room arrival order via per-room FIFO buffers feeding a bounded global worker queue. Implement a degradation path that coalesces rapid typing events per room when backlog grows and drops non-critical metadata. Explain backpressure, per-room ordering, and provide a test plan for correctness and graceful shutdown?

Design a beginner-friendly concurrency dispatcher for a real-time analytics pipeline ingesting events from 100 sensors. Each sensor's events must be processed in arrival order; events across sensors may be processed in parallel. Use per-sensor FIFO buffers feeding a bounded global worker queue. Add a backlog-triggered degradation path that drops non-critical fields to preserve throughput. Provide concrete test plans and graceful shutdown behavior?

Design a bounded, multi-stage real-time ranking pipeline. N producers emit events as (user_id, item_id, score, ts). Stage 1 normalizes scores per user using a per-user accumulator with fixed memory. Stage 2 maintains a per-user top-K heap in bounded RAM, merged by M workers. Stage 3 periodically flushes global top-K to a sink. Guarantee per-user order and ranking correctness under backpressure and dynamic worker resizing; outline data structures, a runnable sketch, and a test plan?

Design a beginner-friendly concurrency exercise: a distributed event router for an analytics pipeline. Dozens of producers emit events tagged by topic. A central router maintains per-topic FIFO buffers and forwards to a fixed-size worker pool. Ensure per-topic ordering, bounded buffering, and backpressure by delaying incoming events when the global backlog grows, plus graceful producer shutdown and a concrete test plan?

Design an intermediate concurrency problem: implement a three-stage streaming pipeline that guarantees exactly-once per-record processing without external transactions. Ingress: N producers emit (record_id, key, ts, value). Stage1: M stateless transformers; Stage2: K per-key in-order aggregators; Stage3: durable sink. Requirements: bounded buffers with backpressure, dynamic worker resizing, per-key in-order across all stages, and an in-memory dedup/commit buffer to handle replays. Provide data structures, a runnable sketch, and a test plan?

Design a speculative execution layer for a real-time collaborative editor where user actions arrive as a DAG of edits with dependencies. Implement a multithreaded executor that runs independent edits in parallel, defers dependents until prerequisites finish, and detects conflicts on the same position to rollback. Include a bounded replay queue to cap work and a rollback protocol. Provide a runnable sketch in Go or Rust and discuss guarantees?

Design a beginner-friendly concurrency controller for a real-time telemetry ingester: dozens of producers send events tagged by tenant_id and priority (high/low). A bounded global worker pool processes events in parallel across tenants while preserving per-tenant FIFO ordering. When backlog crosses a threshold, implement a preemption mode that drops or coalesces low-priority events and caps per-tenant buffers. Describe backpressure, per-tenant ordering guarantees, and provide a concrete test plan for ordering, backlog behavior, and graceful shutdown?

Design a beginner-friendly concurrency controller for a real-time telemetry pipeline: dozens of microservices emit event records tagged by tenant ID. A bounded global worker pool processes events; per-tenant FIFO buffers preserve arrival order within a tenant while allowing tenants to share workers. When backlog grows, apply a tenant-aware drop policy that preserves newest events for high-traffic tenants and discards oldest for low-traffic tenants. Explain backpressure, per-tenant ordering, and a concrete test plan?

Design a bounded, per-key ordered event dispatcher. Incoming events carry a key (user_id) and payload. The system must preserve per-key FIFO order even as worker pool size changes (scaling up/down). Use a central bounded queue, a set of per-key FIFO queues, and a stable partitioning scheme (consistent hashing) so same key maps to same worker. Implement backpressure to stop producers when in-flight exceeds capacity, and include spill-to-disk (LRU) store for evicted events. Provide runnable sketches in Go or Python?

Design a beginner-friendly concurrency controller for a real-time telemetry pipeline from edge devices to cloud analytics. Each device sends readings that must be processed in device order. A bounded global worker pool processes readings in parallel across devices. Add per-device rate limiting and a global degradation path: when backlog crosses a threshold, switch to sampling mode that processes only every Nth reading per device. Explain backpressure, per-device ordering, and provide a concrete test plan for ordering, degradation behavior, and shutdown?

Design a real-time, multi-tenant event processor where events arrive tagged with tenant_id and event_type. Implement a central router that distributes events to per-tenant FIFO queues backed by a global bounded buffer, with a dynamic worker pool that can rebalance across tenants to maximize throughput. Ensure backpressure, strict per-tenant ordering, and exactly-once processing using per-tenant sequence numbers and a durable, replay-ready log, with cancellation and graceful shutdown?

Design a beginner-friendly concurrency exercise: a multi-tenant serverless scheduler. Tenants (A-D) submit function invocations; a global bounded worker pool executes functions. Each tenant's invocations must be processed in arrival order (per-tenant FIFO), while invocations from different tenants are interleaved for parallelism. Implement per-tenant buffers, global backpressure, and a degradation path: when backlog grows, suspend low-priority tenants and let high-priority ones proceed with a best-effort policy. Provide a concrete test plan for per-tenant ordering, backpressure, and degradation fairness?

Design an in-memory, concurrent stream join operator for two input streams A and B. Each event has a key and a timestamp. Implement a per-key sliding-window equi-join with multiple worker threads that can process different keys in parallel, but guarantee in-order output per key. Bound memory usage with eviction, and apply backpressure when downstream slows. Compare locking vs lock-free implementations and outline testing strategies and failure scenarios?

Design a per-session ordered event dispatcher for a real-time multiplayer game server. Each game session has its own FIFO queue; multiple producers can enqueue events across sessions, and a fixed-size pool of worker threads processes events. Requirements: (1) preserve strict per-session order; (2) allow cross-session work-stealing for load balancing; (3) enforce a global bounded queue with backpressure to producers; (4) support dynamic session creation/destruction with zero deadlock and graceful shutdown; (5) discuss memory reclamation and safety?

Design a bounded, deadline-aware task scheduler for a live image-processing pipeline. Producers enqueue tasks labeled CPU-bound or IO-bound with deadlines; implement a two-tier priority with earliest deadline first and aging to prevent starvation. Use per-worker local queues with work-stealing, and a global backpressure mechanism when backlog grows. Ensure deadlines are respected and test bursts with latency metrics?

Design a beginner-friendly concurrency setup in Go for a real-time notification service where many producers emit payloads that must be delivered to users in per-user order. Implement a global bounded queue and per-user FIFO channels so that each user's messages are processed in order, while a small worker pool handles delivery. Explain how you enforce backpressure, avoid starvation, and test ordering and race conditions?

In a real-time video analytics service, cameras stream frames that must be processed in per-camera order while frames from different cameras can run concurrently. Design a bounded, backpressured dispatch with a central queue and per-camera FIFO queues, plus a small worker pool. Explain ordering, starvation avoidance, and failure handling. Provide a runnable asyncio Python sketch demonstrating enqueue, dispatcher, queues, and graceful shutdown?

Scenario: A telemetry inlet ingests events from numerous IoT devices. Each device’s events must be processed in arrival order, while events from different devices are handled concurrently by a small worker pool. Design a beginner-friendly Go solution using a bounded global queue and per-device FIFO channels to preserve per-device order. Add deduplication for repeated (deviceId,seq) pairs, implement backpressure, and ensure fairness when bursts occur. Provide a runnable sketch and brief testing plan?

In a GPU-accelerated image-processing pipeline, dozens of producers generate work units with different priorities and data dependencies, and a pool of workers dispatch kernels. Design a bounded, multi-producer multi-consumer queue with backpressure that supports per-item priority without starving high-priority tasks. Explain data structures, memory ordering, and how you avoid ABA and deadlocks. Include a runnable minimal sketch (Rust or C++) showing enqueue/dequeue semantics and a basic test strategy with synthetic load?

Design a streaming dataflow for real-time analytics that processes events into fixed 1-second windows. Implement per-window bounded queues, a dynamic worker pool, and a watermark-driven cancellation protocol: late events crossing the watermark cancel the window and abort pending tasks. Guarantee in-window output order and no deadlocks under backpressure. Explain testing strategies and trade-offs?

Design a fault-tolerant, multi-region task queue for a real-time data-enrichment service serving many tenants. Each tenant has a cap and can enqueue interdependent tasks. Propose a bounded, distributed queue with backpressure, delivering at least once while achieving exactly-once processing for idempotent handlers, plus per-tenant ordering and a recovery plan. Include a test strategy?

Design a backpressure-aware streaming engine for real-time analytics: streams partitioned by sensor_id; each partition has a bounded queue and a 5s tumbling window; a watermark advances to emit aggregates; late data goes to a late-path buffer for a grace period; exactly-once via incremental checkpointing of partition offsets and window state; discuss latency-throughput trade-offs and testing strategy?

Design a beginner-friendly concurrency pattern for a bounded multi-producer, multi-consumer router: many producers publish tasks tagged by resource_id into a shared bounded global queue. Implement per-resource FIFO buffers and a small worker pool that processes tasks from those buffers, while guaranteeing per-resource order and fair progress between resources. Explain backpressure, starvation avoidance, and a simple test plan to verify ordering under bursty loads?

You're building a real-time analytics ingestion service for a multi-tenant SaaS platform. Each incoming event carries tenant_id and a local sequence number. You must preserve per-tenant in-order semantics across keys while allowing full parallelism across tenants. Design a bounded, multi-queue scheduler with per-tenant queues, a fixed-size worker pool, and backpressure when buffers saturate. Describe data structures, synchronization approach (locks vs lock-free), deadlock avoidance, and how to achieve exactly-once processing on failure. Provide runnable sketches in Go or Rust and outline a testing plan?

You are building a real-time notification system with a bounded, multi-producer, multi-consumer queue. Producers label tasks as critical or normal. The queue capacity is fixed; producers block when full. A worker pool must fetch tasks in a fair, per type round robin to avoid starvation. Provide a runnable sketch in Go (or Python/Java) and discuss backpressure, cancellation, and testing for latency and task ordering?

In a real-time task processing system, multiple producers enqueue jobs into a global bounded queue with capacity C. A fixed pool of workers consumes jobs. Extend a beginner concurrency pattern to support two priority levels: high and normal. High-priority jobs must be served before normal ones, while preserving FIFO within each priority. Producers should block when the queue is full. Implement backpressure signaling and outline a concrete test plan to verify ordering and backpressure?

Design a beginner-friendly concurrency pattern for a real-time ingest system where producers submit messages tagged by dynamic topics. Each topic must preserve per-topic in-order delivery, while a bounded global queue and a small worker pool process items across topics. Topics can be created or removed at runtime; ensure backpressure signals to producers when quotas are reached and gracefully drain or archive messages on topic removal. Explain test plan for per-topic ordering under churn and for topic lifecycle events?

In a real-time ingestion service, dozens of producers emit per-tenant events into a fixed-size global queue. Implement a bounded, multi-tenant queue that guarantees per-tenant in-order processing and fair sharing while allowing dynamic partition rebalancing without pausing producers. Provide a runnable minimal sketch in Go or Rust showing enqueue/dequeue and a basic test plan for backpressure, ordering, and rebalancing?

In a real-time video channel encoding pipeline with thousands of channels, producers enqueue per-channel tasks into a bounded global queue and per-channel local queues. Design a backpressure-aware, low-latency scheduler (Rust; crossbeam or Tokio) that preserves per-channel order, avoids starvation, and scales to many cores. Include a runnable sketch showing enqueue, worker pull, and backpressure?

Design a bounded, multi-producer, multi-consumer processing system for streaming analytics. Each event has a topic id; events within the same topic must be processed in order, but topics may run in parallel. Implement a dynamic worker pool that can grow/shrink at runtime and rebalance tasks across topics while preserving per-topic order. Include backpressure signaling when the global queue is full, fairness across topics, and a graceful shutdown that drains in-flight items per topic?

In a high-frequency risk-checking pipeline, many trading engines emit per-instrument events that must be processed in instrument-local order by a pool of workers. Design a bounded multi-producer, multi-consumer queue in Rust (Tokio) with per-instrument FIFOs and global backpressure. Include how to register new instruments, graceful shutdown, and a runnable minimal example showing enqueue, dispatch, and exit?

In a high-throughput streaming service, multiple producers publish events across distinct topics to a shared bounded buffer. Design a dispatcher in Rust that routes events to per-topic worker pools using a single ring buffer. Include per-topic offsets, backpressure when full, fair scheduling, and a clean shutdown. Provide a runnable minimal sketch and testing guidance?

In a real-time event ingestion path for a multi-tenant analytics platform, producers publish per-topic events into a bounded global ring buffer. A pool of workers must deliver events in per-topic FIFO order while interleaving topics for throughput; design a bounded, two-level queueing system that guarantees backpressure, avoids starvation, and remains live under bursts. Describe data structures, synchronization (atomics, memory ordering, or locks), failure modes, testing strategy, and show a runnable minimal sketch in C++ that enqueues into a bounded global ring and dispatches per-topic FIFO?

In a live video encoding service, dozens of producers submit encoding jobs tagged by tenant_id to a bounded system. Design a hierarchical, bounded queue with per-tenant queues feeding a global worker pool. Each tenant has a max concurrent jobs quota; the global pool has a total cap. Explain enqueue/dequeue, backpressure propagation, starvation avoidance, and how you would test correctness and latency under burst traffic. Provide a language-agnostic sketch?

You’re building a high-throughput streaming service for financial trades. Multiple producers enqueue trades into a bounded buffer; a small pool of workers applies risk checks and routes trades to downstream systems. Design a concurrency solution that guarantees per-instrument total ordering, backpressure, and fault-tolerance with at-least-once semantics. Provide a runnable sketch in Rust or Java showing enqueue, per-instrument dispatch, and recovery via a durable log?

Design a beginner-friendly concurrent workflow for a video-processing service: hundreds of producers submit video render jobs tagged by videoId. A bounded global queue accepts jobs; ensure per-video in-order processing while keeping a small worker pool. Propose a concrete Go or Python asyncio design that guarantees per-video FIFO, backpressure, and test plan to verify ordering and throughput?

Design a concurrent per-shard event processor for a real-time analytics pipeline: events arrive from multiple producers into N shards, each with a bounded queue and dedicated workers. Implement backpressure to prevent overflow, fairness across shards, and strict per-shard ordering. How would you verify ordering, backpressure, and starvation avoidance with realistic unit and integration tests?

In a real-time chat platform: dozens of chat rooms publish messages to a central router. Each room's messages must be delivered in the order published, while a global cap on in-flight messages bounds memory. Design a beginner-friendly concurrency solution (Go or Python asyncio) with: a global bounded queue, per-room FIFO buffers, a small worker pool, and a mechanism to retire inactive rooms to reclaim resources. Explain backpressure, ordering, and a simple test plan?

Intermediate: In a real-time event processor, N producers emit events into a bounded global queue of size Q. A pool of M workers consumes events. Each event has a key (e.g., user_id). Guarantee per-key in-order processing across all producers while allowing parallel processing for different keys. Implement per-key FIFO buffers with a maximum size K and a global backpressure mechanism when the queue is full. Decide overflow policy (drop oldest, drop new, or reject) and justify?

In a streaming analytics system, dozens of data shards emit aggregation tasks that must be processed within strict latency budgets. Design a bounded, hierarchical queue: a global bounded backlog that feeds per-shard FIFO queues, with a fixed worker pool. Enforce backpressure to producers when full, isolate shards to prevent starvation, and implement a fairness policy (e.g., weighted round-robin or tokens) to allocate processing time fairly across shards. Include a runnable minimal sketch in Rust or C++ showing enqueue and dequeue semantics and a basic test strategy to verify latency and ordering?

Design a real-time event router for a chat platform that guarantees per-room FIFO processing while enabling parallelism across rooms. N producers enqueue messages into a bounded global ring buffer of size C. Implement a lock-free multi-producer/multi-consumer router using per-room local queues inside workers and a global scheduler to balance backpressure. On overflow, apply a room-aware eviction: remove the oldest message from the least recently active room to preserve freshness for active rooms while preserving per-room order. Provide concrete data structures and outline a practical test plan validating per-room ordering, backpressure behavior, and starvation avoidance?

In a real-time multi-producer task queue, each task has a unique ID and must be processed exactly once. Producers submit tasks concurrently; workers may crash and tasks can retry. Design a beginner-friendly concurrency solution in Go or Python asyncio with a bounded global queue, a per-task dedup buffer, a small worker pool, and a crash-recovery protocol. Explain idempotence, backoff, and a concrete test plan?

Design a multi-tenant, bounded-concurrency task processor: N tenants push events into a shared queue of capacity Q. Each tenant’s events must be processed in per-tenant order, but tenants can run in parallel. Implement per-tenant FIFO buffers of size K, a dynamic cadence scheduling window per tenant (timer-wheel) to control throughput, and a fairness/backpressure policy that prevents starvation under burst traffic. Describe data structures, scheduling rules, and a minimal test plan?

In a distributed telemetry pipeline for a fleet of delivery robots, producers emit events with robot_id, seq, and payload. Design a concurrency strategy to process events with per-robot in-order handling, a bounded in-flight cap, and exactly-once persistence to an external store. Requirements: 1) bounded global queue with capacity, 2) per-robot buffers to preserve order, 3) a small worker pool to apply side effects, 4) handle late/duplicate events, 5) provide a runnable sketch in Go or Rust and a test plan for ordering, liveness, and recovery. How would you implement this?

Design a high-throughput event processor where dozens of producers publish events across many tenants. A single bounded global queue feeds a small worker pool. Each tenant’s events must be delivered in-per-tenant order, while events across tenants may interleave. Propose a concrete Go or Rust design using per-tenant FIFOs and a central arbiter, with backpressure, fault tolerance, and a test strategy to verify ordering and throughput under burst?

Design an intermediate concurrency interview problem: implement a three-stage streaming pipeline with bounded buffers: Ingress with N producers emits keyed records into a first queue; Transformer stage with M workers applies stateless processing; Aggregator stage with K workers computes per-key aggregates. Guarantee per-key in-order processing across all stages under backpressure, support dynamic worker resizing, and define a clear policy for late or out-of-order messages. Provide data structures and a concrete test plan?

Design a per-topic multi-stage streaming pipeline with dynamic worker pools and per-topic in-order guarantees. Producers publish topic-labeled messages to a bounded input queue. Workers route messages through a topic-specific Dispatcher, Processor, and Sink chain, each with bounded buffers. Ensure per-topic ordering, allow resizing the worker pool per topic, and backpressure that prevents starvation for hot topics. Include data structures, synchronization, and a test plan for late messages and topic churn?

Design a concurrent in-memory rate-limiter router for a fleet of microservices. N producers emit requests labeled by service_key; a bounded global queue feeds M workers. Implement per-key token buckets with independent refill rates and a global budget to cap total in-flight permits. Support dynamic key creation, backpressure signaling when the global queue is full, and a clear burst-idle policy. Provide concrete data structures and a test plan?

In a service handling image uploads, each file triggers a resize and thumbnail generation pipeline. Design a bounded producer-consumer queue in Python using asyncio. Use a Queue with maxsize, a fixed number of worker coroutines, and backpressure so producers await when full. Include clean shutdown and error handling. Provide a runnable minimal example showing enqueue, worker loop, and cancellation?

Write a small Python snippet: create a shared counter initialized to 0, spawn 4 threads that increment it 1000 times each, using a Lock to protect the increment. After joining, print the final value. Explain what happens if the lock is removed and how atomicity is ensured. What value do you expect and why?

In a real-time telemetry pipeline for multi-region IoT devices, design a bounded, region-scoped concurrency model that preserves per-region event order while capping memory usage. Describe data structures, backpressure signaling, and region lifecycle, and provide a runnable prototype outline in Go or Python showing enqueue, per-region dispatch, backpressure, and graceful shutdown. What tests would you add to verify ordering and backpressure?

Context: in a real-time analytics pipeline for a video-conference system, dozens of producers emit events into a shared queue and multiple workers consume them. Implement a bounded, multi-producer, multi-consumer queue with capacity 1024. It must not drop messages while not full, block producers when full, support concurrent consumers, and support a clean shutdown. Describe API, invariants, and a simple synchronization strategy?

Design a bounded, concurrent, multi-priority work scheduler for a rendering service: 3 priority levels (0 highest). Producers enqueue tasks into per-priority queues with backpressure; workers drain from the highest non-empty queue (0→1→2). Include aging to prevent starvation and a graceful shutdown sentinel. Provide a runnable minimal Java example?

Design a latency-sensitive, per-tenant fair scheduler for a multi-tenant streaming job system: N tenants, each with a dynamic quota and an independent FIFO queue; M workers pull jobs from any tenant queue, preserving per-tenant ordering, enforcing quotas via token buckets, and applying backpressure to tenants when global queue fills. How would you implement data structures, dynamic tenant changes, and a concrete test plan?

Design a fault-tolerant, bounded telemetry router: partition by region, with per-device FIFO buffers feeding a small worker pool. Use a central bounded queue to backpressure producers; ensure in-order processing per device via sequence counters and per-device reorder buffers. On regional outage, spill to durable regional store and throttle producers with backpressure. Auto-scale workers from 1 to K based on queue depth and latency?

Implement a thread-safe bounded queue using a fixed circular buffer with mutex protection and condition variables for coordinating producers and consumers. How would you handle enqueue/dequeue operations and implement graceful shutdown when the queue is no longer accepting new tasks?

In a CI/CD runner, hundreds of jobs from different teams submit tasks that form a DAG of artifacts. Design a bounded, multi-tenant work queue with per-tenant FIFO buffers and a dependency scheduler that enforces in-degree readiness. Include backpressure signaling, cancellation, and a minimal runnable sketch in Go or Rust?

Design a beginner-friendly concurrency coordinator for a web crawler: many producers submit domain-URL tasks concurrently. Use a bounded global queue and per-domain FIFO buffers. A small worker pool fetches pages, while a per-domain rate limiter enforces politeness (e.g., 2 requests/sec with burst). Explain backpressure, avoid cross-domain starvation, and outline a practical test plan for per-domain ordering, rate-limiter behavior, and failure recovery?

Design a real-time pipeline for per-user events: N producers emit events labeled user_id into bounded per-user queues of size B. A dispatcher routes available events to M workers while preserving per-user order across all workers. Support dynamic worker resizing, implement a backpressure policy when any per-user queue is full, and specify how late/out-of-order events are detected and handled?

Design a bounded worker pool for a high-throughput API gateway that queues work with backpressure. Use a lock-free ring buffer, N workers, and blocking enqueue when full. Include per-task cancellation, timeouts, and metrics. Compare Go, Rust, and Java trade-offs and explain how you’d debug data races and starvation under burst traffic?

Design a concurrent event broker for a live chat service that guarantees per-user in-order delivery while allowing parallel processing across users, using a bounded buffer; describe backpressure handling when the buffer fills, and compare locking versus lock-free approaches in your language of choice?

You run a real-time data ingestion service. Many producers publish tasks with a deadline timestamp and a payload size. A bounded global queue holds tasks; a scheduler pops tasks by earliest deadline and assigns them to a small worker pool for processing. Design a beginner-friendly Go or Python asyncio solution that enforces backpressure, explores deadline fairness, and includes a concrete test plan for late tasks, jitter, and queue fullness?

Design a beginner-friendly concurrency task queue for a monitoring system: multiple agents publish health checks concurrently; a bounded global queue feeds a small worker pool that writes results to a local store. Implement per-agent rate-limiting and a graceful shutdown that drains in-flight tasks without losing results. Explain backpressure, ordering, and a minimal test plan?

Design a concurrency-safe per-channel message queue for a Discord-like chat service: multiple producers push messages, a single consumer persists them to storage; implement bounded capacity, preserve per-channel order, and handle backpressure. Which synchronization primitives would you use and how would you test edge cases?

Design a concurrency strategy for a real-time trading analytics engine that ingests streams from 10k tickers, computes moving-window aggregates, and emits per-ticker streams to downstream consumers. Propose a bounded work queue, per-ticker partitioned state, dynamic worker pool resizing, and robust backpressure signaling to prevent hot-ticker starvation. Include failure recovery, observability, and a minimal runnable example?

Design a beginner-friendly concurrency event processor: multiple services emit events tagged by type A, B, or C at varying rates. Use a bounded global queue and per-type FIFO buffers. Some types require system-wide in-order processing; others can run in parallel up to a per-type limit. Explain backpressure, cross-type fairness, and provide a concrete test plan for ordering, throughput, and starvation scenarios?

You're building a real-time analytics pipeline with many shards. Propose a concurrent, bounded path that preserves per-shard in-order processing while enabling cross-shard parallelism. Design a data structure and protocol (enqueuing, routing, backpressure, and shutdown). Provide a runnable sketch in Go or Rust showing enqueue, per-shard consumer loop, and graceful shutdown?

Implement a concurrent task-graph executor with dependencies. Tasks form a DAG; a task runs only after all its prerequisites complete. Use a bounded in-flight task pool, per-worker work stealing, and deadlock/backpressure handling. Provide a runnable Go or Rust sketch showing submission, ready-state transitions, worker loop, and graceful shutdown?

In a multi-threaded microservice, there is a shared in-memory counter for total processed events. Provide a concrete, beginner-friendly approach to implement a thread-safe increment using language primitives (Java, Go, or Python) and discuss the trade-offs between lock-based vs lock-free solutions when scaling across cores?

Design a beginner-friendly concurrency pattern for a feature flag evaluation service: many microservices request flag values by key; a bounded global queue feeds a small worker pool that fetches from a remote flag store on a cache miss. Implement per-key request coalescing so concurrent requests for the same key trigger a single remote fetch; ensure fairness, backpressure, and a practical test plan?

Design a bounded, multi-tenant task router for a real-time telemetry ingest service. Producers submit per-tenant event batches; implement a global queue with max capacity N, plus per-tenant FIFO buffers. Build a fair, backpressure-aware scheduler that prevents starvation, supports dynamic tenant creation, and a small worker pool. Provide core data structures and a runnable minimal example?

In a Go HTTP server, you maintain a per-user quota counter in memory. Multiple requests for different users should advance concurrently, but updates to the same user must be serialized. Design a striped lock (a fixed set of mutexes) to guard a map[string]int, map userID to a bucket via hashing, and explain how you minimize contention, handle hash collisions, and ensure correctness when entries may be evicted?

Design a scalable, multi-tenant log processing system: hundreds of producers generate log events tagged by tenant_id. A bounded global queue feeds M workers. Include a MERGE example and a contract-failure rollback plan?

Ingest 100k protobuf events/sec from mobile devices across 5 regions. Events are nested and evolve with new types. Design an end-to-end streaming pipeline to Iceberg with per-record contracts, region isolation, and idempotent MERGE upserts; handle late data up to 15 minutes; emit per-event lineage; include basic data-quality gates and schema evolution. Compare Spark Structured Streaming vs Flink and outline testing/monitoring?

Design a global, multi-source streaming to a lakehouse feature store for ML models used in fraud detection across 5 regions. Data arrives as JSON events with nested fields and optional metrics. Implement per-source data contracts, tombstone support for GDPR deletions, time-to-live (TTL) policies, and late-arriving data up to 3 minutes. Explain idempotent upserts, schema evolution, partitioning, and drift monitoring. Compare Spark Structured Streaming vs Flink for ingestion path and outline testing, observability, and rollback strategy?

Design a real-time feature store for fraud detection. Ingest event streams (user_id, device_id, event_time, features), compute rolling aggregates (1m, 5m, 24h), and serve using a feature-time clock. Ensure training/serving parity, TTL-based invalidation, and offline/online consistency. Compare Redis vs Pinot for the online store and outline testing strategies (drift, canaries, data-quality checks)?

You run a multi-tenant real-time feature store on a lakehouse (Iceberg) used by several ML models. Data sources evolve schemas and models need deterministic joins by (tenant_id, user_id, timestamp). How would you implement feature versioning, per-record contracts, and idempotent upserts, while ensuring offline-online consistency and a plan for drift detection and backfills?

In a multi-region telemetry pipeline ingesting 40k events/sec from Kafka into an Iceberg lakehouse, enforce per-record contracts, region isolation, and schema evolution with late data up to 8 minutes. Design end-to-end using a streaming engine, idempotent upserts, per-record lineage, a schema registry, and a testing/rollback plan. What would you implement and why?

You're building a global privacy-preserving analytics product. Ingest CRM and order data from three regions (customer_id, region, order_id, product_id, amount, timestamp, consent_flag) into a lakehouse (Delta or Iceberg) with per-record lineage and region isolation. Implement dynamic masking policies that evolve over time, ensure GDPR delete propagation, and enforce near real-time dashboards. Describe end-to-end design, testing strategy, and provide a concrete masking policy example plus a MERGE/delete approach?

Design an end-to-end ingestion for a regional mobile gaming service that emits 25k JSON events per minute. Each event includes mandatory fields event_id, user_id, ts, event_type and an optional attr payload. Build a beginner-friendly pipeline that ingests from Kafka, validates per-record contracts, enforces schema evolution in an Iceberg lakehouse, and performs idempotent upserts by event_id. Include per-record lineage and late-arrival handling (up to 15 minutes)?

In a data-mesh across three BUs, each publishes JSON events to a central lakehouse. Design an end-to-end pipeline that isolates data by BU, enforces per-record contracts via a shared schema registry and policy engine, supports schema evolution, and performs idempotent upserts into Iceberg. Handle late-arriving data (up to 6h) and capture per-record lineage. Compare Spark vs Flink for this workload and propose monitoring?

Design an end-to-end ingestion and analytics pipeline for 20 TB/day of nested JSON events from 100 clinics across jurisdictions. Each event contains patient data with optional fields. Build a streaming path (Kafka -> Flink) into a lakehouse (Iceberg) with per-tenant data contracts, dynamic schema evolution, and per-country residency. Implement idempotent upserts into a dimensional model, support late events up to 30 minutes, and a field-level masking policy that varies by tenant and region. Compare Spark Structured Streaming vs Flink for this workload and outline testing, monitoring, and data-quality checks?

Ingest a daily JSONL feed containing user records with PII fields (email, phone). Build a beginner-friendly pipeline that redacts PII at ingest using tokenization, stores tokenized values for analytics, and upserts into a lakehouse dimension table while preserving per-record lineage in a metadata store. Ensure schema evolution for new fields and missing values. Outline tests, monitoring, and a simple SQL example for tokenization and lineage?

How would you roll out a backward-compatible schema change in an Iceberg-backed lakehouse used by multiple BI models when adding a new metric field to a widely consumed table, ensuring zero-downtime, data contracts, and rollback options?

Design a real-time feature store for ML inference at 100k lookups/sec, ingesting 3 streaming sources with evolving schemas. Specify data contracts, TTL-based pruning, feature versioning, and cross-region lineage. Explain data model (online/offline stores), ingestion, schema evolution, drift detection, and monitoring. Compare Flink vs Spark for streaming and outline tests and rollback strategies?

Ingest 2 regional streaming JSON feeds into an Iceberg lakehouse. Enforce per-record contracts: device_id, event_ts, metric non-null; optional fields allowed. Route non-conforming records to a bad_data sink. Support schema evolution for added fields. Use idempotent upserts into a star schema and handle late data up to 2 hours with watermarking. Compare Spark Structured Streaming vs Flink for this use case and outline a minimal test plan?

Design a nightly batch ingestion from three regional CSVs into an Iceberg lakehouse. Enforce per-record contracts: customer_id (string, non-null), event_time (timestamp, non-null), revenue (decimal(12,2), non-null), region (string, non-null); optional: campaign_id, device_type. Implement deterministic masking for customer_id (SHA-256) and redact emails if present. Support schema evolution, idempotent upserts into a star schema, and late data up to 6 hours with a watermark. Briefly compare Spark batch vs Flink batch and outline tests?

Design a multi-tenant regional data ingestion pipeline for a lakehouse (Iceberg) where 3 regions feed data with evolving schemas. Enforce per-record contracts at ingestion, support late rows up to 12h, isolate by region/tenant, and implement GDPR deletes without full dataset rewrites. Include a region-based change feed to downstream features, discuss testing/monitoring, and compare Spark vs Flink for this workload?

You receive three regional CSV feeds with differing schemas. Design a batch pipeline to harmonize into a single Iceberg lakehouse, enforcing a fixed contract: user_id (string), event_ts (timestamp), event_type (string) required; optional value (double). Normalize to a canonical schema, route nonconforming rows to /bad_data, deduplicate by (user_id, event_ts, event_type), and upsert into Iceberg. Support schema evolution via nullable new fields. Include a minimal test plan?

Nightly batch ingestion of 8 regional JSON feeds (~2–5 GB). Each event has record_id, user_id, region, event_ts, event_type, and an optional payload. Design a pipeline to load into an Iceberg lakehouse as a central fact_events table using idempotent upserts on record_id, enforce per-record contracts, route non-conforming rows to region-specific bad_data, and support schema evolution for new fields. Include a concise test plan and a simple row-level lineage approach?

Scenario: Global telemetry ingests JSON events from 200k devices/sec across regions. In addition to a raw event lake, design a versioned feature store on top of Iceberg that materializes simple features (count per device in last 5m, mean value, recency) and keeps per-record lineage to raw events. Requirements: dynamic feature definitions with schema evolution, per-record data contracts, late data handling up to 10 minutes, idempotent upserts, TTL pruning, and per-region data isolation. Include a concrete MERGE example and a high-level monitoring plan; compare Spark Structured Streaming vs Flink for this workload?

Design a pipeline that serves as both a data warehouse and an ML feature store. Ingest batch and streaming signals from 60 partners, partition data by region, and store both raw data and computed features in Iceberg. Implement a versioned feature registry, backfill-friendly feature definitions, and drift alerts to detect distribution shifts. Describe parity between batch and streaming features, and provide a concrete feature example: user_average_purchase_by_region. How would you test and monitor this system?

Design a multi-tenant ML feature store ingesting both batch CSVs and streaming Kafka topics into an Iceberg-based lakehouse. Each tenant has strict data contracts, PII masking, and per-tenant isolation. Implement feature versioning, immutable changelogs, and backfill support while preserving lineage for reproducible model training. How would you architect the end-to-end pipeline and governance?

Design a multi-tenant event ingestion pipeline where 1000 tenants emit JSON events with evolving schemas (tenant_id required, event_ts required). Ingest into a lakehouse (Iceberg) with per-tenant isolation, idempotent upserts, and late data handling. Enforce data contracts via a schema registry, validate at ingress, and route nonconforming records to a quarantine sink. Include GDPR delete handling per tenant and cost/latency trade-offs; compare Spark Structured Streaming vs Flink for this scenario and outline testing strategy?

Design a streaming feature store for ML workloads with 3 sources feeding ~200 features at varying update rates. Requirements: per-record contracts, tenant isolation, feature versioning with time travel, schema evolution, and idempotent upserts into Iceberg. How would you implement ingestion, upsert semantics, drift tests, and monitoring? Include a concrete MERGE-based upsert pattern?

Two regional CSV feeds arrive daily: customers.csv (customer_id, name, signup_ts, region) and orders.csv (order_id, customer_id, order_ts, amount, region). Build a beginner-friendly batch pipeline that validates per-record contracts (non-null keys, timestamps parseable, region in allowed list). Route bad rows to bad_data. Load good data into a Parquet lakehouse partitioned by region/date and implement a simple star schema with customers_dim and orders_fact. Support schema evolution if a new optional field like email is added to customers. Provide a minimal test plan and a sample MERGE upsert for customers?

You're building a streaming feature store for real-time ML in a SaaS platform. Ingest 200k events/sec from 5 modules with nested fields. Requirements: per-record lineage to a catalog, idempotent upserts into Iceberg, dynamic schema evolution, late data tolerance up to 2 minutes, and CI-driven data contracts with PII masking. How would you design end-to-end, including data contracts, governance, and a choice between Spark vs Flink for streaming?

Design an end-to-end pipeline for a fleet telemetry system: vehicle devices emit Protobuf-encoded messages at 1–2 MB/s per region via Kafka, with thousands of fields and frequent schema evolutions. Ingest into a lakehouse (Iceberg) with per-record lineage and idempotent upserts, support late data up to 6 hours, and enforce per-record data contracts. Describe architecture, testing (contract tests), and include a concrete MERGE-based upsert example and schema-change handling strategy?

You're maintaining a lakehouse (Iceberg) ingesting 100B events daily plus user profiles. A regulatory requirement: when a user revokes consent, past records must be masked or retroactively deleted, while preserving auditable lineage. Design an end-to-end solution that models per-record consent, propagates updates efficiently, supports retroactive masking vs deletion, handles late data, and includes data contracts and testing. Include concrete Iceberg MERGE patterns and lineage validation?

Design a multi-tenant, region-distributed data lake (Iceberg) ingestion pipeline for an ad-tech platform. Ingest 200k events/sec with nested attributes, enforce tenant-scoped data contracts, and support dynamic schema evolution. Describe how you implement a contract registry, per-record lineage, idempotent upserts, late data handling, and automated drift rollback with a concrete MERGE example?

You maintain a geo-distributed event pipeline ingesting 6 TB/day of JSON events from 30 regions into an Iceberg lakehouse. Each event carries a per-record contract with required fields and optional nested payloads; new fields may appear over time. Describe a practical end-to-end design that enforces per-record contracts, performs idempotent upserts, handles late data up to 60 minutes, and supports lineage tracking and schema evolution. Include a concrete MERGE example and how you would test contracts?

Batch ingestion exercise: ingest daily vendor CSV feeds with per-record contracts (vendor_id, user_id, event_date YYYY-MM-DD, action) and optional metadata. Build a simple pipeline that validates records, maps unknown columns into a metadata struct for schema evolution, writes to a lakehouse Parquet partitioned by vendor/date, and routes non-conforming rows to a bad_data sink. Add a lightweight per-row lineage manifest to support drift checks and provide a minimal test plan?

Scenario: Identity provider CDC for multi-tenant app used by Apple and Slack, streaming updates to user attributes into a lakehouse (Iceberg) with evolving schema. Design end-to-end pipeline with per-record contracts, tenant isolation, late data handling (15m), and idempotent upserts; specify how to enforce contracts, perform MERGE, and validate quality via tests; include a concrete MERGE example?

You're building a real-time feature store for a high-frequency trading analytics product. Three market data streams (tick, quote, event) feed at ~15k events/sec. Each event includes symbol, ts, and features. Emit per-record lineage to a metadata store; upsert into Iceberg with schema evolution. Backfill late events up to 60s via a backfill window; enforce data contracts with a protobuf/schema registry. Compare Spark Structured Streaming vs Flink for latency vs backfill; include monitoring and contract tests?

You operate a multi-tenant SaaS analytics platform ingesting per-tenant event streams from Kafka into Snowflake. Each tenant has different event schemas that can evolve independently. Design a data pipeline to enforce per-tenant data contracts, support late-arriving events, and minimize schema drift while controlling storage costs. Include schema versioning, validation, and deployment safety steps?

Design a nightly ingest for 4 regional JSON feeds into an Iceberg lakehouse. Enforce per-record contracts: required fields user_id, event_ts, event_type; optional fields allowed; implement a privacy masking policy for payload fields (mask PII unless whitelisted). Route non-conforming rows to a bad_data sink, support schema evolution for new attributes, and perform idempotent upserts into a star schema. Include a minimal code snippet showing contract check and a MERGE-based upsert, and outline a basic test plan?

You ingest 200k newline-delimited JSON app events daily into S3. Each event has event_id, user_id, timestamp, event_type, and attributes. Design a beginner-friendly pipeline to deduplicate by event_id, hash user_id for privacy, validate required fields, and write Parquet data partitioned by date in a data lake. Address simple schema drift and testing?

In a multi-tenant analytics platform, tenants publish JSON events to a central event bus. You must ingest into an Iceberg lakehouse with per-tenant isolation, support idempotent upserts, and tolerate late data up to 60 minutes. Schemas drift often. Propose a concrete end-to-end design: ingestion, schema evolution strategy, data contracts, GDPR delete handling, and a testing plan. Compare at least two engines and outline monitoring?

Design an end to end multi region data mesh pipeline where regional Kafka clusters feed a shared Iceberg lakehouse. Each region enforces per tenant data contracts access controls and GDPR delete handling; include backfill for missed windows and late arriving events up to 2 hours. Expose a real time feature store with drift detection and per tenant lineage and schema evolution, and outline a test plan. Compare Spark Structured Streaming vs Flink for processing?

Design a real-time data pipeline for a multi-tenant MongoDB deployment: capture Change Streams across all tenants, publish to region-scoped Kafka topics, and upsert into a lakehouse (Iceberg) with per-tenant isolation. Include handling of deletes, schema evolution, late data, and GDPR erase requests. Compare Debezium vs native Change Streams, outline idempotency, testing, and a minimal MERGE example?

Design a multi-tenant ingestion pipeline where 6 regional streams emit Avro/JSON events into 8 Kafka clusters, feeding an Iceberg-based lakehouse. Enforce strict tenant isolation (data and compute), per-tenant schema evolution, and per-tenant DSAR deletions. Outline end-to-end flow, partitioning strategy, data contracts, and how you verify no cross-tenant leakage. Compare Spark Structured Streaming vs Flink for ingestion, and outline testing/monitoring strategies?

Ingest three regional CSV feeds into a lakehouse. Build a batch pipeline that enforces per-record contracts (id, ts, user_id non-null; others optional), supports schema evolution for new columns, and upserts into a canonical star schema. Add lineage metadata and a small lineage table for dashboards. Include tests for missing fields, type drift, late rows and a concise MERGE workflow described in words?

You're building a multi-tenant SaaS analytics platform where each tenant streams events to its own Kafka topic (per region). Design an ingest-to-lakehouse pipeline that enforces per-record contracts from a central registry, evolves schemas automatically, isolates data by tenant-region, and supports upserts via MERGE INTO with late data up to 48 hours. Include per-record lineage, simple quality gates, monitoring, and a concrete MERGE example?

Design an end-to-end pipeline that ingests both streaming and batch events into a lakehouse (Iceberg) to power a cross-team feature store for ML models. Requirements: versioned feature definitions, per-record data contracts, idempotent upserts, late data handling, schema evolution, and end-to-end lineage. Compare Spark vs Flink for feature computation and describe testing/monitoring?

You run a global data platform ingesting 40k events/sec per region into an Iceberg lakehouse. Each event has tenant_id, event_ts, action, and a nested payload that evolves differently per tenant. Design an end-to-end pipeline that enforces per-tenant data contracts, supports per-tenant schema evolution, guarantees at-least-once ingestion with idempotent upserts, and keeps dashboards stable despite late data. Include testing, monitoring, and rollback plan?

Two regional CSV feeds arrive daily with overlapping fields but occasional drift. Design a beginner-friendly batch pipeline that (1) enforces a per-record contract: user_id (non-null), event_ts (ISO8601), action_type (enum), and optional metadata; (2) routes non-conforming rows to a bad_data sink; (3) unions valid rows into a central table with basic schema evolution to accept a new optional field; (4) loads into a lakehouse Parquet/ Iceberg; (5) provides a minimal data-quality report and deduplicates by (user_id, event_ts). What would you implement first and why?

Design a scalable, multi-tenant data ingestion and analytics pipeline for 100k JSON events/sec coming from 60 mobile apps across regions. Each tenant has its own data contracts (required fields: tenant_id, event_ts, metric), nested payloads can vary. Build per-tenant isolated tables in Iceberg lakehouse, support dynamic schema evolution, enforce per-record contracts, and propagate GDPR deletion requests to both raw and derived datasets, with lineage capture and access controls. Compare Spark Structured Streaming vs Flink for the path, and outline validation, testing, and monitoring?

Design a global, multi-tenant data ingestion system for a ride-hailing platform with streams for billing, trips, safety, and promotions. Each tenant defines a data contract; schemas evolve independently; late-arriving events up to 15 minutes must be accepted. Describe architecture using Apache Kafka, Schema Registry (Avro/JSON), an Iceberg/Delta lake sink, and a streaming processor (Flink/Spark). Include data model, schema evolution, backfill handling, testing, and observability?
How would you design a data pipeline that handles both batch and streaming workloads for real-time analytics?
How would you design a Kafka Streams application to handle exactly-once processing with stateful aggregations while maintaining sub-second latency during peak loads of 100K events/sec?

How would you implement exactly-once processing in a data pipeline when both source (Kafka) and sink (database) can fail, ensuring no duplicate data or data loss during network partitions and system crashes?

Design a dynamic forest (always acyclic) that supports: link(u, v, w) to join two trees with a new edge of weight w, cut(eid) to remove an edge by its id, updateWeight(eid, w) to change an edge weight, pathSum(u, v) for the sum of edge weights on the path between u and v, and pathKthLargest(u, v, k) to return the k-th largest weight along that path. Aim for amortized O(log n). Explain data structure, edge-id handling, and path queries?

Design a dynamic interval data structure on a real line supporting: insertInterval(l, r, w, id), eraseInterval(id), updateIntervalWeight(id, w), and queries: sumWeightsAtPoint(x) and kthLargestWeightAtPoint(x, k) for a given x. Duplicates allowed; end points are real numbers. Outline a practical structure that gives fast updates and point queries with O(log n) touched nodes and explain how to select k-th weight across multiple nodes?

Design a dynamic leaderboard data structure for a real-time game: implement insertUserScore(userId, score) that adds a new user or updates an existing user's score, removeUser(userId) to drop a user, and getTopK(k) to return the top k users by highest score. Tie-break by userId to ensure deterministic order. Target O(log n) per operation. Describe the data structures you would use, how you handle updates, how you ensure deterministic order for ties, and present a simple implementation outline in your preferred language?

Design a stack that supports push(x), pop(), top(), and getMin() in O(1) time per operation. Duplicates allowed. Explain the approach, discuss invariants and space usage, and provide a compact code sketch (Python or Java)?

Dynamic multigraph connectivity task: Maintain undirected graph with edges added by id and possibly duplicates, deletions by id, and edge weight changes. Support as-of-time queries: (a) is u connected to v at time t? (b) how many connected components exist at time t? Outline an offline approach using a segment-tree over time and a rollback DSU to achieve O((n+m) log m) total time, including how to handle edge lifespans and weight changes?

Design a dynamic interval-weight data structure that supports insertInterval(id, L, R, w) and eraseInterval(id) (duplicates allowed), and queries for a given point x: sumWeightsCoveringPoint(x) and kthLargestWeightCoveringPoint(x, k). Maintain O(log^2 N) update and query costs; describe data organization and how to support kth selection?

Design a data structure that behaves as a double-ended queue for integers. It must support pushFront(x), pushBack(x), popFront(), popBack(), and median() which returns the current median value; for even counts, return the lower median. All operations should be amortized O(log n). Explain how you organize storage, handle duplicates, and describe how to maintain the median efficiently when deletions occur from either end (hint: use two balanced multisets or heaps with lazy deletions and rebalancing)?

Design a dynamic sequence data structure (rope) that supports insertAt(i, v), eraseAt(i), and rangeQuery(i, j) returning both sum and maximum subarray sum within A[i..j]. Duplicates allowed. Achieve amortized O(log n) per update and O(log n) for queries. Explain how you augment nodes with sum, prefMax, suffMax, bestMax, and how splits/merges propagate those values; discuss handling empty ranges and edge cases?

Design a dynamic interval-weighted set on a 1D line. Intervals [l, r] carry weight w and a unique id; support insertInterval(l, r, w, id), eraseInterval(id), and updateWeight(id, newW). Provide efficient queries: sumWeightsAtPoint(x) returning the total weight of all intervals covering x, and kthLargestWeightInRange(l, r, k) returning the k-th largest weight among all intervals that intersect the range [l, r]. Scalable to up to 2e5 intervals with coordinate compression?

Design a dynamic sequence of integers supporting insertAt(index, value), eraseAt(index), and rangeKthSmallest(l, r, k) that returns the k-th smallest value in subarray [l, r] with duplicates. Propose a dynamic wavelet tree variant (value range up to 2^31-1) yielding O(log V * log N) per operation. Explain how per-level bitvectors support insert/delete, how to choose/maintain coordinate compression, and how to implement rangeKthSmallest from prefix counts. Provide rough pseudocode for insert and kth?

Design a dynamic string multiset data structure that supports insert(s), eraseOne(s) (remove one occurrence), and two queries: countWithPrefix(p) which returns how many strings currently in the set have prefix p, and kthStringWithPrefix(p, k) which returns the k-th string in lexicographic order among strings with prefix p. Duplicates allowed. Provide data structure, update procedures, and query algorithms with expected complexities and trade-offs?

Design a dynamic forest data structure that supports insertEdge(u,v,id,w), eraseEdge(id), and queries pathSum(u,v) and pathMax(u,v) on a graph with possible duplicate edges. Aim for near O(log n) amortized updates and queries. If u and v are already connected when inserting, replace the heaviest edge on the path if beneficial to maintain a spanning forest. Explain your approach and data layout?

Design a dynamic forest data structure that supports linking two trees with a weighted edge, cutting an existing edge, updating an edge weight, and querying the sum of edge weights on the unique path between any two nodes. Provide amortized O(log n) per operation and explain how you prevent cycles?

Design a dynamic sequence data structure that supports insertAt(index, value), eraseAt(index), and rangeGCD(l, r) with 1-based indices and duplicates allowed. Achieve amortized O(log n) per operation. Explain the data structure (e.g., implicit treap or rope) and how gcd is maintained under split/merge, including edge cases and how you handle non-overlapping gcd reuse?

Design a dynamic 1D interval multiset with operations insertInterval(l, r, w, id) and eraseInterval(id). Each interval has a weight w (duplicates allowed). Implement queries: sumWeightsAtPoint(x) returning the sum of weights of all intervals covering x, and kthLargestWeightAtPoint(x, k) returning the k-th largest weight among intervals covering x. Target amortized O(log N) updates and O(log N) queries. Explain data structure, coordinate compression, and how to handle deletions and duplicates?

Design a dynamic interval data structure on the number line that supports insertInterval(l, r, w, id) and eraseInterval(id) (duplicates allowed by id). Provide queries: sumWeightsCoveringPoint(p) and kthLargestWeightCoveringPoint(p, k) for a given point p. Target amortized O(log^2 n) updates and O(log^2 n) queries. Describe the data organization, how to handle duplicates, coordinate compression, and how to perform kth selection efficiently?

Design a dynamic interval data structure on a line that supports: addInterval(l, r, w, id), eraseInterval(id), updateWeight(id, newW). Queries: sumWeightsAtPoint(x) and maxWeightInRange(a, b). Coordinates up to 1e9; duplicates allowed. Target amortized O(log^2 n) updates and O(log^2 n) queries. Describe data organization, id-to-node tracking, and how you ensure correctness for overlapping intervals?

Design a data structure to maintain a dynamic forest of undirected weighted edges supporting: addEdge(u, v, w) only if u and v are in different trees, removeEdge(id), and updateEdgeWeight(id, newW). Provide queries maxWeightOnPath(u, v) and sumWeightOnPath(u, v) for the path between u and v. Achieve amortized O(log n) per operation and explain edge representation, how to avoid cycles, and how duplicates and edge IDs are managed?

Design a dynamic weighted dictionary of strings with insertWord(word, w) and eraseWord(word, w) (duplicates allowed). Provide queries sumWeightsForPrefix(prefix) and kthLargestWeightForPrefix(prefix, k). How would you implement it and ensure O(length(word) * log n) updates and O(log n) prefix queries?

Design a dynamic rope-like string container that supports insertAt(pos, s), deleteAt(pos, len), and replaceAt(pos, s); and queries substringHash(l, r), compareSubstrings(l1, r1, l2, r2) (return -1/0/1), and longestCommonPrefix(i, j). The data structure must handle total length up to 2e6, with amortized O(log n) edits and O(log n) hash queries. Propose an implicit-treap rope where each node holds a chunk and stores subtree length and 64-bit rolling hash; explain split/merge, hashing, collision handling, and how to implement the LCP and substringHash efficiently?

Design a dynamic multiset with duplicates that supports insert(x), erase(x) (erase one occurrence), and getMedian() in amortized O(log n) per operation. Explain a concrete implementation using a max-heap for the lower half and a min-heap for the upper half, plus a lazy-deletion map to handle erasures, and how getMedian is computed when the total size is even vs odd?

Design a time-aware dynamic connectivity data structure. Support operations: addEdge(u,v,id) with a lifespan until its removal, removeEdge(id), and connected(u,v) queries at the current time. Edges are active over time intervals; scale to 2e5 ops. Propose an offline approach using a segment tree over time and a rollback DSU to achieve near O(log n) per op, and outline how to manage edge lifespans and query ordering?

Design a dynamic time-window data structure for a multiset of weighted events, each with a timestamp. Support insertEvent(t, w) and eraseEvent(t, w) (duplicates allowed). Implement queryMaxSubarraySumInWindow(t1, t2) that returns the maximum subarray sum over any contiguous sequence of events with increasing timestamps within [t1, t2], along with the start and end timestamps achieving it. Target amortized O(log n) updates and O(log n) queries. Explain your data layout and combination rules?

Design a BrowserHistory data structure that supports visit(url), back(steps), forward(steps), and current(). Visiting a new URL clears the forward history; back/forward move within the stored URLs. Provide a concrete, beginner-friendly approach with O(1) amortized per operation and O(n) space. Include a minimal implementation sketch?

Design a dynamic autocomplete data structure for a code search tool that stores terms with frequencies; implement insertWord(word), eraseWord(word), and querySuggestions(prefix, k) returning up to k completions starting with prefix, ordered by descending frequency then lexicographically. Discuss a Trie-based design with per-node top-k structures and update costs?

Design a dynamic multiset of integers supporting insert(x), erase(x) (one occurrence per operation), and kthSmallest(k) (1-based). Duplicates allowed. Outline a data structure and algorithm to achieve O(log n) updates and O(log n) kth queries. Include how to handle values up to 1e9 without pre-allocating all indices, and show how insert/erase affect internal counts?

You’re building a music streaming app; design a dynamic playlist data structure as a sequence of songs. Support insertAt(index, songId, duration), eraseAt(index), and rangeTotalDuration(l, r). Duplicates allowed. Achieve amortized O(log n) per operation. Describe the structure, how inserts/erases adjust augmented data, and outline the algorithm for rangeTotalDuration?

Design a data structure to maintain a dynamic catalog of items each with a baseline score and a timestamp. Support operations: insertItem(id, score, t), updateItem(id, score, t), eraseItem(id). Queries: topKInLastWindow(k, t, W) returning k items with highest decayed score within the time window [t-W, t], where each item's decayed score is score * e^{-λ (t - t_i)} with t_i the last update time for that item; and sumScoresInWindow(t, W) giving total decayed score in the window. Aim for amortized O(log n) per update and O(log n + k log n) for topK, under memory constraints. Explain data structures, decay handling, and tie-breaking?

Design a dynamic weighted dictionary keyed by strings with duplicates allowed. Implement insertWord(word, weight) and eraseWord(word, weight). Provide queries: sumWeightsWithPrefix(prefix) and kthLargestWeightWithPrefix(prefix, k) for all words starting with prefix. Aim for amortized O(log n) updates and O(log n) queries. Discuss data structure, handling duplicates, and how you support kth largest with prefixes in real time?

Design a data structure to maintain a dynamic set of weighted intervals on a line. Each interval [L, R] has a weight w and a unique id. Supported operations: addInterval(id, L, R, w), removeInterval(id), updateIntervalWeight(id, newW). Queries: sumWeightsAtPoint(x) giving the total weight of all intervals covering x, and kthLargestWeightAtPoint(x, k) returning the k-th largest weight among intervals covering x. Aim for amortized O(log N) updates and O(log^2 N) queries. Explain data layout and update steps?

Design a dynamic set of axis-aligned rectangles with duplicates allowed. Operations: insertRect(x1,y1,x2,y2,w) and eraseRect(id) to manage weighted rectangles.
