Support queries: pointQuery(x,y) returning total weight of all rectangles covering (x,y), and kthLargestPointQuery(x,y,k) returning the k-th largest weight among those rectangles currently covering (x,y). Aim for amortized O(log^2 n) updates and queries. Describe data structure, coordinate compression, and handling of duplicates and deletions?

Design a dynamic sequence of chat messages with operations: insertAt(index, msg), eraseAt(index), and rangeWordCount(l, r) which returns the total number of words across messages l..r. Each message is a string; duplicates allowed. Explain a practical implementation that keeps operations near O(log n)?

Design a data structure to maintain a real-time leaderboard for a chat app with a sliding window W seconds. Provide operations: addEvent(userId, value, ts), evictOlderThan(ts), and topK(k, ts) returning the top k users by total value within [ts-W+1, ts]. Duplicates allowed; values non-negative. Explain data organization, update rules, and eviction strategy. What are the complexities and trade-offs?

Design a dynamic leaderboard data structure to manage players with unique IDs and integer scores. Supported operations: addPlayer(id, score), removePlayer(id), updateScore(id, delta), and topK(k) returning the top k players by score (ties broken by id). Duplicates allowed in scores. How would you implement to achieve O(log n) updates and O(k log n) topK while enabling fast ID lookups?

Design a dynamic 2D convex hull that supports insertPoint(x,y, id) and erasePoint(id) (duplicates allowed). Provide queries maxDotProduct(w) for a vector w = (dx, dy) using the active points. Deletions require an offline approach: describe an offline solution using a segment-tree over time, how to assign active intervals [tAdd, tDel), how each node stores a convex hull of its points, and how to answer queries by aggregating hulls along the path to time t with O(log^2 n) total time?

Design a dynamic interval data structure on the number line with operations: insertInterval(l, r, w, id), eraseInterval(id), updateWeight(id, newW) (duplicates allowed across ids). Provide queries: sumWeightsAtPoint(p) and kthLargestWeightAtPoint(p, k) among intervals [l, r) containing p. Target amortized O(log N * log W) updates and O(log N * log W) queries. Explain data organization, how you handle overlaps, and duplicates?

Design a data structure to track ride events per driver in a ride-hailing analytics system. Provide operations: insertEvent(driverId, ts, revenue), eraseEvent(eventId), and queries TopKDrivers(windowMs, k) and TotalRevenue(windowMs) for the last windowMs milliseconds. Target amortized updates O(log n) and queries O(log n + k log n). Explain data organization, eviction policy, and tie-breaking?

Design a dynamic multiset of 32-bit integers supporting insert(x), erase(x) (one occurrence), and queries at any time for the maximum xor obtainable from any subset of the current multiset. Duplicates allowed. Propose an offline solution using a segment-tree over time with a rollbackable linear basis to answer each query in O(32 log n); outline data structures, update rules, and complexity?

Design a dynamic multiset of words with duplicates that supports insertWord(w), eraseWord(w) (by count), containsWord(w), and countWithPrefix(prefix). Use a Trie with per-node endCount and subCount; explain how you maintain counts during insert/erase and how countWithPrefix(prefix) works. Provide time complexities?

Design a dynamic MST-maintenance structure for an undirected graph with parallel edges. Support: addEdge(u,v,w,id), eraseEdge(id), updateEdgeWeight(id,newW). Queries: isConnected(u,v) and totalMSTWeight(). Describe data structures and how MST updates handle edge replacements and duplicates, including time complexity guarantees?

Design a dynamic interval set on a line. Each interval [l, r) has a weight w and duplicates allowed. Support:
- insertInterval(l, r, w) -> id
- eraseInterval(id)
- updateWeight(id, w)

Queries:
- totalWeightInRange(a, b): sum over x in [a,b) of the total weight of intervals covering x
- kthLargestCoverageInRange(a, b, k): consider the multiset of coverage weights on [a,b) induced by all active intervals; return the k-th largest weight among the elementary subsegments induced by interval endpoints within [a,b)?

Design a dynamic sequence data structure that stores integers and supports insertAt(index, value), eraseAt(index), and rangeMedian(l, r). Duplicates allowed. Values are 32-bit integers. Achieve O(log V) per operation and O(log V) for rangeMedian, where V is the value range, using a Dynamic Wavelet Tree or an equivalent structure. Explain the data layout, how inserts/erases update the structure, and how rangeMedian is computed?

Design a dynamic undirected multigraph data structure with edge IDs that supports addEdge(u, v, w, id), eraseEdge(id), and updateEdgeWeight(id, newW). Maintain per-node degrees, and provide queries: 1) countNodesWithDegree(d), and 2) topKDegreesByFrequency(k) returning the k degree values with the highest node counts. Duplicates allowed; ensure amortized O(log N) updates. Describe data structures, edge-id handling, and how to compute top-k without mutating counts?

Design a dynamic data structure for a multiset of weighted intervals on the real line. Support insertInterval(l, r, w) and eraseInterval(l, r, w) (duplicates allowed). Provide time-aware queries as of time t: sumWeightsCoveringPoint(x, t) and kthLargestWeightCoveringPoint(x, t, k) for all intervals covering x at time t. Target amortized O(log n) updates and O(log^2 n) queries. Explain coordinate compression, per-node multisets, and time-versioning?

Design a dynamic multiset of integers representing session durations. It must support insert(value), eraseOne(value) (erase a single occurrence), countLE(x) (number of elements <= x), and kthSmallest(k) (the k-th smallest value, 1-based). Duplicates allowed. Describe the data structure you would implement, how duplicates are stored, and provide brief pseudocode for each operation, including how to locate the kth smallest?

Design a dynamic 2D weighted point set supporting insertPoint(x,y,w) and erasePoint(x,y,w) with duplicates allowed. Provide queries sumWeightsInDiamond(cx,cy,r) and kthLargestWeightInDiamond(cx,cy,r,k) for points inside the L1-ball around (cx,cy) with radius r. Target: amortized O(log^2 n) per operation. Explain data layout, coordinate transform to (u=x+y, v=x-y) to map diamond to rectangle, and how to support kth selection with duplicates?

Design a dynamic interval multiset over the real line supporting insertInterval(l, r, w, id) and eraseInterval(id) with duplicates allowed. Provide queries: sumWeightsInRange(L, R) returns total weights of all active intervals intersecting [L, R), and kthLargestOverlapWeightInRange(L, R, k) returns the k-th largest weight among intervals that intersect [L, R) at the current time. Aim for amortized O(log n) updates and O(log^2 n) queries. Discuss coordinate compression, duplicate handling, and a practical 2D structure to support kth largest?

You manage a timeline as a set of overlapping intervals [l, r], each with a weight w. Build a dynamic interval-weight data structure that supports insertInterval(l, r, w) with duplicates allowed, eraseInterval(id), and queries at a point x: sumWeightsAtPoint(x) and kthLargestWeightAtPoint(x, k) among intervals covering x. Aim for amortized O(log^2 n) per operation. Describe data layout, per-node multisets, and how you handle deletions and duplicates?

Design a data structure to maintain a multiset of integers supporting insert(x), erase(x) (erase a single instance if duplicates exist), and rangeCount(l, r) that returns how many elements lie in the inclusive interval [l, r]. Duplicates allowed. Target amortized O(log n) per operation. Describe the underlying structure, how duplicates are tracked, and how rangeCount is computed efficiently?

Design a dynamic compressed trie (prefix tree) to store a multiset of strings with weights, supporting operations: insertKey(s, w), eraseKey(s, w) (duplicates allowed), and queries: sumWeightsWithPrefix(p) and kthLargestWeightWithPrefix(p, k) for all keys starting with p. Target amortized O(|s| log U) updates and O(log U) prefix queries, using a compressed trie with per-node weight multisets. Explain data structure, update rules, and how kth selection handles duplicates?

Design a data structure to implement a queue that supports enqueue, dequeue, and getMin in O(1) time. Explain the data layout, how each operation maintains the minimum, and how duplicates are handled. Provide an implementation plan and edge-case behavior for empty states, in a language of your choice?

Design a simple LRU cache with capacity C that supports put(key,value) and get(key) in O(1). On capacity overflow, evict the least recently used item. Explain the data structures and the update rules for recency when get or put is called?

Design a dynamic multiset of integers with operations insert(x), erase(x) (one occurrence), and getKthSmallest(k). Duplicates allowed. Ensure O(log n) expected per operation. Explain which data structure you would use (e.g., a balanced BST with subtree sizes or a Fenwick tree over compressed values), how duplicates are stored, and provide a concise implementation sketch for insert, erase, and getKthSmallest?

Design a dynamic undirected multigraph with edge insert(id, u, v, w), eraseEdge(id), and updateEdgeWeight(id, newW). Duplicates allowed. Implement subgraph queries on vertex indices [L,R]: - sumWeightsInSubgraph(L,R): sum of weights of edges with both endpoints in [L,R] - kthLargestEdgeWeightInSubgraph(L,R,k): k-th largest weight among those edges Target amortized O(log^2 n) for both updates and queries. Explain the data structure, including segment-tree over vertex IDs and how edges are distributed and aggregated?

Design a dynamic 2D weighted point set. Support operations: insertPoint(x, y, w, id), erasePoint(id), updatePointWeight(id, newW). For a given axis-aligned rectangle [x1, x2] × [y1, y2], implement queries: (a) sumWeightsInRectangle(x1, x2, y1, y2) and (b) kthLargestWeightInRectangle(x1, x2, y1, y2, k) among active points inside the rectangle (duplicates allowed). Aim for amortized O(log^2 n) updates and O(log^2 n) queries. Describe data organization and how to handle duplicates and dynamic changes?

Design a dynamic interval data structure on the numeric axis [0, 2^32-1] that supports: addInterval(l, r, w, id), eraseInterval(id), updateWeight(id, newW). Queries: countCoveringPoint(p) and kthLargestWeightCoveringPoint(p, k) for a given p (k <= countCoveringPoint(p)). Target amortized O(log^2 N) for both updates and queries. Describe the data structure, how you handle overlaps and duplicates, and how the k-th weight is extracted without enumerating all covering intervals?

Design a data structure to process a stream of integers with three operations: add(x), remove(x) (remove one occurrence if present), and getMedian() which returns the current median value (or the average of the two middle values if even). Duplicates allowed. Explain how you maintain the two halves and how you rebalance on insert and delete; discuss time complexities?

Design a Trie-based dictionary that supports insert(word), erase(word), and autocomplete(prefix, k) returning up to k words starting with prefix in lexicographic order. Duplicates are tracked via word frequency; a word only appears in results if its frequency > 0. Describe data layout, update rules, and how to implement autocomplete to stop after k results. Provide a coding sketch?

Design a data structure to maintain the dynamic union of half-open intervals [l, r) for a real-time booking system. Support addInterval(l, r), removeInterval(l, r) with overlapping intervals, and queryTotalCovered() returning the total booked time. Aim for amortized O(log n) updates. Explain data layout, how overlaps are merged, and provide a simple example?

Design a dynamic interval set on a 1D axis (e.g., time) that supports insertInterval(l, r, w) and eraseInterval(l, r, w) with duplicates allowed. Provide queries sumWeightsAt(x) and kthLargestWeightAt(x, k) for a point x. Target amortized O(log^2 n) per operation. Explain data layout, coordinate compression, and how to combine per-node weight structures to answer kth-largest?

Design a dynamic interval-weight data structure on a number line. Implement operations: addInterval(l, r, w) with duplicates allowed, eraseInterval(id), and updateIntervalWeight(id, w). Queries: sumWeightsAtPoint(x) for total weight of all intervals covering x, and kthLargestWeightAtPoint(x, k) for the k-th largest weight among intervals covering x. Target amortized O(log N * log W) per operation with coordinate compression. Explain data layout, handling duplicates, and how to perform kth selection?

Design a dynamic multiset of integers that supports insert(x), erase(x) for a single instance, and queryRank(x) returning the number of elements strictly less than x, as well as findKthSmallest(k). Propose a simple implementation using a balanced BST augmented with subtree sizes and a duplicate count; discuss handling duplicates, deletions, and edge cases?

Design a data structure to track weighted events per user key over time. Supports: upsertEvent(key, timestamp, weight) (duplicates allowed), eraseEvent(eventId) to delete by id, updateEventWeight(eventId, newWeight). For a key and time window [t0,t1], provide: sumWeightsInWindow(key, t0, t1) and kthLargestWeightInWindow(key, t0, t1, k). Target O(log n) updates and O(log n) queries. Explain how you’d implement with time-versioning and how duplicates are handled?

Design a dynamic 1D interval data structure on a number line supporting insertInterval(l, r, w) and eraseInterval(id, w) with duplicates allowed. Provide queries: totalWeightCoveringPoint(x) and kthLargestWeightCoveringPoint(x, k) for a fixed point x. Aim for amortized O(log n) updates and O(log n) queries. Explain coordinate compression, segment-tree mapping of intervals to O(log n) nodes, and per-node multisets to support sums and kth selection, including erase-by-id?

Design a dynamic string data structure for a text editor that supports: insertAt(pos, ch), deleteAt(pos), replaceAt(pos); and queries: hash(l, r) returning a 64-bit hash and substringEquals(l1, r1, l2, r2) to test identity. The aim is amortized O(log n) updates and O(log n) queries. Explain the data structure and how to maintain rolling hash with dynamic indexing, handling splits/merges, collision risks, and edge cases?

Design a dynamic multiset of integers supporting insert(x), erase(x) (duplicates allowed), and querySumInRange(l, r) which returns the sum of all elements with values in the inclusive range [l, r]. Explain the data structure you would use, how you handle duplicates, and outline how insert/erase adjust subtree sums to enable range queries in O(log n) time on average?

Implement a dynamic username registry using a Trie that supports addUser(name), removeUser(name) (one occurrence per call), and prefixCount(prefix) returning how many usernames start with the given prefix. Duplicates allowed. Explain how this would power a chat app's username auto-suggest, how counts are maintained for duplicates, and deletion handling with O(length) per operation?

Design a dynamic rope data structure for a mutable string supporting insert(pos, s), delete(pos, len), and substringHash(l, r) in O(log n) time. Use an implicit treap where leaves store string chunks; each node tracks subtree length and a rolling hash. Explain split/merge, hash maintenance, and collision handling, plus how to answer substringHash efficiently?

Design a dynamic, undirected graph data structure that supports edge insertions and deletions with unique edge ids. Implement a query twoStepPaths(u, v) that returns the number of distinct vertices w such that edges (u, w) and (w, v) exist (i.e., number of two-step paths from u to v). Use adjacency hash sets and explain update costs and correctness. Scenario: in a payments network, two-step routing checks rely on quick counts?

Design a dynamic forest data structure that maintains an edge-weighted forest with operations: link(u, v, w, id) to add a weighted edge between two trees; cut(id) to remove an edge; updateWeight(id, newW) to update an edge's weight. Queries: pathSum(u, v) for the sum of weights along the unique path, and kthLargestEdgeOnPath(u, v, k) for the k-th largest edge weight on that path. Aim for amortized O(log n) updates/queries; discuss edge-node representation and how rotations preserve path aggregates?

Design a persistent rope data structure for a collaborative text editor: support insert(pos, text), delete(pos, len), and queryHash(l, r, version) returning a rolling hash of substring [l,r] as of a given version. Ensure O(log n) edits and O(log n) hash queries with path-copying persistence; discuss memory usage, collision handling, and how to implement balancing and concatenation?

Design a rope data structure to store a mutable string, supporting insertAt(pos, s), deleteAt(pos, len), and substring(l, r) in O(log n). Describe the node layout, how implicit keys and leaf substrings work, and how split/merge maintain substring views; include edge cases and a brief complexity sketch?

Design a dynamic multiset of integers with insert(x), erase(x) (one occurrence), and queryKthSmallest(k). In addition, support a global addAll(delta) that adds delta to every element in the set. All operations must be O(log n). Propose a concrete data structure and algorithm; discuss handling duplicates, lazy offset, and how erase maps to stored keys after offset changes?

Design a payroll analytics data structure to maintain a dynamic set of employee salaries with operations: addEmployee(id, salary), removeEmployee(id), updateSalary(id, newSalary). Provide queries: sumSalariesInRange(minSalary, maxSalary), countSalariesInRange(minSalary, maxSalary), and kthSalaryInRange(minSalary, maxSalary, k). Duplicates allowed, IDs unique. Aim for amortized O(log n) per operation; discuss data layout, how to support range queries efficiently, and how you handle updates and deletes?

You're building a lightweight search autocomplete for a chat app. Design a Trie that supports insertWord(word), deleteWord(word) removing a single occurrence, and countWordsWithPrefix(prefix) returning how many stored words start with the prefix. Assume lowercase a-z, duplicates allowed; describe structure, operations, and a quick example?

Design a dynamic rope to store a mutable string with operations insertAt(i, s) and deleteAt(i, len). Provide substringHash(l, r) and equalSubstring(l, r, l2, r2) in O(log n). Explain data structure choices, how you maintain size and hashes, and collision mitigation. Assume long strings typical of code editors?

Design a mutable string data structure that supports:
- insertCharAt(i, c)
- deleteCharAt(i)
- countOccurrences(P) for any pattern P
- kthOccurrenceIndex(P, k) returning the index of the k-th occurrence

Provide expected time bounds, how edits affect global counts, and how to handle overlapping occurrences. Assume n up to 1e6 and a small alphabet?

Design a dynamic forest data structure (link-cut tree) that supports: link(u, v) to connect two trees, cut(u, v) to remove an edge, updateVal(u, x) to assign a new value to a node, and pathQuery(u, v) that returns the path's sum, maximum, and minimum values. Target amortized O(log n) per operation. Explain how the splay-based augmentation maintains sum/mx/mn during rotations, and how to compute path aggregates?

Design a persistent binary trie for 32-bit unsigned integers that supports insertValue(x) and eraseValue(x) with duplicates. Provide time-travel queries: countInPrefix(version t, prefix, length) and kthLargestInPrefix(version t, prefix, length, k) returning the k-th largest value among numbers matching the top-prefix. Aim for O(log W) updates and O(log W) queries. Explain persistence via path-copying, handling duplicates, and memory trade-offs?

Design a dynamic prefix dictionary: insertWord(word, weight), eraseWord(word, weight) with duplicates allowed. Support queries sumWeightsWithPrefix(prefix) and kthLargestWeightWithPrefix(prefix, k). Propose a Trie where each node stores an ordered multiset of weights (with counts) and a subtree total weight. Update along the word path for insert/erase; sum is retrieved from the prefix node; kthLargest uses the node’s multiset?

Design a dynamic forest supporting:
- link(u, v, w): connect two trees with an edge of weight w
- cut(u, v): remove the edge between u and v
- makeRoot(u): re-root the tree containing u
- pathQuery(u, v): return the sum of edge weights along the path u-v
- updateEdge(id, newW): update the weight of a specific edge by its unique ID
Notes: allow parallel edges; aim for amortized O(log n) per operation; assume up to 2e5 nodes and edges?

Design a dynamic 1D interval multiset on a number line with insertInterval(l,r,w,id) and eraseInterval(id). Queries: sumWeightsCoveringPoint(p) and kthLargestWeightCoveringPoint(p,k). Use coordinate compression and a segment tree; each node holds a multiset of weights for intervals fully covering that node. Insert/erase add/remove w on O(log n) nodes; sum is path-sum; kth uses per-node order statistics with a global binary search on weights?

Design a dynamic forest data structure that supports link(u, v, w), cut(eid), and pathSum(u, v) for the sum of weights along the path between u and v. Duplicates allowed; undirected edges with weights. Aim for amortized O(log n) per operation. Explain how a Link-Cut Tree (edges as nodes) handles makeRoot, access, and path aggregates, how edge IDs map to cuts, and correctness under sequences of links/cuts. Include a minimal example?
Design a dynamic multiset that supports insert(x), eraseOne(x), and getKthSmallest(k) in O(log n) time. Duplicates allowed. Explain the data structure and algorithm?

Design a simple persistent stack of integers. The API should support: push(x) -> returns a new version id, pop(version) -> returns a new version id, top(version) -> returns the top value of that version (or null if empty), and isEmpty(version). Explain the data structure, how each operation creates new nodes without copying the whole stack, and analyze memory usage and time per operation?

Design a dynamic multiset of strings (duplicates allowed) that supports insert(s), erase(s) (one occurrence), and queries: countInPrefix(p) and kthStringWithPrefix(p, k). The kthStringWithPrefix should return the actual string, not just its index. Explain the data structure and update/query procedures, with expected time bounds?

Design a data structure for a fixed-size sliding window maximum: support push(x), popOldest(), and getMax() in O(1) amortized time. Duplicates allowed. Explain the data layout, how you maintain the current max as the window slides, and edge cases when the window isn't full?

Design a dynamic multiset that supports insert(x), erase(x) (duplicates allowed), and getMedian() in O(log n) time per operation. Describe your data structures, how duplicates are tracked, how you rebalance the two halves, and how erase is performed when the target value is not at the top of a heap?

Design a data structure to maintain a dynamic multiset of strings with operations: insert(s), erase(s), and getKthLexicographic(k). Duplicates allowed. All operations should be O(log n) on average. Explain the internal layout (counts per string, ordering), how erase handles missing keys, and how getKthLexicographic finds the k-th item. Example: insert 'apple','apple','banana','cherry'; getKthLexicographic(3) => 'banana'?

Design a dynamic forest data structure that supports: link(u, v, w) to connect two trees with an edge of weight w, cut(u, v) to remove that edge, and updateEdge(u, v, newW) to change the weight of the edge between u and v. Provide queries: sumPath(u, v) and maxPath(u, v) returning the sum and maximum edge weight along the unique path between u and v. Achieve amortized O(log n) per operation and explain trade-offs?

Design a dynamic prefix trie storing words with multiplicities. Operations: insertWord(word, delta) and eraseWord(word, delta). Queries: sumCountsWithPrefix(prefix) and kthLargestCountWithPrefix(prefix, k). Duplicates allowed. Each node maintains subtreeSum and an order-statistics structure of word counts in its subtree. Explain update and query times and how to handle worst-case with many near-identical prefixes?

Design a dynamic event-logging data structure for real-time analytics. Each event has (id, category, timestamp, weight). Support insertEvent(id, category, timestamp, weight) and eraseEvent(id). Queries: sumWeightsInCategoryInWindow(category, tStart, tEnd) and kthLargestWeightInWindow(category, tStart, tEnd, k). Duplicates allowed. Target amortized O(log n) updates and O(log^2 n) queries. Explain indexing by category and time, how to handle duplicates and erase, and memory considerations?

Design a dynamic weighted interval data structure over a 1D axis that supports: addInterval(id, l, r, w), eraseInterval(id), updateWeight(id, w). Query: queryMaxInRange(L, R) returning the maximum total weight at any point x in [L, R] and the leftmost x achieving it. Assume coordinates up to 1e9 and weights can duplicate. Provide amortized O(log C) updates and O(log C) queries, where C is the coordinate range. Explain data layout, overlap handling, and retrieval of the arg max?

Design a dynamic interval set with weights supporting insertInterval(l,r,w,id) and eraseInterval(id,w) (duplicates allowed). Provide queries sumWeightsAtPoint(x,t) and kthLargestWeightAtPoint(x,t,k) at time t. Target amortized O(log n) updates and queries. Explain data layout, time/versioning, and duplicate handling?

Design a dynamic weighted interval stabbing structure. Scenario: an online ad platform schedules campaigns as time intervals [L, R] with weight w; allow insertInterval(id, L, R, w), eraseInterval(id), and updateIntervalWeight(id, newW) (duplicates allowed for same [L,R]). Provide queries: sumWeightsCoveringPoint(t) and kthLargestWeightCoveringPoint(t, k) for a given time t. Target amortized O(log^2 N) per operation and O(log^2 N) for kth largest. Describe data organization, coordinate compression, and how you handle deletions and duplicates?

Design a time-versioned data structure for a dynamic set of 1D intervals [L, R] with weights, supporting insertInterval(L,R,w) returning id, eraseInterval(id), and updateWeight(id, newW). Provide two versioned queries for a fixed x and version t: (a) sumWeightsCoveringX(x, t) and (b) kthLargestWeightCoveringX(x, t, k). Aim for amortized O(log^2 n) updates/queries using persistence and coordinate compression; discuss handling duplicates and memory?

Design a time-traveling priority queue for a trading simulator that supports: insert(key, id), delete(id), increaseKey(id, newKey), decreaseKey(id, newKey), and queries maxAtTime(t) and kthLargestAtTime(t, k). Each operation should be O(log n) amortized; provide a persistent structure (e.g., treap) with versioning. Explain memory bounds, how deletions work across versions, and how to answer historical queries efficiently?

Design a dynamic interval multiset on a 1D axis. Support insertInterval(l, r, w, id) and eraseInterval(id, w) (duplicates allowed). Queries: sumWeightsAtPoint(x) = sum of weights of all intervals covering x; kthLargestWeightAtPoint(x, k) = k-th largest weight among those intervals. Achieve O(log N) updates; for kth queries use binary search on weight with per-node counts; implement with a segment tree over coordinates storing weight multisets and an id→node-list map?

Design a dynamic string dictionary with duplicates. Implement operations: insertWord(word), eraseWord(word) removing one instance, and countWithPrefix(prefix) returning how many stored words start with that prefix. Use a Trie with per-node prefixCount and endCount. Explain how duplicates are tracked, how eraseWord validates availability, and the expected time/space behavior?

Design a Trie-based dictionary that stores words with duplicates and supports insertWord(word), eraseWord(word), and countWordsWithPrefix(prefix) efficiently. Assume lowercase English words, max length 100, duplicates allowed. How would you implement and what are the time complexities?

Design a dynamic interval set on a number line that supports addInterval(a,b), removeInterval(a,b), and queryPoint(x). Intervals are closed and merged to keep the set disjoint. Implement so each operation is O(log n) on average. Explain how you merge or split intervals and how you handle edge cases like full coverage or empty sets?

Design a data structure to maintain a streaming sliding window with fixed size k. Implement operations add(value) and getSum() that returns the sum of the most recent min(windowSize, k) values. The structure should run in O(1) amortized per operation and support negative values. Describe the data layout, update rules, and edge cases when fewer than k elements exist?

Design a dynamic forest data structure supporting operations: link(u, v, w, id) to connect two trees with a weighted edge, cut(id) to remove the edge, and updateWeight(id, newW) to change the edge weight. Provide queries: sumPath(u, v) and kthLargestOnPath(u, v, k) for the path between u and v. Explain data structure and approach for achieving efficient path sums and kth-largest on a path, including trade-offs?

Design a dynamic interval set on a number line. Maintain a set of closed intervals with these ops: addInterval(l, r) inserts and merges overlapping intervals; removePoint(x) deletes the single point x from the union (splitting an interval if needed); and totalCovered() returns the total length of the union. Work with large coordinates and up to 2e5 ops; aim for amortized O(log n) per op?

Design a dynamic, duplicate-tolerant priority queue that supports: insert(key, id), erase(id), decreaseKey(id, newKey), and kthLargest(k). Duplicates allowed. Aim for amortized O(log n) per operation and O(log n) for kthLargest. Explain a concrete data structure (e.g., treap or balanced BST) with (price, id) ordering to disambiguate equal keys, how erase by id works, how decreaseKey is implemented, and how kthLargest finds the k-th largest when duplicates exist. Context: high-volume order book or job scheduler?

Context: beginner level data-structures. In a streaming analytics scenario, design a dynamic array that supports append(value), updateAt(index, value), and rangeSum(l, r) in O(log n) time per operation. Propose using a Fenwick tree or segment tree; describe how you handle 1-based indexing, growth when appending, and duplicates in values. Include a concrete example with values [3,5,7], append 2, updateAt(2,6), and sum(1,3)?

Design a dynamic multiset that supports insert(x), erase(x) (one occurrence), and getMedian in O(log n) time. Explain how you handle duplicates, how you rebalance two heaps, and how to erase efficiently (e.g., lazy deletion)? Provide a small concrete example sequence to illustrate?

You are tasked with designing a dynamic latency histogram for a real-time analytics system: implement insertLatency(x), eraseLatency(x) (duplicates allowed), and percentileQuery(p) that returns the smallest latency t such that at least p% of latencies are <= t? Describe the data structure, how updates adjust counts, and how percentile queries are computed with duplicates and deletions?

Design a data structure to maintain a sliding time window of event durations. Events arrive as (ts, dur). The window spans the last W seconds. Support insertEvent(ts, dur), advanceWindow(now) to drop expired events, sumDurationsInWindow() and kthLargestDurationInWindow(k). Duplicates allowed. Target O(log n) updates and O(log n) kth queries. Explain your structure and trade-offs?

Design a dynamic interval set with possible duplicate intervals [l, r], each carrying a weight w. Operations: insertInterval(l, r, w, id), eraseInterval(id), and queryOverlapSum(L, R) that returns the sum of weights of all intervals that intersect [L, R]. Provide amortized O(log n) updates and O(log n) queries. Describe the data structures, how duplicates and deletions are managed, and outline the algorithm for overlap sums?

Design a dynamic session tracker: each session has an id, a score, and a lastActive timestamp. Support insertSession(id, score, ts), updateScore(id, delta), expireSessionsBefore(ts) removing expired sessions, topK(window, k) returning the k highest scores among active sessions (active = ts >= now - window) breaking ties by id, and medianScore(window) returning the median score among active sessions. Target near O(log n) per update and O(k log n) for topK. Explain data structures and tradeoffs?

Design a dynamic integer sequence that supports insertAt(index, value), eraseAt(index), and rangeSum(l, r) with duplicates allowed. Propose a practical solution using sqrt-decomposition: partition the sequence into blocks of size around √n, each block storing its elements and a cached sum. Describe how you maintain blocks, update sums on insert/erase, how you split/merge blocks, and how sum(l, r) runs in O(√n). Include a concrete example?

Design a dynamic sequence that supports insertAt(i, v), eraseAt(i), and rangeKth(l, r, k) to return the k-th smallest value in subarray [l, r], duplicates allowed. Target amortized O(log^2 n) per operation. Explain data structure choices (e.g., implicit treap with per-subtree ordered multisets or a segment-tree-of-multisets with coordinate compression), how updates propagate, and how to answer range queries efficiently?

Design a data structure to maintain a dynamic dictionary of words supporting insertWord(word), deleteWord(word), and countWordsWithPrefix(prefix) in O(len(word)) time for insertion/deletion and O(len(prefix)) time for prefix queries. Describe the data structure, how duplicates are handled, memory management, and edge cases, and provide a brief implementation sketch in a language of your choice?

Design a dynamic interval data structure over the integer line supporting insertInterval(id, l, r, w) and eraseInterval(id) (duplicates allowed) and two queries: sumWeightsCoveringPoint(p) and kthLargestWeightCoveringPoint(p, k). Aim for amortized O(log^2 n) updates and queries. Describe the data layout (segment-tree-of-multisets or interval tree), how to erase by id, and how to perform kth selection across the path from root to leaf?

Design a dynamic suffix automaton that supports appendCharacter(c), popCharacter(), countOccurrences(P), and kthOccurrenceIndex(P,k) for patterns P in the current string, with length up to 1e6 and alphabet a-z; explain how you maintain states, handle backtracking on pops, and ensure near-linear total time for sequences of operations?

Design a dynamic interval set on a fixed coordinate axis supporting addInterval(l, r, w, id) and removeInterval(id) with duplicates allowed. At any point x answer (a) countIntervalsCovering(x) and (b) kthLargestWeightCoveringPoint(x, k). Target amortized updates O(log N) and queries O(log N log W). Describe data layout (segment tree over coordinates with per-node multisets), deletions, and how to implement kthLargest across multisets?

Implement a dynamic word multiset that supports addWord(word), removeWord(word), and countPrefix(prefix) in O(len(word)) for updates and O(len(prefix)) for queries. Duplicates allowed. Design a Trie where each node stores passCount (how many words pass through) and endCount (how many end here). Explain insertion, removal (with underflow handling), and how countPrefix('pre') computes the answer?

Design a dynamic interval-weighted structure on a discrete line supporting insertInterval(l, r, w) and eraseInterval(l, r, w) with duplicates; provide queries: sumWeightsCoveringPoint(x) and kthLargestWeightCoveringPoint(x, k) for any x. Target amortized O(log^2 N) updates and O(log N * log W) queries. Explain data organization, coordinate compression, and how to perform kth selection with duplicates?

Design a dynamic leaderboard data structure to support a game with many players: addOrUpdatePlayer(playerId, score), removePlayer(playerId), getTopK(k), and getPlayerRank(playerId). Achieve O(log n) updates and O(log n + k) to fetch the top-k. Explain how you handle duplicates (equal scores) and score changes?

Design a persistent, immutable priority queue that supports: insert(x) -> id, min(), popMin() -> (id, x) and a new version, decreaseKey(id, newX), plus versioning operations forkVersion() and checkoutVersion(v). How would you implement O(log n) per operation with O(log n) new nodes per update and multiple versions coexisting?

Design a dynamic interval map: maintain a set of disjoint intervals [l, r] each with a weight w. Support insertInterval(l, r, w) that adds the range, merging overlaps by splitting existing intervals so the final structure remains disjoint; eraseInterval(id); updateWeight(id, w). Queries: sumWeightsInRange(a, b) and kthLargestWeightInRange(a, b, k). Strive for amortized O(log n) updates and O(log n) queries using a treap of endpoints and augmented weights?

Design a dynamic 1D interval multiset on the number line. Each interval i has a closed range [l_i, r_i] and a weight w_i; duplicates allowed. Provide operations insertInterval(l,r,w) -> id, eraseInterval(id), and updateWeight(id,newW). At any time t, support: (a) sumWeightsCoveringPoint(p,t) and (b) kthLargestWeightCoveringPoint(p,t,k) for intervals covering p. Target amortized O(log N) updates and O(log^2 N) queries. Describe data structures, persistence, coordinate compression, and handling of deletes and duplicates?

Context: A lightweight text editor stores a document as a sequence of characters. Design a data structure that supports: 
- insert(pos, s): insert string s at character position pos
- delete(pos, len): remove len characters starting at pos
- substring(pos, len): return the substring of length len starting at pos
Aim for O(log n) time per operation on average. Describe the data structure (e.g., an implicit treap or rope), how you handle splitting/merging chunks and maintaining lengths, and outline the algorithms for each operation with a small example?

Design a dynamic 1D interval set on a coordinate axis that supports: insertInterval(id, L, R, w), eraseInterval(id), updateWeight(id, w). Duplicates allowed. Queries: sumWeightsAtPoint(x) and kthLargestWeightAtPoint(x, k) for the current coordinate x. Coordinates up to 1e9; up to 2e5 intervals. Explain data structure, how you map intervals to nodes, handle removals by id, and implement kthLargest with per-node weight frequencies. Provide complexity and trade-offs?

Design a dynamic interval container over a time line that supports: addInterval(id, l, r, w), removeInterval(id), updateInterval(id, newW). Duplicates allowed. Queries: sumAtPoint(t) = sum of weights of all intervals covering time t, and kthLargestAtPoint(t, k) = k-th largest weight among active intervals at time t. Propose the data structure, update procedures, and both time and space complexities, with a practical bandwidth-reservation scenario on a shared link?

Context: you’re building an online ad platform that schedules campaigns as weighted time intervals [start, end]. Design a dynamic interval store that supports insertInterval(start, end, weight) -> id, eraseInterval(id), and two queries at a point p: sumWeightsAtPoint(p) and kthLargestWeightAtPoint(p, k) among all intervals covering p. Duplicates allowed. Aim for amortized O(log N) updates and O(log N log M) kth queries; describe data layout, interval decomposition strategy, and how to implement the kth-largest using counts from per-node weight Fenwicks?

Context: Calendar-like resource management. Design a data structure that supports addReservation(start, end) returning an id, cancelReservation(id), and queryPoint(t) returning how many active reservations cover time t. Use coordinate compression and a Fenwick tree to achieve O(log n) per operation. Explain interval storage, cancellation mapping, and edge handling for inclusive/exclusive endpoints?

Design a dynamic forest data structure supporting link(u,v,weight) and cut(u,v) to maintain a spanning forest, with edge weights allowing duplicates. Provide two path queries: pathSum(u,v) = sum of weights on the path, and pathKth(u,v,k) = k-th smallest edge weight along the path. Achieve amortized O(log n) updates and O(log n) queries. Explain data structure, edge representation, and how to compute kth?

Design a dynamic forest data structure that maintains a collection of trees under edge insertions and deletions. Support: link(u, v, w) to connect two trees with edge weight w; cut(u, v) to remove that edge; and pathQuery(u, v) returning two values: the sum of edge weights along the path and the maximum edge weight on that path. Also support updateEdge(edgeId, newW). Explain how to keep path aggregates correct under rotations and guarantee O(log n) amortized per operation?

Design a dynamic prefix-aware dictionary that stores strings with counts (duplicates allowed). Implement: addWord(s), removeWord(s) removing one occurrence, queryPrefixCount(p) giving how many distinct words start with p, and kthWordWithPrefix(p, k) returning the k-th word in lexicographic order among words beginning with p. Handle up to 2e5 words, optimize memory and updates; propose a data layout (e.g., compressed Trie) and discuss trade-offs and edge cases?

Design a rope-based dynamic sequence that supports: insertAt(i, val), eraseAt(i), updateAt(i), and queryMaxSubarray(l, r) which returns the maximum subarray sum within the subarray [l, r]. Ensure amortized O(log n) for updates and O(log n) for queries. Explain how you store per-node aggregates (sum, maxPrefix, maxSuffix, maxSub) and how split/merge operations update them. Consider all-negative arrays and duplicates?

Design a dynamic interval-weight index: insertInterval(l, r, w) and eraseInterval(id) with duplicates allowed. Provide queries sumWeightsCoveringPoint(x) and kthLargestWeightCoveringPoint(x, k) for a given coordinate x. Achieve amortized O(log N) updates and O(log^2 N) queries using coordinate compression; explain the data layout, how to handle duplicates and id-based removals, and the trade-offs of a Fenwick-per-node approach?

Design a data structure to maintain a dynamic histogram over a fixed value domain [-1000, 1000]. Implement insertValue(x), eraseValue(x) (duplicates allowed), and findQuantile(p) returning the smallest value v such that at least p fraction of elements are ≤ v. Aim for O(log D) per operation with D = 2001. Explain using a Fenwick tree on counts and how to handle edge cases when total count is zero or p is 0 or 1?

Design a dynamic interval-weight data structure that supports insertInterval(l, r, w) and eraseInterval(l, r, w) with duplicates allowed. Provide queries sumWeightsAtPoint(x) and kthLargestWeightAtPoint(x, k). Aim for amortized O(log n) updates and O(log^2 n) queries. Outline the data organization (coordinate compression, segment-tree-of-multisets), how deletions with duplicates are handled, and how you implement kthLargestWeightAtPoint using binary search over weights across the node multisets. In a real-world setting such as online ad campaigns active over time windows, how would you choose w and manage stale intervals?

Context: A calendar stores booked time blocks as closed intervals [start, end] in minutes. Implement a data structure with operations: addInterval(start, end) which merges overlaps/adjacent blocks, removeInterval(start, end) which subtracts the given range from existing blocks (splitting if needed), and isTimeBooked(t) which returns true if t lies in any interval. Achieve O(log n) per operation on average. How would you implement and handle edge cases?

Design a dynamic interval index for a 1D line that supports insertInterval(l, r, w), eraseInterval(id), and updateWeight(id, w) with duplicates allowed. Provide two queries: (a) sumOverlapAt(x): total weight of all intervals covering point x, and (b) sumWeightsFullyContainedIn(a, b): total weight of intervals fully contained in [a, b]. Target amortized O(log n) updates and O(log n) queries. Explain data organization, handling of overlapping duplicates, and how to perform queries efficiently?

Design a data structure to maintain a dynamic set of closed intervals [l, r] on the integer line. Support: addInterval(l, r): insert and merge any overlapping/touching intervals; removeInterval(l, r): subtract this range from all intervals, splitting if needed; totalCovered(): return the total length of the union of all intervals. Aim for average O(log n) per operation. Explain the representation, merging/splitting logic, and edge cases with an example?

Design a dynamic interval multiset with operations: insertInterval(id,l,r,w), eraseInterval(id), updateIntervalWeight(id,newW). Queries: maxOverlapPoint() returning the maximum total weight across all points and the leftmost coordinate attaining it; and sumWeightsAtPoint(x) returning total weight of intervals covering x. Coordinates up to 1e9; duplicates allowed. Provide amortized O(log U) per operation?

Design a dynamic multiset of integers that supports insert(x), erase(x) (one occurrence), rank(x) returning the number of elements strictly less than x, and select(k) returning the k-th smallest element (1-based). Duplicates allowed. Aim for O(log n) expected time per operation. Explain the data structure you would use, how duplicates are stored, and how select/rank traverse equal keys. Include a brief example sequence demonstrating operations?

Design a dynamic interval multiset with weights. Implement operations insertInterval(l, r, w) -> id, eraseInterval(id). Maintain a function queryGlobalMax() that returns the coordinate x where the sum of weights of all active intervals covering x is maximized, and the value at x. Intervals may duplicate; coordinates up to 2^31-1. Provide an implicit segment tree solution and discuss time and space?

Design a dynamic sequence over lowercase letters supporting insertAt(index, ch), eraseAt(index), countInRange(l, r, ch) and mostFrequentInRange(l, r) (return the character with highest count and its frequency). Achieve expected O(log n) per operation. Describe the data structure (implicit treap/rope with per-node freq[26]), how insert/erase update size and freq, and how to implement range queries by split/merge. Provide a high‑level implementation plan and edge cases?

Design a persistent rope data structure that supports insertAt(i, s), deleteAt(i, len), and getHash(l, r, t) returning the polynomial rolling hash of substring [l, r] in the string as of version t. Duplicates allowed; aim for amortized O(log n) per update and O(log n) per hash query. Explain your persistence strategy and how you maintain rolling hashes across versions?

Design a dynamic interval multiset on the real line supporting insertInterval(l, r, w, id) and eraseInterval(id). For a query at point x, return (a) sumWeightsAtPoint(x): total weight of all active intervals covering x, and (b) kthLargestWeightAtPoint(x, k): the k-th largest weight among active intervals covering x. Aim for O(log n) updates and O(log n) queries. Explain data structure, how duplicates are handled, and how erase interacts with future queries?

Design a dynamic interval multiset on the real line: support insertInterval(id, l, r, w) and eraseInterval(id) (duplicates allowed via distinct ids). For a point x, provide (1) sumWeightsCoveringPoint(x) and (2) kthLargestWeightCoveringPoint(x, k). Aim for amortized updates O(log N) and queries O(log N · log W). Explain the data structure and algorithms?

Design a dynamic interval data structure that maintains a multiset of closed intervals [L, R] with weights and unique ids. Support insertInterval(L, R, w, id), eraseInterval(id), and updateIntervalWeight(id, w). Implement queries at a point x: (a) totalWeightAt(x) = sum of weights of all intervals covering x, and (b) kthLargestWeightAt(x, k) among those intervals. Duplicates allowed. Aim for amortized O(log n) per update and O(log n) per query. Sketch data layout and correctness?

Design a dynamic forest data structure for a network of servers where edges carry latency weights. Support: link(u,v,w) to connect two trees with latency w, cut(eid) to remove an edge, updateEdge(eid,newW) to change latency, and queryMaxPath(u,v) to return the maximum edge latency on the path between u and v (or -inf if not connected). Target amortized O(log n) per operation. Explain the data structure choice and edge representation for efficient path queries and connectivity?

Design a dynamic bitset over a universe [1, 10^9] that supports set(l, r), reset(l, r), flip(l, r), sum(l, r), and kthOne(l, r, k). Use a run-length encoded interval map to achieve near O(log M) updates, where M is number of stored intervals. Explain data structure, edge cases, and complexity; provide a robust approach for sparse updates in large N?

Design a dynamic interval-weight data structure on a line that supports: addInterval(id, start, end, weight), eraseInterval(id), and updateInterval(id, newStart, newEnd, newWeight). Provide two queries: sumWeightsAtPoint(x) and kthHeaviestWeightAtPoint(x, k) for the set of active intervals covering x. Aim for amortized O(log n) updates and O(log n · log m) queries for sums, and O(log n · (log m)^2) for kth; assume weights compress to [1..m]. Describe the data organization and update/query strategies, handling duplicates and deletions?

Design a data structure to maintain a sliding window of the last N events in a high-throughput stream. Support: push(id) to append an event, and topK(k) to return the k most frequent ids in the current window, breaking ties lexicographically. The window automatically discards the oldest events when size exceeds N. Describe the data structures, update strategies, and time complexities?

Design a dynamic interval multiset on a number line: insertInterval(l, r, w, id) and eraseInterval(id) (duplicates allowed). For a point p, compute sumWeightsAtPoint(p) and kthLargestWeightAtPoint(p, k) among active intervals covering p. Target amortized O(log N) updates and O(log N log W) queries. Propose a segment tree over compressed coords with per-node weight multisets; explain updates by id and how to perform the kth query?

Design a dynamic forest data structure (no cycles) that supports: link(u,v,weight), cut(edge_id), updateWeight(edge_id, newW), and queryPathMax(u,v) returning the maximum edge weight on the path between u and v in the current forest. Duplicates allowed for weights; ensure amortized O(log n) updates and queries. Explain how to maintain max-weights on preferred paths and handling multiple edges between the same endpoints?

Design a dynamic string editor data structure that supports insert at position, delete substring, and substring hash queries with O(log n) edits and O(log n) hash lookups. Propose a rope-based solution using an implicit treap, where each node stores size and a double rolling hash (mod1, mod2). Explain split/merge, hash maintenance, collision mitigation, and memory trade-offs with a realistic editor workload?

Design a dynamic rope-based data structure that maintains a mutable giant string formed by concatenating leaves. Support insert(i, s) and delete(i, len). Provide efficient countOccurrences(P) and kthOccurrenceIndex(P, k) for any pattern P, including overlapping matches and matches spanning leaf boundaries. Explain how leaf splits/merges and how you maintain cross-leaf matches to preserve near-log time per operation?

Design a dynamic sequence data structure that supports:
- insertAt(i, x)
- eraseAt(i)
- rangeKth(l, r, k) // k-th smallest value in a[l..r]

Duplicates allowed. Target amortized O(log^2 n) per operation for n up to 2e5. Explain the data structure, how inserts/deletes affect internal aggregates, and how to compute rangeKth efficiently (e.g., via a value-domain search using per-block counts)?

Design a dynamic interval set over a 1D coordinate axis. Support operations:
- addInterval(l, r, w, id) with duplicates allowed
- eraseInterval(id)
- updateIntervalWeight(id, newW)
Provide queries:
- sumWeightsAtPoint(x) for all intervals covering x
- kthLargestWeightAtPoint(x, k) among those intervals
Aim for amortized O(log n) updates and O(log^2 n) queries. Explain data structure and how to handle overlapping intervals and duplicates, including space considerations and edge cases?

For a dynamic sequence of integers, design a data structure that supports append(value), insertAt(index, value), eraseAt(index), and rangeFreq(l, r, value) returning the number of occurrences of value in subarray [l, r]. Duplicates allowed. Propose a sqrt-decomposition approach: partition into blocks of size ~sqrt(n), maintain per-block vectors and a frequency map. Explain updates and block splits/merges with a concrete example: start [3,5,7], append 3, insertAt(1,4), eraseAt(2), rangeFreq(1,4,3)?

Design a dynamic text structure for a mutable document supporting insertAt(i, c), deleteAt(i, count), and substringEquality(l1, r1, l2, r2) that returns whether two substrings are equal. Aim for amortized O(log n) updates and O(log n) substring checks. Explain the data structure choice, how to maintain rolling hashes under split/merge, and how to handle hash collisions robustly (e.g., double hashing)?

You maintain a per-stream time-windowed weighted event index. Each event is (stream_id, timestamp, weight); duplicates of identical triples are allowed. Implement operations: addEvent(stream_id, timestamp, weight), eraseEvent(stream_id, timestamp, weight). Queries: sumWeightInWindow(stream_id, t1, t2) and kthLargestWeightInWindow(stream_id, t1, t2, k). Target amortized O(log n) updates and O(log n) queries. How would you organize data and handle duplicates?

Design a dynamic forest structure that supports: (1) link(u,v,w) to add an edge of weight w between u and v (edge-id assigned), (2) cut(id) to remove edge by id, (3) updateEdge(id, newW). Queries: pathSum(u,v) = sum of edge weights along the unique path, and kthEdgeOnPath(u,v,k) = weight of the k-th edge on that path from u to v. Amortized O(log n) per op. Duplicates allowed. Explain data representation, edge-nodes, and how to implement kth query efficiently?

Design a dynamic string data structure that supports insertAt(index, ch), eraseAt(index), and countCharInRange(l, r, ch) for lowercase letters. The goal is practical implementability with roughly O(sqrt(n)) updates and queries. Describe layout, when to split/merge blocks, and how per-block counts are maintained. Include an example using the string 'hello': insertAt(2, 'a'), eraseAt(4), then countCharInRange(1,4, 'l')?

Context: online leaderboard of numeric scores (duplicates allowed). Implement a data structure that supports: insertScore(s), eraseScore(s) (one instance), getKthScore(k) returning the k-th smallest score, and getRank(s) returning how many scores are <= s. Assume scores lie in [0, 1e6]. Use a Fenwick tree with static range; outline insertion/erasure, how to implement getKth via binary lifting, and handle ties?

Design a dynamic interval-weight data structure on the integer axis. Support insertInterval(id, L, R, w) and eraseInterval(id) (duplicates allowed). Queries: sumWeightsAtPoint(x) returning the total weight of all intervals covering x, and kthLargestWeightAtPoint(x, k) returning the k-th largest weight among intervals covering x. Target amortized O(log N) updates and O(log^2 N) queries. Outline data layout, coordinate compression, and how per-node multisets enable kth selection?

Design a versioned multiset with persistence: support insert(x), erase(x) (duplicates allowed), and queries countLessThan(version t, x) and kthSmallest(version t, k) for any historical version t. Optimize memory: aim for O(log n) time per operation and O(log n) new nodes per update; discuss persistent tree structures and versioning strategies?

Design a dynamic 2D spatial index for weighted points that supports insertPoint(x,y,w,id) and erasePoint(id) (duplicates allowed with same (x,y) but different ids). Provide operations: updatePoint(id, x, y, w) and queries: kClosestPoints(xq, yq, k) and sumWeightsInCircle(xq, yq, r). Target amortized O(log n) updates and O(log n + k) for kClosest, and O(log n) for sum. Explain data structure choices, balancing strategy, and how you handle deletions and duplicates?

Design an offline dynamic connectivity solution: given a sequence of edge additions and removals over time and connectivity queries at specific times, compute whether two nodes are connected at those times. Propose an approach using a segment-tree over time plus a DSU with rollback, explain edge lifetime mapping, multi-edge handling, and complexity guarantees?

Design a dynamic multiset of integers that supports insert(x), erase(x) (one occurrence), kthSmallest(k), and countLessThan(x) in O(log n). Duplicates allowed. Explain your approach (e.g., balanced BST with subtree sizes or Fenwick with coordinate compression), how you handle duplicates, and edge cases for k out of range or x not present?

Design a data structure to manage a live order book for a single instrument. Each order has a unique id, a price (int), and a quantity. Support insertOrUpdateOrder(id, price, quantity), cancelOrder(id), sumQuantitiesInPriceRange(minPrice, maxPrice), and kthLargestQuantityInPriceRange(minPrice, maxPrice, k). Duplicates allowed at the same price. Provide amortized O(log^2 n) updates and queries and explain how you handle cancellations and memory?

Context: live leaderboard. Implement a data structure MedianSet that supports insertScore(x), removeScore(x) (one occurrence), and getMedian() in O(log n) per update; duplicates allowed. Describe the two-heap approach with lazy deletions, balancing, and how removal works when the value isn't at the top. Example: insert 5, 1, 3, remove 1, then median?

Design a lightweight 1D histogram data structure for values in [0, 1_000_000] that supports: insertValue(v), eraseValue(v) (one occurrence), rangeCount(l, r) counting how many values lie in [l, r], and kthValueInRange(l, r, k) returning the k-th smallest value within [l, r]. Aim for O(log M) per operation. Compare Fenwick vs segment-tree-of-frequencies and discuss handling of duplicates and memory?

Design a data structure to maintain a dynamic set of closed intervals on the number line. Implement addInterval([l, r]), removeInterval([l, r]), and totalCoveredLength() returning the length of the union of all intervals. Intervals may repeat; aim for amortized O(log n) per operation. Provide concrete behavior with examples: after add [1,3], add [2,5] => total = 4; after remove [2,3] => total = 3? Explain approach and edge-cases?

Design a dynamic multiset to back a live leaderboard: implement insertScore(playerId, score), eraseScore(playerId, score) (duplicates allowed per user over time), and getRank(score) which returns how many scores are <= score across all players. Use a treap augmented with subtree sizes; explain how duplicates are distinguished by playerId and how getRank works. How would you implement this and why?

Context: A simple text editor buffer. Design a dynamic string buffer supporting insertAt(index, text), deleteAt(index, length), and getFragmentHash(l, r) for substring comparisons. Use an implicit treap (rope) where each node stores a string block, its size, and a rolling hash; maintain subtree hash. Describe split/merge, hash propagation, and Unicode handling. Example: start 'abcde', insertAt(2,'XYZ'), deleteAt(4,2), getFragmentHash(2,6)?

Design a dynamic forest data structure that supports makeRoot(u), link(u,v), and cut(u,v), plus path queries pathSum(u,v) and pathKthLargest(u,v,k) where edge weights may duplicate. Target amortized O(log n) per operation. Describe a concrete implementation, how path aggregates are maintained, and how kthLargest is computed along a path?

Design a data structure that maintains a dynamic multiset of integers supporting insert(x), erase(x) (one occurrence), and getMedian() in O(log n). Explain a two-heap (lower max-heap, upper min-heap) approach, how to rebalance after insert/erase, how duplicates are handled, and how to implement lazy deletion. Include a short example of operations: insert 1, 3, 2, erase 3, and report median after each operation?

Design a dynamic sequence that supports insertAt(i, value), eraseAt(i), and rangeKth(l, r, k) returning the k-th smallest value in subarray [l, r], with duplicates allowed. Aim for amortized O(log^2 n) per operation. Describe the data structure, how inserts/erases affect counts, and how rangeKth is achieved efficiently?

Design a dynamic set of lines f_i(x)=m_i x + b_i supporting insertLine(id, m, b), eraseLine(id), and queryMax(x, t) returning the maximum value among lines active at time t. Explain enablement using a time-segment-tree over operation times with Li Chao trees per node, and provide complexity and update strategy?

Context: An analytics system tracks event scores as integers. Implement a data structure that supports addEvent(score), removeEvent(score), and countAtMost(threshold). Duplicates allowed. Scores up to 1e9; at most 2e5 events. Design with coordinate compression and a Fenwick tree: pre-map scores, update counts on insert/erase, and answer countAtMost(threshold) by prefix sum up to the largest compressed score <= threshold. Example: addEvent(5), addEvent(7), removeEvent(5), countAtMost(6) -> 1?

Design a dynamic sequence data structure supporting insertAt(index, value), eraseAt(index), and rangeSum(l, r). Add a new operation moveSegment(l, r, dest) that moves the contiguous subsequence [l, r] to start at position dest (dest is the index in the new sequence). Duplicates allowed. Specify amortized time, how augmented sums are updated, and how you handle overlapping dest with [l, r]?

Design a time-windowed dynamic multiset: insertEvent(id, t, v), deleteEvent(id). Queries: sumInWindow(t, W) and kthLargestInWindow(t, W, k). Duplicates allowed. Implement with a deque for events, a running sum, and an order-statistics BST (value→count) to support kthLargest in O(log n). Expire old events as t–W+1 advances?

In a city-scale ride-hailing network, nodes are locations; edges represent routes. Over time, edges are added and removed: addEdge(u,v) at time t, removeEdge(id) at time t; queries ask if u and v are connected at time t. Design a data structure to answer all connectivity queries in O((N+M) log M) total time using a segment tree over time and a rollbackable DSU. Describe edge lifetime mapping and complexity?

Design a dynamic data structure for a mutable array A supporting insertAt(i, x), eraseAt(i), and appendValue(x). Maintain quick answers for rangeKth(l, r, k): the k-th smallest value in A[l..r] after each operation. Duplicates allowed. Target amortized O(log n) updates and O(log n) queries. Outline the data structure, how inserts/erases affect internal state, and a correctness sketch?

Design a dynamic 3D point set that supports insertPoint3D(x, y, z, w), erasePoint(id), and updateWeight(id, newW). Provide queries: sumWeightsInBox(x1, x2, y1, y2, z1, z2) and kthLargestWeightInBox(x1, x2, y1, y2, z1, z2, k) within an axis-aligned box. Duplicates allowed. Target amortized O(log^2 n) updates and queries; discuss using a 3D range tree with fractional cascading and multiplicity-safe keys to handle duplicates?

Context: Implement a stack that supports push(x), pop(), top(), getMin(), and getMax() in O(1) time. Duplicates allowed. Explain the data layout and the exact update rules for min and max stacks, and illustrate with the sequence: push(3), push(5), push(2), push(2), pop(), what are getMin() and getMax() after the pop?

Design a dynamic set of lines y = m x + b supporting addLine(m,b,id), removeLine(id), and queryMin(x) returning the minimum y across all active lines for a given x. Duplicates allowed. The structure must handle online interleaving of adds/removes up to N operations and supports queries in O(log^2 N) expected time. Explain lifetime interval assignment, per-node Li Chao maintenance, and edge cases with identical slopes?

Design a dynamic weighted interval structure that supports addInterval(l, r, w) returning id, eraseInterval(id), updateIntervalWeight(id, newW), and queryPoint(x) returning the total weight of all intervals covering x. Intervals may overlap and duplicates are allowed. Optimize for amortized O(log N) updates and O(log N) queries with coordinate compression for large domains. Explain data layout and edge cases?

Design a mutable sequence of integers with operations: insertAt(i, v), eraseAt(i), and rangeKth(l, r, k). Additionally, support versioning: rangeKth(l, r, k, t) returns the k-th smallest value in [l, r] after applying all edits up to version t. Propose a data structure and algorithm with amortized O(log^2 n) per operation, explain persistence and how updates affect past versions?

Design a dynamic string-frequency dictionary that stores strings with counts. Implement: addString(s), removeString(s) (one occurrence), and queryTopK(prefix p, k) that returns the k most frequent strings starting with p, ordered by frequency descending and then lexicographically. Up to 2e5 total insertions. Provide a practical approach and discuss time/memory trade-offs; keep it beginner-friendly?

Design a dynamic multiset that supports insert(x), erase(x), and getKthSmallest(k) in O(log n) time, including duplicates. Explain coordinate compression and a Fenwick tree of counts store the distribution, and how to compute the k-th smallest value using a prefix-sum lift. Example: insert 3, 5, 3; getKthSmallest(2) -> 3; erase(3); getKthSmallest(2) -> 5. How would you implement this?

Context: In a streaming analytics system, implement a fixed-size sliding window structure that stores the latest w integers. Provide operations: add(value), getSum(), getMin(), getAverage(). Each update evicts oldest when full; require amortized O(1) time. Outline data structures (queue, running sum, monotonic deque for min) and edge cases when window not yet full?

Design a fully dynamic sparse matrix data structure supporting: set(i, j, v) to insert or update non-zero entries, erase(i, j) when value becomes zero, and queries: sumSubmatrix(i1,i2,j1,j2) and kthLargestInSubmatrix(i1,i2,j1,j2,k) (ignoring zeros). Aim for O(log^2 N · log V) per operation, with N up to 2e5 and V distinct values. Describe data layout, sparsity handling, and how the kth query is performed efficiently?

Design a dynamic interval multiset on a line: insertInterval(l, r, w, id) and eraseInterval(id) with duplicates allowed. Provide queries: totalWeightInRange(a, b) = sum of weights of all intervals intersecting [a,b], and kthLargestOverlap(a, b, k) = the k-th largest weight among intervals overlapping [a,b]. Aim for amortized O(log n) updates and O(log^2 n) queries. Explain data structures, handling duplicates with IDs, and persistence considerations?

Design a dynamic data structure to manage a weighted set of intervals [L_i, R_i) on a 1D axis. Support insertInterval(id, L, R, w) and eraseInterval(id). For a given coordinate x, provide: (a) sumWeightsCoveringPoint(x) and (b) kthLargestWeightCoveringPoint(x, k) among all currently active intervals that cover x. Duplicates allowed. Aim for O(log M) updates and O(log M · log W) queries using a segment-tree-of-multisets approach; outline the data layout and update/query algorithms, plus edge cases and complexity?

Design a dynamic Trie-backed multiset of strings (duplicates allowed) that supports insert(s, w) and erase(s, w). Provide queries sumWeightsWithPrefix(prefix) and kthLargestWeightWithPrefix(prefix, k) for all strings starting with the given prefix. Aim for amortized O(log n) updates and O(log n) queries, where n is the number of stored strings. Explain data structures, memory trade-offs, and how you maintain per-node weight multisets?

Design a dynamic sequence of integers supporting: insertAt(i, v), eraseAt(i), countInRange(l, r, a, b) and kthInRange(l, r, k). Provide amortized O(log n * log sigma) per operation. Values drawn from large domain. Explain data structure, how inserts/erases update the structure, and how to implement range counts and kth in a subarray?

Design a stack that supports push(x), pop(), top(), and getMin() in O(1) time. Duplicates allowed. Describe the two-stack approach that maintains the current minimum on each push, how pops update both stacks, and how to handle empty state. Include a short example sequence and expected min values?

Design a fully dynamic forest data structure to support: link(u,v,w) to connect two trees with an edge of weight w; cut(eid) to remove an edge; updateWeight(eid,w) to change edge weight; queryPathSum(u,v) to sum weights on the path between u and v (0 if not connected). Achieve amortized O(log n) per operation. Explain data structure, how path aggregates are maintained, and edge-id handling?

Design a dynamic interval index that stores weighted intervals [l, r] with duplicates allowed. Support insertInterval(l, r, w) with id, eraseInterval(id, w) removing one instance, and queries: sumWeightsCoveringPoint(p) and kthLargestWeightCoveringPoint(p, k) for intervals covering p. Outline a segment-tree‑of‑multisets approach, including handling of duplicates and time complexity?

Design a 1D dynamic interval multiset on the real line that supports insertInterval(l, r, w) and eraseInterval(l, r, w) with duplicates allowed. Add time-aware queries: sumWeightsCoveringPoint(p, t) and kthLargestWeightCoveringPoint(p, t, k) for intervals containing p as of version t. Target amortized O(log^2 n) for updates and queries. Explain data organization, persistence/versioning, and how you handle overlaps and duplicates?

Design a data structure to maintain the last N values in a streaming feed, supporting push(value), sumWindow(), and maxWindow() in O(1) amortized time. The window should always contain the most recent N values; when fewer than N values exist, the current window is smaller. Provide your approach and edge-case handling, with a concrete example for N=5 and sequence 1,2,3,4,5, then pushing 6?

Design a dynamic string of parentheses supporting insertChar(index, ch), eraseAt(index), and replaceAt(index, ch) with ch in {'(',')'}. Implement query longestValidBracketSubstringInRange(l, r) returning the length of the longest contiguous well-formed bracket substring within s[l..r]. Aim for amortized O(log n) updates and O(log n) range queries. Describe the data structure, update mechanics, and range-query procedure; address edge cases?

Design a data structure to maintain a dynamic multiset of weighted intervals on the number line. Support insertInterval(l, r, w, id) and eraseInterval(id, w) with duplicates allowed. Provide queries sumWeightsInRange(a, b) and kthLargestWeightInRange(a, b, k) for intervals intersecting [a, b]. Aim for amortized O(log^2 n) updates and O(log^2 n) queries. Explain data organization, how overlaps are managed, and how id-based erasures are tracked?

Design a dynamic interval set that supports insertInterval(l, r, w, id) and eraseInterval(id) (duplicates allowed). Also support updateIntervalWeight(id, newW). Provide queries: sumWeightsAtPoint(x) and kthLargestWeightAtPoint(x, k) for a fixed point x. Target amortized O(log^2 N) updates and O(log^2 N) queries. Describe data structure: coordinate-compressed axis, a segment tree where each node stores an ordered multiset of pairs (weight, id). Explain how to perform insert over [l,r], erase by id, and how to compute kth largest across the relevant multisets via binary search on weight?

Design a dynamic multiset of integers (duplicates allowed) with operations: insert(x), erase(x) (a single instance), kthSmallest(k), and findRank(x) (count of elements strictly less than x). Target O(log n) average per operation. Describe your data structure choice, how you store counts for duplicates, how kthSmallest and findRank navigate, and edge cases when the multiset is empty or k is out of bounds?

Design a rope-like data structure for a text editor that supports insertAt(i, s), eraseAt(i, len), and substringHash(l, r) returning a 64-bit rolling hash over the substring [l, r]. Duplicates allowed. Aim for amortized O(log n) for insert/erase and O(log n) for substringHash. Describe data layout, how to implement splits/merges, update lengths/hashes, and how to minimize collisions (e.g., double hashing)?

Design a dynamic forest data structure that supports: link(u, v, w) creating a new edge with weight w between two previously disconnected nodes; cut(u, v) removing the edge between u and v; updateWeight(id, w) updating the weight of a specific edge by its unique id; and pathSum(u, v) returning the sum of edge weights along the unique path between u and v. Ensure amortized O(log n) per operation. Explain data structure, path aggregates, and edge-id handling?

Context: beginner-level data-structures. You need a dynamic multiset of integers with duplicates. Design a data structure that supports insert(x), erase(x) (erase one instance if present), and find_kth(k) which returns the k-th smallest value (1-indexed). Guarantee O(log n) expected per operation. Explain how duplicates are stored, how ranks are updated on insert/erase, and outline an implementation using a Treap or AVL with subtree sizes?

Design a data structure IntervalCoverage to manage a dynamic multiset of integer intervals [l, r] (duplicates allowed). It must support addInterval(l, r), removeInterval(l, r) for removing one instance, and queryCoverage(x) returning how many active intervals cover point x. Target amortized O(log n) per operation. Describe coordinate compression strategy, how duplicates are tracked, and edge-case handling (empty, non-existent intervals)?

Design a data structure that supports insertValue(v), eraseValue(v) (one occurrence), and getMedian() in O(log n) per operation for a multiset of integers (duplicates allowed). Explain how you maintain balance between the lower and upper halves, how you implement erase (lazy deletion), and how getMedian behaves for odd/even sizes. Provide a small run: insert 5, 1, 5, 3; erase 5; getMedian?

Design a dynamic command palette data structure that supports insert(cmd), erase(cmd) (one occurrence), and autocomplete(prefix, limit) returning up to limit commands starting with prefix in lexicographic order. Duplicates allowed. Implement with a Trie, justify endCount/subCount, and outline time complexities?

Design a dynamic array of integers that supports insertAt(index, value), eraseAt(index), and rangeSum(l, r) using sqrt decomposition. Explain how you partition into fixed-size blocks, maintain per-block sums, and rebalance after edits when a block overflows (split) or underflows (merge). Provide a concrete example with initial [3,7,2,9], then insertAt(2,5), eraseAt(3), and rangeSum(1,4)?

Design a rope-like data structure to maintain a mutable string, supporting operations insertAt(index, s), deleteAt(index, len), and getHash(l, r) for substring hashing. Ensure O(log n) updates and O(log n) substring hash queries?

Design a dynamic string data structure (rope) that supports insertAt(pos, ch), eraseAt(pos), and getHash(l, r) in O(log n) time. Use an implicit treap with subtree size and polynomial rolling hash; provide precomputed powers and collision-avoidance strategies. Explain splits/merges and how to isolate substring hashes?

Design a dynamic deque that supports pushFront(x), pushBack(x), popFront(), popBack(), and getMin() in O(1) amortized time. Describe the two-stack representation, how each operation updates local mins, how duplicates are handled, and provide a short example sequence (pushBack(3), pushBack(5), pushFront(2), getMin(), popBack(), getMin())?

Design a dynamic 1D interval store with weights on integers. Support insertInterval(l, r, w) (duplicates allowed) returning an id, eraseInterval(id), and two queries: querySumAtPoint(x) = sum of weights of all intervals covering x, and kthLargestWeightAtPoint(x, k) = the k-th largest weight among intervals covering x. Target ~O(log N) updates and O(log N · log N) queries via a segment-tree-over-coordinates with per-node weight multisets; outline data layout and deletion semantics?

Design a lock-free, concurrent skip list that supports insert(key), delete(key), search(key), and rangeQuery(low, high) returning all elements in [low, high], duplicates allowed, with amortized O(log n) updates and O(k) range extraction where k is the number of elements returned. Explain memory reclamation, hazard pointers, and how you handle contention?

Design a dynamic Trie-based data structure to store strings with duplicates. Implement insertString(s) and eraseString(s). Provide queries: countWithPrefix(prefix) and kthStringWithPrefix(prefix, k) to return the k-th string in lexicographic order among all strings starting with prefix, or null if not enough strings exist. Explain handling duplicates, and how to implement kth selection by traversing subtree counts?

Design a dynamic priority queue for a real-time task scheduler: supports insertJob(id, priority, createdAt), updatePriority(id, newPriority), removeJob(id), popNext(), and pruneOld(now, maxAge). Tie-breaking: oldest createdAt. Aim for near O(log n) per operation. Explain data structures (augmented heap + hashmap), lazy deletion, edge cases, and memory trade-offs. Scenario: high-scale service processing user requests with varying priorities?

Design a data structure to maintain a dynamic multiset of items (id, score, ts). Support insert(id, score, ts), erase(id), updateScore(id, newScore), and queryTopKInWindow(K, window) returning the K items with highest score among items with ts >= now - window; items expire automatically after TTL, even if not removed. Aim for amortized O(log n) updates and O(K log n) top-K retrieval. Explain how duplicates, expiry, and concurrency are handled?

Context: dynamic multiset with duplicates. Implement a data structure that supports insertValue(v), eraseValue(v) (one occurrence), and getRank(v) that returns the count of elements <= v. Describe an implementation using a balanced BST with per-node count and subtree size, or a Fenwick over compressed values. Explain handling duplicates, and time complexity. Example: insert 3, 1, 4; erase 3; then getRank(2)?

Design a dynamic interval data structure for on-the-fly maintenance windows. Provide operations: insertInterval(l, r, id), eraseInterval(id), and maxOverlapInRange(l, r). Duplicates allowed and erase must work even if the same [l,r] appears multiple times. The goal is to return the maximum number of overlapping intervals within [l, r]. Explain data structure, update, and query algorithms, and analyze time/space. Provide edge-case handling for single-point intervals and large coordinate ranges?

Design a dynamic 3D weighted point set that supports insertPoint(x,y,z,w), erasePoint(x,y,z,w) (duplicates allowed), movePoint(oldX,oldY,oldZ,newX,newY,newZ) to relocate one occurrence, rangeSum3D(x1,x2,y1,y2,z1,z2) for the total weight in the axis-aligned 3D box, and kthLargestIn3DBox(x1,x2,y1,y2,z1,z2,k) for the k-th largest weight inside that box. Target average O(log^3 N) per operation; discuss coordinate compression, memory trade-offs, and handling duplicates and moves?

Design a dynamic forest data structure that remains acyclic and supports: link(u,v,w) to connect two trees with a new edge of weight w; cut(id) to remove an edge by its id; updateWeight(id, newW) to change an edge's weight.
